title: BOOKING DATE ERROR WITHOUT ANY RESOLUTION
text: I booked a tour using the trip advisor app on my cell phone. I intended to schedule the tour for Tuesday, May 20th, in CORFU, Greece,  to align with my travel plans. However, due to what appears to be an error, possibly stemming from the app’s known occasional glitches, the booking was made for Tuesday, May 13th, which was exactly one week before I would be in Corfu, Greece.I was in Santorini, Greece on May 13th and was surprised when the tour operator contacted me that day to confirm my attendance for the tour in CORFU GREECE.This tour was not inexpensive ($159.16 USD).  I have consistently relied on TripAdvisor/Viator for travel experiences around the world. Upon realizing the date discrepancy, I immediately contacted your support team on May 13th to clarify the situation. I was advised to reach out to the tour operator directly. Unfortunately, they were unable to assist or offer a rescheduled tour for the correct date, leaving me without a tour and no clear path to a resolution.While I understand policies and limitations exist, I am disappointed by the lack of support in this case. Given my history as a repeat customer, I had expected that TripAdvisor/Viator would take greater initiative to assist in rebooking or offer a suitable alternative—particularly when it was clear I had not used the service on the incorrect date and made every effort to resolve the issue promptly.I respectfully request reconsideration of my case, whether in the form of a refund, credit, or rescheduling a comparable tour. It would go a long way in maintaining my trust in your platform and ensuring future bookings.People make mistakes, we are humans, not machines. I would think a company like Viator would make more of an effort to satisfy their customers. But after a number of emails and messages back and forth, they offered me a 5% discount which is unacceptable.

name: Ricardo Feliu
title: Hidden costs
text: On May 6, 2025, I purchased two airline tickets through the JustFly application. One day later, I requested to purchase seats from the same company. After selecting them, they charged my card $189.68. My surprise was enormous when days later they tried to charge me another $189.68, plus $466, plus $22. As a consequence, the card was blocked, fortunately denying these payments due to "fraudulent activity." Because of this, I had to change my card and call each of the companies that make recurring payments.They tried to charge me over 15 times.But my surprise was even greater when upon contacting them, they told me that the $189 was only to "secure" the seats, that the actual cost was the $466 they tried to charge me days later. I never knew what the $22 was for.This is openly deceptive and fraudulent to consumers. These hidden costs are a crude scheme to rob unsuspecting consumers, and someone should do something about it. One only needs to look at the ratings that the public gives this company to realize that this is something regular and recurring that they do to passengers.## JustFly's Deceptive PracticesBased on my experience and other customer reports, JustFly appears to engage in misleading pricing tactics. The company has been criticized for their predatory fees and poor customer service. In one documented case, a customer reported that JustFly didn't provide a final cost quote until after the transaction was completed, and when they tried to cancel, they faced significant cancellation fees even within minutes of booking.JustFly's website advertises "cheap flights" and claims to offer savings on flight and hotel bundles, but these promotions may mask additional charges that appear later in the booking process or after completion.**Customer Service Issues**When customers attempt to resolve issues, they often encounter difficulties reaching effective customer service. One customer reported having to navigate through multiple phone menu layers before reaching a live person, only to be stonewalled when asking to speak with a supervisor.Your experience with hidden seat charges aligns with the pattern of behavior reported by other customers. The practice of charging an initial fee to "secure" seats and then attempting to charge significantly more later appears to be part of a concerning business model that relies on unclear pricing and unexpected fees.

It took several hours of going around in a loop with their “chat” service which could not progress as I did not have a valid booking number (because my villa had been cancelled!). Eventually a human rang me and offered an alternative. This was a one bedroom property!!! How can anyone seriously suggest this was an alternative to a three bed (for four adults). Then I waited for someone from escalation who told me he was the most senior person I could ever hope to speak to. Shame with such authority and power he could only authorise £100 “compensation” which I could only use in VRBO. A similar villa now costs £900 extra. He very patronisingly explained this was due to the short notice. I will laugh one day but not today. Hosts apparently get suspended from renting property once they have cancelled a client like this but perhaps they’d be less likely to cancel if they had a fine to pay (which could go towards helping customers rebook!!).The same thing happened in 2021 too. 13 days before travel and the villa became uninhabitable. name: Hope Jackson
title: Do not use this website.. You don't get what you see and will not get your money back!
text: Do not use this website... The pictures they allow on their site looks nothing like the property once you get there. Then when you try to get your money back because of false advertisement there is no help through this site.. Here is a review from a Villa in Bali called Villa Belize that we had the worst experience with and Vrbo is doing nothing!Photos are fixed to make you believe you are staying in such a luxury environment. My party reserved this place for a trip during one of the most humid times of the year in Bali. Every day we had to call the host because the air conditioning units were not working. You basically felt like you were sleeping outside.. Speaking of sleeping outside, photos doesn't show that pretty much all bathrooms except 1 is open concept so there is exposure to the outside.. The only bathroom that doesn't have exposure to the outside has the toilet, shower and sink right next to each other in this very small area.. This is the bathroom they show, but what's not shown is once you take a shower the whole bathroom gets very wet and takes a full day to dry, so you can't have your stuff out in the bathroom... The window in their also doesnt close completly which is a way for pest to get in.. Moving on to the rooms, the gaps between the doors are large enough for any pest to get in so every night we had to fight off some type of pest... Mainly little lizards, mosquitos, hugh  roaches.. I know Bali is the climax for these types of pest and I dont mind them on the outside, however there was easy access to the inside. This was supposed to be a enjoyable trip for a wedding we was attending and my birthday.. I ended up having to move out on the second day in the middle of the night due to pest in my room. We brought this attention to the house manager, who was nice to respond promptly and was willing to work with us stating we would get our money back. The stipulations was that the other two people in my party would find other lodging as well. We all ended up having to readjust and pay for lodging elsewhere spending additional money. However, we still are struggling to get our money back from the owner after several attempts and sending everything requested to VRBO who also is not very helpful in standing by their customers and investigating more.. Im in Bali often and have lodge at various places, which have been awesome. I must say this has been the worst experience I've ever had in Bali and hope no one else have to experience what we have.. Pictures im attaching will be all the gaps in doors and open spaces in room and bathroom.. Please don't go by the pictures posted by the owner as you will be very disappointed once you arrive and see you have been mislead! Pictures shown by the owner are very misleading and villa is not worth the money paid!

name: stuart
title: Vrbo could do better but clearly not that bothered
text: Booked a villa for extended family of 10 through Vrbo which was changed 3 days before departure. Substitute villa was unfinished (kitchen incomplete, work still being done on pool). We had to battle to get 3rd villa (which was lovely) but lost 1 day of holiday sorting out. Compensation offered amounted to $10/ person. Vrbo's attitude typically that of large/ faceless organisation i.e. hollow words ("we're so sorry"/ "We truly regret the inconvenience") coupled with paltry compensation. Problems arose through no fault of ours and Vrbo didn't do anywhere near enough when problem arose, when we were trying to sort it and then afterwards. Reading other reviews, this is consistent theme. BE WARNED ALL WHO ENTER WORLD OF VRBO....

name: Jennifer Kloihofer
title: Beware! Lying thieves run Vrbo
text: A word of caution to anyone planning a trip, don’t use Vrbo.I booked a place and cancelled it within the house cuz I found a better place on Airbnb and my full 100% Vrbo refund was missing $534.15!When I called them they tried to blame it on foreign currency exchange…. I cancelledthe booking within the hour! What kind of foreign currency exchange scam are you running Vrbo?And if that’s the case why do you say you give a 100% refund?Not 100% refund minus foreign currency exchange rates.Oh also, I was given no reference number for my incident or contact information for the department handling these types of issues for vrbo so I have no idea if or when someone will be contacting me about returning my stolen $534.15.I will NEVER use Vrbo again and strongly encourage anyone who does to always double check to make sure they received all of the refund they should have gotten if they have cancelled a reservation in the past!

name: Hillel Posner
title: Simple story, VRBO failed us
text: Simple story. We went to Mexico to see my dad one last time (he is very ill). 3 days before the trip our host had not responded to our request for location. We called VRBO, they said we had to wait until check in before they would do anything. The night before check on, at 1 am, VRBO cancelled the reservation. They said we could book on hotel, VRBO or Expedia, there were no places within the price margin they gave us on these platforms. We were stuck with no reasonable options. Just had to spend a ton of money. VRBO did nothing. So much for their guarantee. Didn't even offer to help find another place. We lost a lot of money and had a lot of stress. Would never use again.

name: Carrie Doyle
title: I’d honestly give zero stars if…
text: I’d honestly give zero stars if possible. We’ve had the most awful experience ever with VRBO!! We’ve been super hosts for over 5 years, had over a hundred positive reviews, and they just cancelled all of our listings without warning for no valid reason. We’ve spent over 20 hours solid on the phone getting hung up on, dropped calls, transferred, and every time being told they couldn’t help us. There’s one person in there entire company who can make decisions on our account and not once has he ever emailed us back or called  after 10 emails on our end and 8 phone calls. They say his department doesn’t have phones 🤔 and that he has no supervisor to talk to. I’ve asked if he’s a real person and not a bot and their only answer is that “he’s part of our team”!! It turns out there reasoning for cancelling our listings is because the mother of one of our already booked renters messaged us asking for room/bed layout and we used the words “contact” and “email” after she asked if her daughter could contact us with any more questions in regards to their upcoming travels. Her daughter originally booked me as her wedding photographer (that is my full time profession) and I recommended they also book our rental for her family. Naturally she already has my number and my email to communicate about her wedding. It appears that VRBO has ai generated tag words that if you use them in messaging you will get your listings disabled. I went to the extent of providing them the following documents to prove our case and they will not reinstate our listings at all and will not let us talk with anyone who can actually help us. I provided them…1. An original email inquiry for wedding photography from nearly a year ago.2. A copy of my photography contract with her.3. A copy of my photo business questionnaire where it lists the woman who messaged us on vrbo as her mother4. A copy of their booking of the property nearly a year prior to her mom messaging us about room/bed layout5. A copy of their receipt of down payment for lodging and photo booking from nearly a year prior to her message.6. And letters from both my bride and her mother stating they had no idea that having the mother of the bride message us on vrbo would be an issue and get us flagged for removal.Vrbo refuses to look at any of it, refuses to let us talk to Leon who apparently is the only person on earth who can make a decision on our account, and refuses to even acknowledge that they are not providing us any customer service help even though we’ve supported their business financially and been super hosts for over 5 years.They are truly the worst worst platform for hosts. Zero support, zero customer service, and zero professionalism. We’ve had nothing but a very positive experience on Airbnb and booking.com. Every time we have a question they are so helpful. Save yourself the time and headache and steer clear of vrbo. In our research they have numerous current lawsuits, fail to payout hosts, we’re recently under investigation with BBB, and are in financial trouble from poor management.Updated as a response to VRBO....As of 4/21/25 there has been no email response from the team responsible for our account with Leon being the team leader for our account. His original email to us was 02/27/25 of which we responded that same day with questions. He has not responded once to us in nearly 2 months. Customer support tells us to communicate with him about our case and he refuses to respond even once and refuses to provide us customer service.

name: Jeanne Ackles
title: Cannot get them to return our damage deposit. No means of communication except ai.
text: We have been back home from our holiday for 6 weeks and cannot get anyone to return our damage deposit. I have been trying to find a link for this company for communication in order to get our deposit back and are completely at a loss. We left our rental spotless and fully sanitized. So very angry!!

name: Manuel Rabelo
title: By far the worst app for hosts
text: By far the worst app for hosts! Their market maker is awful, they change pricing without telling you, and their fees are outrageous. Their customer service is the worst (if you can understand them), and customer support is extremely rude. If you cancel a reservation because their system failed, they charge you 10% and suspend your account. Stick with AirBnB for your hosting experience, they are by far better.

name: Karen Cracknell
title: The main problem with Vrbo is they do not communicaTE WITH EACH OTHER OR THE CUSTOMER PROPERLY EVERYTHING IS A STANDARD FORMAT.
text: The main problem I had with Vrbo was when you tried to get a refund not from the property that you may have cancelled but from Vrbo themselves for the service fee etc. It took me at least 6 weeks after numerous phone calls and emails which were always replied with ( we understand your frustration but are awaiting reply from owners of property. It was not the the owners I had a problem with it was vrbos side of things but they just kept blaming the owners and saying they had tried to contact the owners but they would not reply and when I spoke to said owners they had no knowledge of vrbo trying to contact them.At the end of the day it was not the part of the contract with the owners but a contract with vrbo.It was not untill I got my solicitor involved that things started to move very quickly and a satisfactory outcome was achieved.So Vrbo sort your refund procedure out because we can all do without the hassle when all we want is what vrbo originally promise when you have to cancell a villa.

name: Melissa Flowers
title: THE WORST APP AS A HOST
text: THE WORST APP AS A HOSTThe app is not user friendlyDoes not allow for a co hostThe customer service is HORRIBLEWe appreciate that many people do use it and want the business but at the expense of EXTREME STRESSthey do not have the option of ID verificationThere seems to be no care or concern for hosts or their propertyWE WILL DROP OUR PROPERTY

name: Chalet Kanimbla
title: Hosts, don’t waste your time with Stayz/VRBO!
text: Hosts, don’t waste your time with Stayz/VRBO!I used to be a loyal Stayz traveller, so naturally, I wanted to list my property with them when I became a host. My listing has now been live for over a year. In that time, I’ve received consistent weekly bookings on Airbnb, with over 50 reviews and an average rating of 4.96. On VRBO? Just two bookings in total.I pay a premium for a channel manager to keep my listings synchronized across platforms, so before cancelling, I reached out to VRBO support to check if there was an issue with my listing.Unfortunately, the support experience was incredibly frustrating. The agent I spoke with, Ella Mae B, wasted 30 minutes of my time and repeatedly directed me to check MarketMaker to assess demand. I explained clearly that there’s no demand issue—I’m getting plenty of bookings through Airbnb. My suspicion is that VRBO’s algorithm doesn’t rank your listing well until you’ve had at least three booking reviews, similar to what I experienced with Airbnb (which only took a few weeks to overcome).That said, it seems like a classic chicken-and-egg problem—or worse, that Stayz simply doesn’t work anymore, and support won’t acknowledge it.Ella Mae was unwilling to escalate the issue or provide any real help. After trying my best to make the platform work, I’ve decided to cancel my listing and will be recommending that other local hosts don’t waste their time either.

name: Stephen Willis
title: 24 hour emergency line is nothing of the sort. Weekend ruined.
text: Arrived to find only 2 of the 5 bedrooms were unlocked, and we had booked for 10 people. 24 hour emergency phone was nothing of the sort. Message service only, and no reply forcing most of our family to stay in a nearby hotel. Not sure what they would do with a significant emergency, and family celebration weekend ruined.

name: Martin Mosebury Smith
title: A very strange booking platform
text: A very strange booking platform. Minimal information available despite an AI assistant. Enquiry to the host not functional. Having made a booking and confirmed by bank card received a message "Your request was declined". Are we booking accommodation for an offered service or not?

name: Vicente Garcés
title: HOST DONT USE VRBO
text: HOST DONT USE VRBO. They owe me $2,000. One of the guest that came to one of my properties did a charge back and the first time it was solved on my favor. The second time on guest favor. OF COURSE vrbo didnt do nothing about it and their emails are “ we cant do nothing about it”. Well you MUST do something about it as you are the platform that brings guest. Pls be careful this is a SCAM that is going on and the platform behind (vrbo) wont do nothing to solve it. Other platforms like AIRBNB will pay you as a HOST and get the loose as they are huge and we are the ones investing in those properties. I just remove 7 of my listings as I cant go through this type of looses and dont have a platform behind that will cover me. USELESS!!!!!

name: Kotikjeff
title: This company is not easy to deal with
text: This company is not easy to deal with. A phantom.  They do not communicate. CannotTrack and take payments properly. They are totally disorganised. Seem to be a third party with Hoseasons. Keep to Hoseasons.What an ordeal. Steer clear.

name: VICKY H
title: Deliberately misleading property description
text: I recently booked a chalet in Tignes Les Breviaries called 'Crystal Ridge' through VRBO. The chalet was described to us as 'ski-in/ski-out' and in the event there isn't much snow, it is only 100m from the Boisses gondola (this was also verified by the host through VRBO before I booked). Both of these statements are categorically untrue. The chalet is no where near a piste and it was 500-700m from the Gondola which is an issue when you have young kids and a partially sighted guest. In addition to this, the water pump/pipes in the boiler room on the ground floor where the washing machine is situated were leaking. There was water all over the floor which had been soaked up with towels and blankets. They all had a stench of stale water. At one point the water leaked out into the main ground floor area and we had to mop it up with our own allocated towels. These were not replaced despite asking 3 times. The kitchen was full of broken crockery which we asked to be removed - this request was ignored and on checkout, i insisted the managing agent had a look and their solution was to put the pile of broken items back on top of the fridge and leave them to the end of season!! The carpets throughout were dirty and stained, the bathtubs had mould around the silicon and the car park and ski/boot room are actually about 100m away from the chalet!I have liaised extensively with the host 'Poplidays' and VRBO, neither of whom are prepared to make a proper partial refund for the deliberately misleading description. AND on top of this, Poplidays attempted to get me to sign a legal agreement containing a non-disclosure clause to prevent me leaving a review!! Funnily enough, VRBO won't allow my review to be posted either!DO NOT USE VRBO or POPLIDAYS (France)Update: Your 'dedicated team' have completely failed to help, i've already been liaising with them on a daily basis basis. The VRBO 'book with confidence' guarantee which protects for material misrepresentation of the property description is completely meaningless as a chalet described as 'Ski-in/Ski-out' when it is nowhere near a piste and is impossible to access by ski is indeed a material misrepresentation. I'm now pursuing the matter with the bank and the trading ombudsman.

name: Wilson Miller
title: Host cancelled the hose we were staying…
text: Host canceled the house we were staying in 17 days before graduation for my daughter from college.  Reservation has been made for a year on which they sat on the money.  VRBO will do nothing!  Makes me not want to use them.  Can you imagine flying to an island, Europe, etc and the house is not available.  You purchase plane tickets etc and the same.  No, Thank you.  Airbnb is just as bad!

name: Ann Catterlin
title: We’re in 662 Cottage Dr at Napa’s…
text: We’re in 662 Cottage Dr at Napa’s Silverado Resort.There’s NO Heat. The coffee pot they claim to have, doesn’t work.There’s only 2 salad forks…We called customer service 2x, left messages, NO ONE returned the call.I will never forget and never rent again.I plan on finding out the owner of this unit. Pretty disappointed…

name: Enrica Bridgwater
title: The worst possible platform to advertise your property
text: The worst possible platform. The customer service is literally useless. They never answer any questions. They don’t know anything and they keep passing the call to somebody else. I usually spend hours purely because they pass my call onto other departments but at the end no one can deal with my query. They are NOT a transparent company and you cannot talk to anyone at the accounts department. Does it actually exist?  If I could I would give 0 stars to this company. Do not advertise with them.

name: Babi
title: Scam host using Vrbo
text: My complaint is not against this platform but against a host who has an ad for a studio for rent in Swansea. I tried to make the reservation through the platform in early January, but it was having difficulties in accepting payment with my card details and With the payment deadline approaching, I asked what payment alternative the lady had available to me so that I could guarantee the reservation. She sent me bank details to do a bank transfer. I did but after a few days without a response I asked the lady again to which she replied that the reservation had been cancelled and that my messages were suspicious!! I went to my bank to ask for the refund, and till now I have nothing. I contacted the platform asking for help, and they promptly provided me with her phone number and email address. As I do not live in the UK, I contacted them via WhatsApp and have not been able to do so yet. The lady's name is Sandra Lopez and I hope that at least what happened to me will not happen to anyone else in the future. I also hope to could have my money back somehow, because I haven't given up on finding that person and getting in touch with her.

name: Emily Smith
title: Overdue payment demands despite never booking
text: Made the mistake of asking a host a question about their property. I am being bombard with emails saying "payment overdue" despite never tying to even make a reservation. Emails are pressuring in tone and sound as if I have failed to make an agreed payment.  Even after explaining I hadnt made a reservation and didn't want to book. Seems to be no way of stopping this. Wouldn't book as do not like this pressurising tactic.

name: James H
title: Cancelled and Abandoned.
text: I recently booked accommodation through VRBO, only to later find the same property listed on Airbnb for the same dates — but at four times the price. When I contacted VRBO about this, they told me the host was considering removing the listing and suggested that I cancel the booking myself.When I asked VRBO for help, their support was completely unhelpful and offered no real solutions or protection, leaving me to deal with skyrocketing prices elsewhere.This experience has left me questioning why anyone would book through a platform that offers renters no security or support when things go wrong.

name: S. Bailey
title: VRBO not paying hosts? Hacked?
text: I have been an owner whose property is hosted by VRBO for 7 years now, and until this year they were very good.BUT this year we have had guests who have received spam messages from them in January with concerns re’ guests payment security, and now we haven’t received the payments from VRBO long after guests have been and gone.Vrbo help line chat assistants just bump up the issue to a specialist team or an accounts team (depending on the chat assistant) and you never hear anything again and don’t receive your host payments.Was VRBO hacked in January 2025?Are payments made by guests safe?Next guest arrives in 30 days and if we aren’t paid out then more bad press will follow asI’m starting to think it’s best to leave VRBO to ensure the longer term security of our business.

name: Blake Choplin
title: HORRIBLE experience
text: HORRIBLE experience.  I booked a reservation on March 10 for a trip on April 4.  When I called the location on March 30, I was told the reservation was cancelled.  Vrbo had not given me notice or provided a refund.  As of April 11, I still have not received a refund.  I sent an email to their customer service.  They replied and asked for details and told me to reply to that email, but the email address was "donotreply" so of course my response was bounced back to me.  I had to call customer service and demand a refund.  I also called my credit card company to dispute the charge because I don't trust Vrbo to actually refund the money.  We will see if I can actually get my money back.  I will NEVER use this service again.  STAY AWAY!

name: Jed Graham
title: I am a host and owner
text: I am a host and owner. I wanted to add VRBO because they claim their guests stay longer, and I wanted to increase my booking frequency. In the last 6 months, I have not had one booking. Then, per their crazy gimics to increase frequency, they offer discounted rates. For my short-term rental during the high-traffic season in Florida, the going rate is $6000 to $7000 per month. VRBO makes a deal for $2400 per month. (for 6 weeks at $3600). I will lose 1600 plus 800 which is $2400. A 50% loss. Then they add $1400 booking fees to my portion. I called them and complained that this was not a fair contract. Of course, you get the usual corporation story. I sent them notice of failure to perform as expected and a breach of contract due to there not being a meeting of the minds. Their legal department referred me back to Vrbo for help. What a joke. As a result, we see so many owner-hosts cancel their reservations. Now, VRBO claims I will owe them 10% for cancelation. Good collecting that money.

name: Enrique Schmid
title: Very Disappointing Experience – Reservation Canceled Again
text: This is the second time I’ve had a reservation with VRBO canceled after booking. In both cases, the explanation was that there was "no availability" — yet the listing still shows as available for the exact same dates I had selected. This is misleading and unacceptable.The process has been extremely inconvenient and time-consuming. I spent valuable time planning my trip and coordinating logistics, only to have everything fall through without a valid reason. VRBO needs to do a better job vetting listings and ensuring availability is accurate. I’m very disappointed and now seriously reconsidering whether to use this platform again.

name: Rebecca Davis
title: Terrible
text: Terrible. Booked 2 places both of which were cancelled because they no longer use vrbo as a booking agent. Checked with a 3rd to be told that they too no longer use them. All 3 were marked as available. We are now holiday-less and still waiting for around £1000 in refunds. Disgraceful company. Customer service friendly but they can't change the processes that lead to these kinds of issues.

name: Jenni
title: No, No, No - Do Not Use VRBO
text: I will keep this short - do not use this company!They change prices/payment due with no clear explanation, take more money from your account than you have authorised and finally make Customer Service so painful that you eventually give up.I will never use this company again.Note: VRBO responses to negative reviews are all a mix of the same generic words - suspect artificial intelligence generated.

name: M. Schoenmaeckers
title: Landlord cancels for a higher bidder
text: For the second time this year, the owner of a property we booked via VRBO this year canceled on us, because they got offered a higher price for their property. VRBO do absolutely nothing, despite their promise the first time this happened. Holiday home brokerage platforms should be avoided at any time- there’s a fundamental flaw in that they take a hefty fee but no responsibility, leaving tenants in the cold. If you want to rent a property, either have a rental contract agreed directly with the owner on the right terms, or through a platform where the platform is a party to the contract. VRBO should start taking responsibility and forbid landlords to apply unethical practices through their platform. Barring such measures, VRBO should be closed down and not be allowed to lure innocent tourists into contracts that are meaningless and where they enjoy ZERO protection!

name: Kia
title: AVOID AT ALL COST
text: AVOID! Absolutely awful customer service. The host was not reachable on the day of my arrival to Turkey in Oct. We were left stranded and had to book alternative accommodation. The host then cancelled the booking the following day and I have been trying to get a refund for 5 months. I have also been asking for the transcript of my chat with the VRBO customer service which proves that they also could not reach the host on the day of my arrival.Mariam has been very unhelpful and ignoring my requests to escalate the matter to her senior management.

name: Lisa
title: Scammed on my holidays last month
text: On my holidays last month, I booked 2 flats in 2 different cities in Morocco with VRBO. Both of them were cancelled last minute in the evening, when we were waiting for the check-in details.The reason for cancelling? Not complying with "Minimal age"!!!I am 53 years old. Is there minimal age 100 years old?2 "ghost houses" or scams in 2 bookings means that we had 100% bad experience  with VRBO and we do not want to use it again, we only want our money back and will delete the app soon after this is solved.They are offering us credits to use in next bookings even though we told them that after 2 scams we are not interested in being scammed again. Twice is more then enough.WE DO NOT RECOMMEND VRBO cause we had 2 (two) "ghost houses" in 2 bookings, within 7 days.On our poor experience, we can say that they are very bad 👎 and they're customer service in not helpful.I would stay away from using VRBO app.

name: Shaun
title: Horrible company
text: Horrible company! Call center is in India and they are no help. Stayed at a property that was falsely advertised and I called VRBO for a refund. They refused and said to talk to the Host. The Host stop responding to me. DO NOT USE VRBO FOR ANY BOOKINGS!

name: Sarah
title: If I could give zero stars
text: If I could give zero stars, I would. ★☆☆☆☆  10 months of absolute incompetenceMy property has been showing in the WRONG LOCATION on VRBO for 10 months. I’ve contacted them repeatedly — emails, calls, support tickets — all ignored or closed without resolution.Guests are confused, I’m losing bookings, and VRBO’s response? Non-existent.They’re quick to take thousands in commission, but when it comes to basic support or fixing THEIR error? Silence.Shocking customer service. Shocking platform. Avoid listing with VRBO unless you enjoy talking to a brick wall while watching your income disappear.

name: Rupesh Patel
title: Hire a flat in Camden, pay for it and be homeless
text: Absolute farce of a company/organisation.  For my wife's birthday, we decided to visit London for the weekend.  Obviously, we made plans for certain places we wanted to visit so we chose a suitable apartment in a lively part of London, Camden.  Found a lovely apartment at a reasonable price, even invited friends to visit us the evening we get there.  When we got there, the post code provided was wrong and so, my family and I had to walk two miles to get to the given address as the Uber had dropped us off according to the postcode.We were sent a video to obtain our key, which was a bit of an adventure by itself.  So we walked to the property only to find the address provided looked nothing like the place in the video.  So no key to get in either.  Puzzled, I started looking at the paperwork.Even though I clearly booked the apartment in Camden, I eventually found out by investigating the numerous emails that the landlord of this property owns more than one place and we were booked into the place shown in the video - ten miles away.On a cold, rainy Winter's night, my family and I are stranded standing in a lobby of a building where we had nothing booked.  Last minute I found (expensive and probably) the only room available for my wife and I.  My friends, luckily accomodated my two teenage children.Next day I finally receive a message from the landlord that the apartment is ready for us on Saturday at 5pm and that I have to collect the key at 2pm.  We had plans and so I refused to check in and demanded a full refund and some compensation towards the extra expense and inconvenience we had to endure.On numerous occasions, I have contacted the landlord (who insists that I contact Vrbo) and Vrbo as well.  NOTHING!  No reply, no refund, no compensation.  This is an absolute joke of an organisation - AVOID LIKE THE PLAGUE.

name: Mike
title: VRBO  IS A VERY VERY VERY VERY BAD …JUST ASK PAPA AND THE GRANDKIDS
text: VRBO  IS A VERY VERY VERY VERY BAD  COMPANY  THEY HAVE NO PROBLEM PULLING THE RUG OUT FROM UNDER YOU.......Me and my grand kids spent week looking at aruba homes to rent , they had a ton of fun,, pappa we like that one papa we want that one, they finally settle in on the one with the flamingo in the pool ! we booked the vacation home thru vrbo 4 months ago, 12 people total going kids grandkids family... we are all going down to watch papa run the aruba marathon .....6 weeks to are vacation they send email , heres the emailHi Mike, I hope you're doing well. Unfortunately, the house Moko 119 is no longer part of our program. We explored alternative options for you, but we regret to inform you that there is no availability for your reservation dates. We will proceed with the cancellation. We sincerely apologize for any inconvenience this may cause. Please let us know if there’s anything we can do to assist you further. thats was it no help as they claim they will do. first they said i didnt send the documents , then they said the property  is not part of are program,, my first time booking this stuff,, just shameful.  never new this could happen legal ? moral?  bad buisness. now i need to find a place for 12 people including 5 kids, in a short time

name: vr-no
title: Should have looked at TrustPilot
text: I was stupid for not looking at Trustpilot before booking through vrbo.Booked an apartment, was nearly immediately contacted by the host trying to get me to cancel and book direct.  I didn't respond, the next day the host tries calling me.This really frustrated me, we just wanted to book, arrive and enjoy... instead we get hassled about cancelling/booking direct to presumably save them some money.Called vrbo, asked to cancel/refund the booking based on their host breaking guidelines... You would think vrbo would have been appreciative when we brought this to their attention.  No.  3 hours on the phone over 3 days with various different people, none of whom are authorised to do anything.  Nobody calls or emails back as they say they will.Upshot, we lost 50% of the money and til the end vrbo were trying to stop us cancelling (before the 50% deadline) to wait for some mystical 'violations' department to respond.  Can't help but feel they were just trying to get 100% of the money instead of the 50%.The guy on the last correspondence even told me not to worry because of the 'book with confidence guarantee'.  This absolutely does not exist.Absolute joke, please use a different portal.

name: Kerre Woodham
title: Despair is spelt Vrbo
text: I have been trying for nearly a month to get paid for hosting a stay at my holiday home.  Six separate agents have given me six different reasons for why I have yet to be paid.  I spent 45 minutes on hold with one agent before hanging up.  When it was escalated, the agent rang me at midnight my time.  I didn't pick up.  I was asleep.  She then emailed me and asked me to email her back.  I did and received an email back saying the email address is no longer monitored.  I rang an 8th agent - after hanging up on the 7th - and he told me my situation hadn't been escalated.  I've now been assured by a 9th agent the escalation agent will call me back before midnight.  I have lost faith and hope I will ever be paid.  I have lost faith and hope in Vrbo.  I have lost faith and hope in humanity.

name: Rosie
title: Stayed at 421 Hamden
text: Stayed at 421 Hamden, pictures on website totally deceiving , showed large refrigerator, full kitchen, had no stove and small refrigerator, said had hot tub and hair dryer, neither , lousy cable and internet service , showed two beds, only 1, small pool, used hot plate for cooking , asked to be moved to better condo with said amenities , didn’t happen

name: Jazzy
title: So in the end I'm very dissapointed got ranted at by an owner, have no vacation rental and lost $44,14
text: I booked an luxary home on Bonaire. Paid and got a confirmation.Then I get a message from the owner that the object is sold and not for rent and he tells me I have to cancel. I check back and there's nothing about this in the text, I choose dates that were available and have a confirmation and receipt. He rants at me. I app the helpdesk (nice woman). She says I have to cancel, but I refused. I have a contract and I didn't breach. If they can't deliver they should. So she says she will and the owner will be penalized.I get a confirmation that I will get my money back in 5 days. They didn't offer compensation or alternative rentals.I got my money back minus $12,14 a day later (maybe because of the exchange rates $-€ ? Although both my card and their company are US based) and have to pay VISA the international fee, twice!So in the end I'm very dissapointed got 'yelled' at by a rental owner owner, have no vacation rental and lost $44,14Nice detail. The owner sent me his mail to vrbo by mistake and it showed he did have the capacity to be nice, even to suck up to people.**update**After this review they contacted me and send me the money back. Got it in 3 days. Due to banking costs and exchanges, still a few cents short, but they tried. Too bad their site doesn't offer the option to review rentals nor owners when they cancel due to their neglect to update dates. I hope at least the app got the money from the owner.I changed my review to 2 stars. Bcause although I still have to find a replacement myself and it cost me a lot of time, effort and frustration, I've got my money back.

name: Dhruv Patel
title: BED BUGS! Amazing stay turned horrible with extremely disappointing corporate support!
text: It started with a seemingly normal stay in Mammoth Lakes, CA (Meadow Ridge 37 (VRBO Property # 2451906)): easy check-in, property well-maintained, no issues! Everything you’d expect from a corporate conglomerate of VRBO and Vacasa Property Management. We arrived on Wednesday and stayed till Sunday for a ski weekend.On Friday morning, some folks in our group started noticing hives and rashes on their bodies. We just figured it was environmental - maybe brushing up against some pine, maybe pollen, or something they ate. Everyone was itchy and took plenty of OTC meds, but limited help.On Sunday morning, we proceeded to start the check-out process and discovered bed bugs under one of the mattresses!! We squished a few of them and noticed blood coming out of them - which was our rudimentary validation of what caused the hives….they were indeed bed bug bites.We called VRBO and Vacasa and were told that we can evacuate the property and the local team would come check on the situation and give us a call to discuss next steps.It’s been over a week at this point. Limited to no communication from Vacasa, VRBO threw up their hands and said it wasn’t their problem, and now we’ve been punted off to 2 different companies (Sedgwick and Rental Guardian)….with little to no actual communication or response.Honestly, we’re just looking for a little courtesy in letting us know how to navigate this situation and playing fairly given a lot of inconvenience, very likely bed bug infestation in our clothes and homes, and really bad daily medical issues. It seems as though Vacasa and VRBO are not interested in taking this situation seriously and really dropping the ball, in addition to blatantly breaking their respective terms and conditions - which articulate “clean and safe” stays and properties.I’m hoping this post will get someone’s attention that can help work through our situation. To date, the only people we’re aware of that are involved are Cole Davis (Assistant Manager for Vacasa in Mammoth Lakes) and Nicole James from Sedgwick (her manager is Cathy Guzman, Qualified Manager, CA license #2B88261 who is part of Sedgwick Claims Management Services, Inc., CA license #2549023).

name: Trei Cap
title: VRBO Bait and Switch
text: I booked a unit through VRBO that was apparently managed by Retreatia. I arrived at the Retreatia office and was surprised at the partially damaged check-in kiosks and workers slopping down ramen take-out on the couch by the check-in area. It was not what I was expecting for a $500+ nightly rental. Nonetheless I tried to keep an open mind and proceeded with the check-in process.I was greeted by a rude check in attendant who threw some papers in front of me and asked me to sign. I regularly review contracts in my profession so I very quickly scanned the document and noted that there were several terms and conditions that were substantially different from what I signed when I booked the unit through VRBO.com.I asked the check in attendent about that and she immedialy took offense. She explained that they would refund my money or I could sign. It was obvious that this check-in attendent really wanted to exert her authority by threatening to cancel my rental which would have been really problematic after traveling more than 1,500 miles with my family.These types of strongarm tactics are not acceptable. Retreatia is a bait and switch operation and you are left with little choice but to sign and accept their onerous terms and conditions even if they differ from what you accepted in your original reservation.Many of the additional terms and conditions were reasonable but one in particular was not. At check-in you are told that you will be charged $300 if you fail to clean all dishes and remove all trash/recycling from the unit as part of your "check-out" duties. I have stayed at many vacation rentals and this is not a standard policy. They have a very early check-out time of 10AM and no one needs the added stress of cleaning the condo on the day they check out. Policies like this should be disclosed before they charge your credit card $500+ per night for their units.On the check-out day I noted the cleaning service only spent about 5 minutes cleaning each vacant unit. After witnessing this I realized that 1) the units are not very clean and 2) Retreatia is essentially not cleaning these units and passing that duty off to you as the customer. That is why they threaten customers with a $300 fine for failing to clean dirty dishes and remove garbage.The unit itself was nice but there were no pool/hottub towels and  the on-site HOA manager instructs you to contact your respective rental manager to obtain towels. I hesitated to contact Retreatia for anything after the disappointing check-in experience.

name: Canarental
title: Final Update Case 137589675 - Double charge commission - Alert for Hosts
text: Update – Latest Regarding Case 137589675After leaving my last review on Trustpilot, I was contacted via email by someone named Tania, who told me that she would review the case again.The details are below, but to summarize what happened briefly: regarding the booking in question, Vrbo withheld commission fees both on a canceled payment—which I never received—and on the replacement payments I issued for the canceled one. In other words, they charged the commission twice.Today, Tania wrote to me again, and I quote:"Hola, Alessandra:Nuestro departamento superior respondió a la solicitud.Si desea tomar acciones legales pídale a su representante que contacte nuestro equipo a legal*vrbo.comAtentamente,TaniaVrbo Support Team"They are taking advantage of the fact that I would need to hire a lawyer to recover the unjustified commission charge, which amounts to €100. Truly a wonderful strategy (the email legal*vrbo.com only responds to certified and forensic email addresses).But I will do it anyway—it will be my pleasure.However, I’d like to give you an extra tip: Vrbo is also part of this platform, where I have already filed a complaint:"In case of a dispute with Vrbo, you may use a conventional mediation procedure or any other dispute resolution method established by law. Once you have submitted your written request to Vrbo and, if you do not receive a satisfactory response within 60 days, you may take your dispute to the mediator under the conditions outlined on their website. Our entity is a member of Confianza Online (a non-profit association), registered in the National Register of Associations Group 1, Section 1, national number 594400, CIF G85804011, Calle Castelló 24, Esc 1 2° izq., 28001 Madrid (Spain), phone (+34) 91 309 13 47 and fax (+34) 91 402 83 39 (www. confianzaonline .es). You may turn to Confianza Online for alternative dispute resolution (: https://www. confianzaonline. es/como-reclamar/formulario-de-reclamaciones/). If these disputes relate to electronic transactions with consumers or data protection in this area, claims will be resolved by the Confianza Online Mediation Committee, accredited for alternative consumer dispute resolution. If the claims concern digital advertising or data protection related to this field, they will be submitted to the Advertising Jury of AUTOCONTROL. Additionally, you may use the mediation services provided by e-POM, available at https://e-pom. eu/."Furthermore, I have also filed a complaint through OCU.Of course, I have already closed my calendars on VRBO (for the little revenue it generates, it won’t be a big loss), and as far as I’m concerned, I’ll see them in the appropriate legal venues.Here are the details of my unfortunate experience.On August 2, 2024, I received the following booking HA-DP28JH with the guest's payment split into two installments:€811.10 at the time of booking€1,365.00 on January 20, 2025The total amount of the booking was €1,950, from which the commissions (5%) and transaction fee (3%) would be deducted, resulting in an estimated net amount of €1,831.99. After deducting an additional 3% for transaction fees, the final estimated amount to be received was approximately €1,780.It is clear that the Vrbo commission of €118.01 (including VAT) had already been deducted from the guest’s first payment.In January, I was contacted by your customer support (email exchange available), requesting that the second payment be split into two installments, as the guest had a €1,000 limit on their credit card.Following this request, I canceled the second payment of €1,365.00 and issued two new payments:One for €1,000One for €350The traveler successfully completed both payments.However, upon receiving the payments, I noticed that in addition to the initial €118.01 (the total commission for the booking), additional commissions totaling €82.58 (€22.08 + €60.50) were charged. This resulted in a total commission of €200.59, to which an additional €70.77 in payment processing fees was added. This brings the total deductions to €271.36 on a €1,950 booking—equivalent to a 14% fee withheld by Vrbo.This is a clear breach of our contract, and you are well aware of this. The PPB (Pay-Per-Booking) model stipulates a total commission of 8% on the booking amount (5% Vrbo commission + 3% payment processing fee), plus VAT if applicable. Not 14%.

name: John Wallis
title: VRBO owes me 600 Euros
text: My case involves an offer I accepted from VRBO  which they have completely failed to honour. I rented a house from them in the north part of Gran Canaria in February. On our first evening there, we suddenly noticed that the owner had installed surveillance cameras in the kitchen and also in the living area, which was a horrible shock to us and turned out also to be totally prohibited under VRBO regulations.The following morning I had a conversation with VRBO via online chat, they requested photos of the cameras and once they’d seen those they immediately offered to cancel the booking, set up a refund of the rental payment and also give me 600 euros compensation, the compensation payment being conditional on me booking any alternative accommodation with themselves, Expedia, Booking.com or Stayz.  I did exactly what they said and booked a new place to stay through booking.com – it wasn’t really ideal for us but it was the only thing available in that area at such short notice. We packed up all our stuff that we’d just unpacked the night before and moved out the same morning.True to their word, the rental money was refunded to my credit card 3 days later, but no sign of the 600 euros.  I sent them a couple of emails on the subject and then eventually received a reply stating that they were not going to pay the 600 euros because I hadn’t followed their terms which they now said were that the new booking had to be made with themselves, Expedia, Hotels.com, or Stayz.   I replied and explained that these were not the instructions I was given and sent them a Word file with a transcript of the entire online chat conversation where they made the original offer of 600 euros and told me to use (amongst other choices) Booking.com. I then received a reply where they didn’t address my argument at all and ended it with this rather ugly warning:“However, your concern has been heard by our company's leadership, and the decision is final. We regret that we will not be able to respond to any further escalations of this issue. We understand that this outcome may have not been the one you were seeking, but we have to make sure the program is administered fairly.As we have thoroughly explained this matter to you and this decision is final. Any further replies to discuss and/or argue the reimbursement amount will be closed without reply. “It was the promise of the 600 euros compensation that made up our minds to move to a new place rather than stay put and try not to use the rooms with the cameras in them. I regarded the offer as a firm contract with VRBO and I find their current position quite shocking. I did look into suing them in the Small Claims Court but it turns out that (conveniently for them) their operation is based in Dublin, ROI which would make that option extremely complicated and impractical.

text: This is in response to the 'resolution' that VRBO is referring to on March 10, 2025.VRBO came back again and offered $500 us another 'good will' gesture. name: Jackie
title: Customer Support ? What Customer support ?
text: Through Expedia I booked a lodge in Cornwall on 3rd March and was confident to go  ahead because I was guaranteed full refund for a cancellation by 29th April . My contract was with Vrbo, not the host, but cannot communicate with them.Waiting for my refund with baited breathWILL NEVER BOOK THROUGH VRBO AGAIN , BE WARNED

name: Matthew Pliskin
title: VRBO does not have my back
text: VRBO does not have my back. I prepaid a $4,000 dollar booking in February to stay at a place in June. On March 7th the host sent a payment request outside of the App through gmail demanding an unexpected $1,900 security deposit to be paid by March 10th. VRBO called the host and they canceled the request, but now my trust is totally gone and I don't want to stay there. VRBO will somehow not cancel the reservation and collect the money back from the host. What is the point of VRBO if they allow hosts to try to scam people and then don't have their back?UPDATE: I wanted to give a rather horrifying update on how this turned out. VRBO categorically denied cancelling the reservation based on her soliciting me for $1,900. They told me they spoke to the host and everything was fine and she had canceled that deposit request.I then did more research and found that the listing  was actually a scam entirely. The real house is being sold by a realtor that I called and he informed me it is not a VRBO.  If they allowed links in the review I would link the VRBO listing and the realtor listing. Shockingly, the VRBO listing is still up as of now.I shared all of this with VRBO and they still refused to cancel for several days. I had two VRBO agents try to get me to cancel and just eat the $4,000. Eventually, I had to deal directly with the host and tell her I was going to the cops and media. She finally initiated the cancellation; she apparently didn't want to because there is a 10% fee if she initiates, so once I caught her she was hoping VRBO would cancel. VBRO eventually apologized and offered me $120 as a gesture of goodwill telling me to shut up and go away.I filed complaints with BBB and CFPB.VRBO is a truly terrible company. Never rent without reviews that was my bad.

name: T M
title: Do not book with vrbo
text: Do not book with vrbo.  We did and it had no heat or hot water in the showers.  We contacted the host and the lied about sending maintenance out. Now vrbo won’t do anything about it. The host is in violation of short term rental laws. And vrbo will do nothing about it but waste my time!! Horrible customer service! I have spoken to BeachBox rentals the company that hosts the property. I’ve spoken with VRBO on MANY occasions. They said to bad on getting a refund or support for this because we didn’t report it while there. We thought it was being handled by the host. That did not happen. We filed a claim with our credit card. As per your customer service, since they aren’t able to help. I’m done wasting my time with this company.

name: Cassy Catino
title: We got scammed and VRBO could care…
text: We got scammed and VRBO could care less. Host charged us extra cleaning fees without showing proof but still VRBO wouldn't do anything. We sent in proof that we reached out to the host our first night with concerns, on existing damage but was still charged for the concerns we reached out about on check in. We rented a one room condo, host said the floors were dirty and charged us an extra $250 on top of our already paid cleaning fee. Total scam. No wonder why people are going back to hotels and resorts.

name: Jeff Dunn
title: I booked with VRBO as I have several…
text: I booked with VRBO as I have several times before and I had good experiences.     This time we arrived at 8pm to find the apartment we booked in the NULU area of Louisville to have been clearly slept in and not cleaned, beds were unmade, towels in a pile in the bathroom and no spare sheets or towels.   Now this should be in a review with the host, but I can't because I did get the owner to cancel my reservation and refund my money so that after a long 12 hour work day we could try and find alternative arrangements at 9pm at night.   We did.  Paid much more.   The issue is that once its cancelled, it didn't happen as far as VRBO so there's no remedy for the afflicted party.   Information that people might want to know can't be shared.   So, if this is the case, ratings in general must be overstated.  VRBO basically isn't involved and as with most of these services you can maybe get a chat with a Virtual Assistant that never seems to understand your particular problem and wastes your time.   VRBO also steers you to their app and away from the Desktop; which is fine.   Except as your trying to send feedback in a window pops up blocking you from seeing what your writing and as we all know, spell check is wreaking havoc with your words.  There is now way to actually contact them that I can find.    This was a great inconvenience and costly.   So this is my only recourse.

name: Leo
title: Terrible service, website buggy
text: I tried to contact the customer service to cancel a booking request I made 60min earlier. First, a girl picked up where it was impossible to understand her.Then, the second lady told me she will take care of it. Now the host accepted and there is nothing I can do to change the booking. It's just standard in other platforms that you can still change a request once it hadn't been accepted yet.On top of that, when getting any mail about the booking, the links on the CTA don't work and lead to error pages.In general I'm outraged by this terrible experience. I'll never book again here.I wanted to give a smaller player a chance, but the experience is just not up to standard.

name: Arne
title: Never again
text: We rented a 4 bedroom "luxura" villa in Mijas .Total disaster:Ice cold ( no heating turned on and outside temperature was 4 degrees Celcius !Hair in the beds , breadcrumbs on the kitchen table, oven not functioning , aircon in one bedroom disconnected , tiles in the pool area overgrown with green algeas, the housekeeper who showed up to install us , was drunk ( Seriously ) .When we called to the host the following morning to complain, she threatende to have the police throw us out !Absolutely disgusting experience .Worst part though is that VRBO doesn´t do anything about our complaint.On the chat you get a "parrot´s answer" : I understand your frustration !They don´t want to help

name: Bob-O
title: VRBO doesn't stand behind their consumers
text: Don't book with VRBO they don't stand behind their consumers for misrepresented and unsafe properties. VRBO rates all of are issues as minor and will not refund our money?? How is this OK?  Do yourself a favor and don't use VRBO

name: Marco Kurzmann
title: Geld scheint dem Unternehmen wichtiger als die Gesundheit seiner Kunden
text: (Text in English further below)Man schreibt dem Support mehrmals täglich das man eine Unterkunft hat in welcher das Zimmer komplett verdreckt ist (Böden, Wände, Fenster, Bettlaken, Kühlschrank, Möbel) dass das Bad komplett verdreckt und Schimmlig ist (Gesundheitsgefahr!!!) und das einzige was der Support nach einem halben Tag zusammengebracht hat außer zu vertrösten und mitzuteilen das die Ressourcen begrenzt sind ist genau garnichts, das der Gastgeber der Unterkunft sein Appartement so überhaupt anbietet ist schon ein starkes Stück aber das die Buchungsplatform Vrbo trotz Gefährdung der Gesundheit nach einem bald ganzen Tag nichts weiter zusammenbekommt als in mehreren Anfragen nur zu vertrösten riecht gewaltig nach Beihilfe zum Betrug (Es gilt die Unschuldsvermutung), somit ist dem Unternehmen wohl das Geld wichtiger als die Gesundheit seiner Kunden, einfach nur unfassbar sowas! 🥶PS: Vrbo falls ihr auf die Bewertung antwortet dann erspart es mir eure Telefonnummern und E-Mail Adressen mitzuteilen um an den Support zu gelangen, eine Komplette Rückerstattung oder eine Alternativunterkunft würden mir deutlich mehr helfen, Danke.English:You write to the support several times a day that you have an accommodation in which the room is completely dirty (floors, walls, windows, sheets, fridge, furniture) that the bathroom is completely dirty and mouldy (health hazard!!!!) and the only thing the support team managed to do after half a day, apart from putting you off and telling you that resources are limited, is exactly nothing, the fact that the host of the accommodation offers his flat at all is a strong piece, but the fact that the booking platform Vrbo, despite endangering your health, can't get anything else together after almost a whole day than just putting you off in several requests smells a lot like aiding and abetting fraud (the presumption of innocence applies), so the company is probably more important to the money than the health of its customers, just unbelievable! 🥶PS: Vrbo if you reply to the review please spare me your phone numbers and email addresses to contact support, a full refund or alternative accommodation would help me a lot more, thank you.

name: Geo W
title: The host cancelled our booking without proper notice
text: The host cancelled my booking while my wife and I were waiting in the departure in Seville Spain headed for Morocco. We landed in a foreign place where we couldn’t speak the language. We were offered poor compensation which seems to not be true. There was a disturbance in the airport in Rabat. A lady and the police were screaming, not yelling while I tried to sort things out. Was too tired at this point. We took the suggested white taxi which was not the original plan. It was so dirty. Finally got to our new booking but there was no place to get dinner as everything was closed. Now we need breakfast and it’s 5:00am, morning prayers and no breakfast after no dinner last night. Do not use Vrbo.

name: Samantha Mills
title: Shockingly poor! 0 Stars!!!
text: After travelling for 3 hours with tired and grumpy children we finally arrived at our venue only to be told we were only booked in for a room with a small double bed which was not enough space for all of us. Absolutely disgraceful!

name: tranquilmoments
title: Extremely distressing experience and Vrbo don't care
text: Booked to stay in a property one night with our dogs. The next morning was accosted by a woman/owner rep with her dog, saying we should have told them we had dogs, there was a limit of two, there was an extra charge for them. None of this had been on the listing, which I said. When we got home, they contacted Vrbo wanting extra £75 or they'd put in a bad review of us. When we refused to pay, that's what they did. They also contacted us separately wanting an additional £266, which we also refused to pay. Avoid Vrbo at all costs - our experience has been extremely distressing  - stick to Air B&B

name: Mimi
title: Avoid Expedia and Vbro
text: I have booked a property wit Expedia that after booking referred me to Vbro,that was highly misrepresented. The two bedroom windows were on a ground level with no mosquito net or shatters.Property didn’t have AC either which wasn’t a problem for me as far as could open the windows, the problem was that they are low and opening them gave on access to all the crawling and flying insects, frogs and lizards available around. So I spent first night accompanied by a frog, lizard, flies and mosquitoes and lack of fresh air as the windows are Uber a staircase and a large terrace. In the middle of the night I switched on a huge and noisy fan. Trying to ignore the noise I did get some disturbed sleep.On my arrival I did share my concern with the caretaker of the place as instructed from the owner. Was told that a net has been ordered but may not arrive during my stay. After a second almost sleepless night I contacted the owner and Vbro asking for cancellation. After more than an hour chatting, providing accurate information and photos I have been told I am not allowed cancellations because I have missed the time. I escalated the case and offered the owner to resolve matters privately with evidence provided. They refused.Not a great holiday experience.After hours on the phone I have been offered some refund, about 1/3 of the price I paid.I personally will avoid Expedia and Vbro in the future at all costs.

name: Barbara Nosti
title: BEWARE Aruba Airbnb Villa Bella 619 Palm Beach Noord
text: BEWARE, we rented Villa Bella @ 619 Palm Beach Aruba for a month. January 6-February 6 2025. Well, it unfortunately was not a very pleasant experience. We had a total of 10 persons with us. On Friday January 24, we left the house around 6:50pm for our 7pm dinner @ Momba beach. We come back to our rental house, to find we were invaded. They scaled the back wall of the house prided open the bedroom window, stole money, jewelry, wallet with credit cards in it. Sunglasses, sneaker’s iPhone, underwear backpack. We also had an apartment that came with the house. They broke into that as well. We called the manager Mina to come over, along with calling the police. Police checked out the situation, wrote up a police report. We left the house that night took all that was left of our belongings & went to stay @ the Ritz Carlton for the night, before catching a flight back to our home in NJ. The manager & Owner of the property had no interest in refunding us any deposits or return of the rest of our 2weeks that we didn’t get to enjoy, because of our violation. Please do yourself a favor and stay in a hotel. We were told Airbnb’s are being targeted in Aruba.Shame on Mina the manager & the owner. Personally we believe this was an inside job.The house itself is very beautiful. But, definitely not a safe haven.Barbara NostiUSA

name: Manny Tavano
title: I recently started listing my short…
text: I recently started listing my short term rental on VRBO. I had assumed I would receive the rental payment within a day or two of rental occupancy by the guest. After all, the guest had paid in full to VRBO prior to occupying the property. It seems that for the first rental, VRBO withholds the payment to the property owner for 30+ days. I feel this is excessive, even for a first guest in VRBO. After all, it doesn't take 30 days to vet the owner and VRBO already has the money in hand from the guest. I feel this is a way for them to get interest on a lot of owners money while they "pretend" to vet the owner of the property. This policy was not clear when I joined VRBO and I feel that such a delay is unwarranted.  Beware of this.  I also feel they take way too much of the rental amount.  They do very little for that money other than pay some amount for computer power in a server farm somewhere.  The only other business cost is software updates to their website. Both of these business expenses are minimal per VRBO listing.

name: L Mags
title: 🚨 VRBO Trapped Me in a Scam…
text: 🚨 VRBO Trapped Me in a Scam Cancellation Loop 🚨I tried to cancel my booking within the allowed timeframe (we had a death in the family requiring emergency travel and could no longer afford both trips), but VRBO’s system had a technical glitch that repeatedly looped me back to their AI “travel agent” instead of processing my cancellation. When I finally fought through to a real agent, they acted as if nothing could be done—even though the failure was on their end.Instead of honoring their policy, they ignored the technical issue, refused to take responsibility, and left me stuck paying for a stay I canceled on time. Customer service was dismissive, unhelpful, and unwilling to acknowledge that their system prevented a proper cancellation.BE WARNED: If their website malfunctions, you’ll be the one paying for it—not them. They make it nearly impossible to get a real person, and when you do, they just pretend their hands are tied. Use Airbnb or book directly—VRBO will trap you with their own errors.#VRBOScam #TerribleCustomerService**Edit following reply—you’ve had the details for over a month.  I contacted customer service IMMEDIATELY.  I was strung along for days with a “Don’t worry, the tech team is working on it, and we’ll make sure you get your refund.”  I finally had to contact the rental owner and beg them to try and cancel from their end because I recognized they, too, were being screwed out of an opportunity to rebook.  I forwarded screenshots and gave the reservation number, the stay dates, the rental details, and all other details to at least six different “customer service” reps…. all for VRBO to act like their hands were tied and nothing could be done.  You then went radio silent for three weeks as I calmly and repeatedly asked for updates on the email thread where you promised you were “looking into it.”  I am out thousands of dollars and nearly forty hours of my time, all while juggling funeral arrangements, the grief of losing a loved one, and the heartbreak of missing a family vacation we spent years planning.  The indignity of having to beg a colossal corporation to honor their most basic contractual obligations is demoralizing and humiliating, not that I should ever be surprised by corporate indifference and incompetence.**Testing the waters to see if I “could” take screenshots and then observably slow-rolling me when it appeared I could not is a duplicitous strategy.  I think it would read as such in a court of law when the customer service rep suddenly admitted they could indeed manually cancel a reservation from their end once I was able to forward the screenshots (during the first conversation, I was focused on canceling the reservation and I was afraid to navigate away from the chat and lose my progress to save screenshots).  To the extent you claim you needed “proof” of the technical glitch to confirm things happened as I represented, (1) within the required timeframe, I specifically asked REPEATEDLY for assistance canceling the reservation because the deadline was looming, technical glitch or not, the customer service reps should have taken action to cancel, seeking details regarding the technical error would be secondary, (2) because the glitch looped me into the AI agent chat, the technical glitch was already documented and transcribed for the customer service “agent” to see… all they had to do was “scroll up,” (3) there’s no way that a company as large and well resourced as VRBO doesn’t have the technical capability to pull logs that would help them diagnose a user interface glitch from their end, and it’s undoubtedly not believable that VRBO can’t manually cancel reservations, which is what I specifically asked for you to do.***Your customer service reps are halfway around the world, but MY timestamps still read correctly… please do not AGAIN waste time by claiming I first attempted to cancel 12 hours later than I did.Update after contact with Executive Customer Service Team: They insist on a phone call "to discuss" and still claim they need time to "investigate."  I think all of this needs to be handled in writing.  The storyline is simple--I attempted to cancel within the allowable timeframe for a full refund but was unable due to a glitch that pushed me to the robot agent when clicking the cancellation button instead of processing the cancellation.  The robot agent then told me that it couldn't retrieve my reservation details, even though it displayed the reservation details.  When I fought through to a real agent, they insisted that the issue must be "elevated to a tech team." Despite multiple demands for VRBO to manually cancel the reservation, they refused.  If you have evidence that refutes that, please provide it in writing.

name: Adriana Olivo
title: Zero stars!!
text: Zero stars!!! Horrible experience and even worse customer service.Will never ever use this company.We rented a house for my family and a group of 4 other families for NYE and surrounding days. The house was located in Albrightsville,PA. but myself and 3 of the 4 families are all local Long Island families. Upon arrival at the rented property we saw that the property was completely misrepresented, the photos on the VRBO listing were not accurate to how the house actually was and there were health and safety issues.Upon arrival, we found the hot tub was not in a working order and full of mold so obviously had not been working for some time. This was verified a day earlier that the hot tub was fully functional.  There was a media room that we thought had at least a TV.  No TV just a room with chairs. Playroom with foosball table and games for kids.  Turns out this was just a garage (no heat) with one foosball table.  This isn’t even the worst part.  It looked like the home was under construction.  No blinds on windows, visible MOLD in multiple refrigerators, bathrooms.  Gross.  EXPOSED wires and gas lines under cabinets (no cabinets under sink). title: Wow .. but not terribly surprising
text: Wow ... this is a company that has over 117,000 reviews and is barely making 1 star. I guess I should not be terribly shocked that I am now going to add to that abysmal record.Here's the thing about relying on a third-party platform to manage your vacation rental property - you are beholden to what can sometimes be capricious and arbitrary behavior, and there is simply no recourse.  And what's a bit worse is that there is generally barely an acknowledgement that they care in the least bit that they are causing havoc and behaving in a way that would result in 1 star on a platform like Trustpilot.In our case, a disgruntled minority (16%) shareholder in a property that has been listed on VRBO for 8 years , and which has over 50 5-star reviews, hired an attorney to write a letter to VRBO in an effort to sabotage the listing.  And VRBO decided to deactivate the listing permanently "... until all parties are in agreement...".Of course, they are free to do whatever they want, as is made clear in the terms of their service.  And we cannot be shocked that this tactic worked, because legal departments in large corporations will always take the position of caution.  And finally - when you have 20+ competing properties in the same area on their platform, why should VRBO care? They are still going to get their fees - just from another property.So, I get it. If anything , this experience reveals that strictly from a tactical perspective  that the sole reliance on these systems is risky.  And it's also folly to expect any kind of loyalty or value of the "partnership" that they tout so much.My suggestion?  Build yourself a website, and invest in the marketing of it, and figure out direct payments using something like Stripe, etc as a backup. And be sure to discount the price from your VBRO and other large platform listings as you market the property.Whether or not you have a great deal of success, it's a smart idea because you will be prepared, since you just never know what they are going to do.  The least you can do is have a plan and a system to replace them if it comes to it.
