name: Karen de Nobrega
title: Review not posted
text: I was not able to travel to Vancouver Island on December 25th, 2024 because all ferries were cancelled due to storms and gale force winds. As a result, I was not able to make the first night of a two night reservation. My request for a one night refund was ignored by the host so I contacted VRBO. They asked me to send screenshots of newspaper articles proving that the ferries were cancelled due to the storms so I sent them news articles from the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation and Global News reporting the travel disruptions.VRBO has an extenuating circumstances policy which states that when broad scale travel disruptions prevent a VRBO traveller from completing their reservation, VRBO can activate its Extenuating Circumstances Policy, applicable to all bookings made on VRBO and if such an event occurs, and VRBO activates this policy, they must provide refunds for impacted reservations, regardless of the reservation’s cancellation policy.They failed to invoke the policy and told me it was at the host’s discretion. I am very unhappy but I’ve accepted that I will not receive a refund. However, my mostly positive review of the property was declined because I mentioned that ferries were cancelled and I did not receive a one night refund. VRBO is cherry picking reviews. I think potential customers have the right to know that they will not receive a refund for widespread travel disruptions (particularly at this time of year when they may occur).

name: MC
title: I have had a terrible experience with…
text: I have had a terrible experience with VRBO.  The details are below, but the bottom line is that VRBO has partners (referred to as its "VRBO family"), that have listings on the VRBO platform but that seemingly operate separately.  If you have a problem with one of those bookings, which I had for a listing in Paris, you are basically on your own and have to deal with the respective host directly.  Furthermore, the VRBO website is not transparent. I could not get information on the website of how much I had originally paid, nor how much had been refunded when I received a cancellation notice. This is juxtaposed with my experience with Airbnb, where refunds are automatic and all information on all transations are sent by email and available on the website. This is my last dealing with VRBO.  The details of what transpired follow:I booked a place in Paris on the VRBO website whose stated policy was "100% refund of amount payable if you cancel by Feb 11, 2025." When I cancelled on Feb. 4, I got a message from the host indicating that the booking could not be cancelled. After a number of ambiguous communications with the host who would not honor the refund policy, I phoned VRBO customer services. In turn, the VRBO rep phoned the host and got got the same message as I did, that is, that the host was coordinating with the team on the matter. I found the situation highly stressful so contacted VRBO again. VRBO's response was that I should contact the host directly and wait for a response.Today, 24 hours later, I received an email from the host indicating that my reservation had been canceled and "Your refund is based on the property’s cancellation policy. If you have any questions about your refund, please try contacting the host before calling your customer service."  There is no information on the website under my canceled reservation on how much was paid, how much was refunded -- Nothing.  I have messaged the host and am awaiting a response.I am stunned that this is the way VRBO operates! Never again.

I got back and sent all the info they had asked for...bank statements for each hotel, for each day, ...they wanted our family tree!! It has taken 6 weeks for them to send the biggest fabrication and lies I have ever seen a company do. I have emailed twice to escalate it but I know they will ignore it.  They have lied about everything. They are vile and %^&$. I have voice recordings and emails saying they would pay but we are not protected as they are not ABTA.  Please do not use these ever, that goes for expedia..any issues they will lie!!  VRBO have replied under my review...they have not opened a case. Its pure fabrication. text: A Frustrating and Outdated Experience for Property ManagersAs a property manager with over 20 listings on Vrbo, I am beyond disappointed with their lack of support and outdated policies for those of us managing multiple properties. Those of us who use external systems to efficiently manage our properties are essentially punished for doing so. Meanwhile, their customer service is non-existent when it comes to addressing these concerns.If you’re a property manager or anyone with more than a handful of listings, stay away from Vrbo. I’ve resorted to marking up my listings so high on this platform that they don’t book, simply because Vrbo makes it impossible to operate efficiently without losing money.Vrbo’s failure to adapt to industry standards and offer better support for property managers is not just frustrating, it’s a dealbreaker. name: ZAN

name: mark davis

name: DJW
title: Beware of customer service lies
text: We rented a condo for the week after Christmas. I had not heard about check in information so called. Apparently it was already rented and we were stranded with my 6 year old son. Called VRBO, spent 60 mins on the phone and was told that they would reimburse us for up to $638 per night at a hotel for the firs two nights till they could rebook us and to make the reservation through one of their sites or with the hotel directly. We did. I was also told that someone would call to rebook us immediately after the call and 3 hours later, still no one had called. So called back, because we were no staying in a tiny room with no refrigerator and all this food for 6 days I was upset and the woman hung up on me. I called again and was escalated to resolutions team. Giovannie assured me I would get reimbursed and to send him the itemized bills, I told him for the whole week and he said yes. Again the first person said we would be reimbursed for the first two nights but since we had to throw away all our food, pay now for all of our meals and be stuck in a tiny room instead of a lovely 2 bedroom condo, I was adamant about this. Well comes to sending the itemized bill to Giovannie and crickets. Nothing, called and emailed. Still nothing, escalated it to another person ( who promised to help) and escalated and after many many hours on the phone and being lied to many times, we are now not getting reimbursed anything. Because our stay was less than the original price. Never mind that it was not with all the food wasted and meals we then had to purchase. And they lied as they said we would be reimbursed. I will now only use Air B n B and I will not use anything Expedia or VRBO related. BEWARE

name: kristi
title: Feeling lucky? Then this is the booking app for you
text: Imagine you've spent hours scouring the various listings to find the perfect vacation home for your upcoming epic group trip with family. You've looked at every detail, so many properties, but you found just the right one. You click the button. You make the reservation. The payment is made. The owner accepts the booking. Life is good. All you have to do now is book your experiences/excursions. Good times ahead! Until.....the host/property owner decides to cancel your booking without warning somewhere between the day you booked it and the day you are supposed to check-in. That sinking feeling you get when you see the email in your inbox that there has been a vrbo refund. What?! Did I accidentally cancel it somehow? This can't be true. Log into vrbo and sure enough, it is. Still unclear what happened, initiate chat with customer service where I'm told the owner simply canceled the booking. Now I initially thought vrbo was meh to ok with the customer service on this as they gave a $30 (not earth shattering or remotely compensating for the trouble, but something) onekey credit. Silly me didn't realize said credit is just a token gesture and expires within 2 weeks. Great. I had already booked another property in my panic and the silly policy only allows onekey cash to be used at the time of booking. So, I have essentially received nothing for the roller coaster experience. When I contacted vrbo yet again, the response was simply there is nothing we can do and lots of referring me to the fine print.

name: Hedwig
title: I am incredibly grateful to VRBO for…
text: I am incredibly grateful to VRBO for their outstanding support and professionalism after I faced an unfortunate situation with one of their listings. The listing contained false information that severely impacted my holiday, leaving me frustrated and disappointed. However, when I reached out to VRBO’s customer service team, they truly went above and beyond to address the issue.After explaining the situation, they took my concerns seriously and worked quickly to investigate the matter. Ultimately, they provided me with a fair and generous compensation for the inconvenience I had experienced. This thoughtful gesture truly showed me that VRBO values its customers and is committed to ensuring a positive experience, even when things go wrong.While the situation was far from ideal, I feel reassured knowing that VRBO handled it with such care and consideration. It’s not every day that a company takes accountability and shows appreciation for its customers in such a meaningful way. I’m thankful for their quick resolution, and it’s a relief to know that they genuinely care about their customers' well-being. I will certainly continue to use VRBO for my future travels

name: Mabel
title: Misleading listings and horrible customer service
text: 1 star is actually way more than vrbo deserves. My first (and only) experience with Vrbo.  I booked a property in New York for a work trip and I became very sick and contagious 4 days before my trip and could not travel.  I also simultaneously learned that the property I had booked had a shared bathroom, which was not disclosed anywhere in the listing. I knew this listing didn't offer refunds but tried anyway since it was an emergency situation. After being sent on a run-around by your call center representatives and by the person who listed the property, I was told there was nothing they could do since the property owners set the refund policy NOT Vrbo.  Vrbo doesn't care about their customers even when there is a health emergency and a misleading, false listing.  Shared bathroom is kind of a big deal for someone not to disclose. now I'm stuck paying $1800 (including an absurdly high cleaning fee, for a place with apparently major hygiene and pest issues) that I cannot afford for a place I never stayed at. I understand that the property said no refunds but I've dealt with a lot of hotels/companies who will issue at least a partial refund for extenuating circumstances, especially when I was several days away from my trip, and again, the listing with not what I signed up for.  I've deleted the vrbo and expedia apps and will never use again. Shame on you for not putting your customers first and not addressing false and misleading listings.

text: UPDATE - 19 January 2025 - even owners of properties have advised that Vrbo is not up-to-date, it promotes properties that owners have advised are fully booked - so all in all - not reliable or another way of putting it, lacks integrity.Even Vrbo reply below does nothing to support consumer - it's a pseudo (insincere) customer service reply. name: Kim C
title: VRBO NOT PAYING HOSTS
text: UpdateSince posting this review, I was immediately contacted by phone and in writing by Les from the VRBO Social Response Team, who completely understood my problem, oversaw it's resolution, made a goodwill gesture and kept in touch throughout the whole process. I couldn't have asked for a better service, and it's a real pity that this level of professionalism is a rare find. Thank you Les.ref:!00DC00PxQg.!5008b02j6fKW:ref ]Vrbo 135038809     [ ref:!00DC00PxQg.!5008b02iyaIC:refVrbo 134506137    [ ref:!00DC00PxQg.!5008b02iOcwL:ref ]For the second time, VRBO is not paying rent owed to me and has consistently failed to take action despite my opening several cases with support.  A renter cancelled a stay before making the final payment. Under my terms, no refund is due to the renter. VRBO took their full commission, as if full payment had been received and the rent taken place. The residual amount of the deposit is due to me.  This took place on 5th December 2024.  The payment should have immediately been activated and according to the booking information was actioned on that date.  However, no payment was made and every single day, my account updates to fraudulently state that the payment was made on that particular date. On 16th December 2024, a supervisor called Richard assured me the payment had been made. It hadn't.  On 20th December a customer service rep, Sushmita, said that the payment had definitely been made on that date, and confirmed this in writing.  It hadn't of course. Every time I have tried to reply to a customer service email, I simply get the message that my case is closed.  On 2nd January 2025, I managed to summon the energy for a miserable afternoon on the chat and phone service to customer support. After spending far too long with a brain dead rep, I finally insisted that I get put through to another Supervisor. This time I got Ammar, who sent me an email telling me that my case has been referred on.  Since then I have written to him four times including a screenshot showing that my account has once again updated to say that payment was made on 3rd, then 4th, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th, 9th January etc etc. Ammar has not given me the courtesy of a reply. The only communication VRBO has initiated to me was on 2nd January to tell me that they were suspending my account as I had signed in too many times!!!  The inefficiency, the indifference and total indolence I have experienced from customer service is unbelievable. I am posting here to demand action from VRBO.  Pay me what I am owed.

name: Alex Tsai

text: January 10, 2024 (Edit):A representative named Marcques from Vrbo reached out to me via email to address this issue. title: LEFT STRANDED
text: Do not use this site , booked for fuerteventura for 3 weeks over Xmas and new year , only to find the apartment wasn't trading anymore so left stranded with now to stay, I had informed them earlier of my concerns but was assured it was OK. name: Tom Barry
title: Just when I thought they couldn't get any worse...
text: I am a host and I advertise on VRBO. Against my better judgement, I was persuaded by them to allow instant bookings with the promise that this would lead to more reservations. It didn't, but that is not the current cause of complaint. I was told that I could set house rules which would enable me to reject any instant bookings which contravened those rules - and to reject them without penalty.This turned out to be untrue. I set a rule to say that groups with more than six adults had to contact me before booking. A second rule said that guests with pets must contact me before booking. Finally I got an instant booking - from a group of eight adults with a pet. So I immediately cancelled the reservation.During the cancellation process (which was not easy) I was informed that my listing would be suspended for seven days. So in fact there WAS a penalty. I was also asked to agree to refund the guest's payment - this is complete nonsense of course, as the guest had not paid me. VRBO had taken and were holding the payment.I contacted VRBO. This meant 25 minutes in a queue, 1 minute of conversation and then being cut off. Another call, another queue. The online chat promised a 30 minute wait - until you joined it, when 30 minutes became 60. And they call this support.I did eventually get VRBO to cancel the booking. They then sent a message to the French guest in English. VRBO gave my UK phone number for the guest to call if they had any queries about the 5 to 7 day delay on repayment. I have a French number for Francophone guests and always speak to them in French.In all VRBO made the experience unpleasant and stressful for me and for my potential guest. They made me look unprofessional, which I work hard not to be. The lack of professionalism was not mine.

name: sara ekmekciu
title: The company is fake at all.All they are…
text: The company is fake at all.All they are doing is stealing your money and give you wrong directions.Dont trust them in any case!!!The worst company of all

name: Julian Vicari
title: Homeaway or now VRBO used to be a very…
text: Homeaway or now VRBO used to be a very good website for the renting Villa's. Lately the website just does not work. The filters keep removing themselves and resetting, when you select a property often there is most of the information missing, ie description of the property, the price is missing and biggest of all no way to book ! There is absolutely no booking option. I dont know whether its an issue with my account but I've used Edge, Chrome, incognito mode, cleared cache/cookies, used 3 different computers all the same. Terrible experience using the website and dont get me started with the app!

name: Mr Miles
title: No customer service and cut you off regularly
text: Had an issue with the property rented through VRBO. After hours on calls got through to agent to then be cut off. No customer services.Had raw sewage pouring out into the shower in master bedroom and VRBO think it is ok for the owner to offer a refund of 1.5% Absolutely ridiculous. DO not book through VRBO, they have no customer service

name: Susan
title: Bait and Switch and Dishonestly Not Posting Negative Reviews
text: I originally wrote the following as a review on vrbo.com, but it was inexplicably rejected.  I think VRBO is both dishonest and stupid for not allowing unfavorable but honest reviews.  Eventually the public will figure out that the reason all the reviews are so good on VRBO is because VRBO won't post bad reviews.  The only possible inaccuracy below is whether the host or VRBO provided the refund.  I was unsure who initiated it."I reserved apartment #2, but we were given the entry codes to apartment #3 without being told they were for apartment #3. We couldn’t gain entry and missed the first night. The host refunded the money for that night. The next day we were told we were to be in apartment #3. Although I asked twice I never received an answer as to why we were switched. I had reserved #2 because it had a king-sized bed. Apartment #3 has a queen. Having a larger bed may not be important to some guests, but it was important to us."Additionally, the host gave me a hard time about the refund claiming I only paid for 4 nights instead of 5.  I did initially pay for 4 nights but then added and paid for a 5th night.  He was too lazy to do the researrch to realize this, so I had to do it for him.  I told him via private message that I will NEVER rent from him again, which is sad because we visit the Uptown area in Minneapolis where he has rentals once or twice each year.I had initially thought that the host was the problem, but after reading the reviews on Trustpilot, I see that VRBO has many of its own problems.A few days after I posted the above paragraphs, a nice VRBO agent called me and said he would find out why my negative review was not accepted to be posted on vrbo.com.  I received an email from VRBO stating, "I wanted to inform you that your review has been submitted to our system; however, it has unfortunately been rejected due to the disclosure of the property's location."  I do not mention an address or any way to locate the property in my review.  This just seems like another bogus reason not to post a negative review.VRBO now says that mentioning apartment numbers is disclosing the location.  I rewrote the review without apartment numbers.  We'll see if they post it now.Now they say only I can post it if I have the email in which they rejected my review the first time.  I no longer have it, so they win.  A bad review will not be posted on vrbo.com.I GIVE UP!  It's no wonder people don't post bad reviews there.  I have jumped through hoop after hoop and still can't post the review so people know that the host where we rented an apartment is not so great and definitely NOT responsive.

name: Shay
title: Hosts not being paid
text: I’ve been waiting weeks for my pay out as a host! I’m told it’s pending but nothing. Other host have shared that they have been waiting months for payments. Will not take anymore booking from this site, sticking to Airbnb who pay their hosts on time.

name: Chris
title: Avoid this company
text: We booked a property and when we showed up, the code didn’t work but there were 4 unknown individuals inside that opened the door and said they were fixing the lock. We felt unsafe. They were there with us for 20 minutes then left. The place was also in need of cleaning so we went to buy cleaning supplies to stay in it. While out, the owner called and said the 4 people were coming back to the property again later. We felt even more unsafe and said we weren’t going to stay there. Owner offered a full refund but said we had to get it through VRBO. Tried calling them a few times but couldn’t get through.  In the meantime we received a call from the owner saying it was dirty and would require an additional cleaning fee. We hadn’t even stayed at the property. The place was as we found it. Eventually got in touch with VRBO and told them what happened. Owner now refuses to give the refund and company says that since we did not take pictures of the unknown individuals at the property that they won’t issue a refund. Even though the supervisor we spoke to admitted they wouldn’t have taken pictures either. Avoid this company!  Awful to deal with! Deceitful and no integrity.

name: Ian
title: Tried to book twice with this outfit
text: Tried to book twice with this outfit - the owners dont respond so it would suggest that they havent really signed up - will not use VRBO ever now

name: M M
title: Negligent, misinformed and washing hands
text: Neither the platform nor the host for a Helsinki flat costing over 180euros per night announced that the check in was only possibly until 10pm! We arrived from the airport at 2am and found a message from that morning (while we were flying) that the check in was only possible until 10pm and were left in the -12c cold with small children in a foreign country without shelter. We took the first hotel we found available and paid 330euros for that night. The host washed her hands and said she couldn’t do anything and took zero responsibility for this gross negligence of not disclosing critical information. The platform also washed their hands and blamed me for not “following the rules” when the “rules” were only informed to me a few hours before the check in opened and while I was traveling without internet. I tried to fight my case and they refunded me less than a third of my costs incurred due to their negligence. Not only that, we got a bad cold due to standing in the freezing weather and we ended up going to sleep at 4am. We missed the 9am tour on our only day in Helsinki and also we spent the entire holidays with a bad cold. I highly recommend to never book with them. Awful negligent unprofessional and inconsiderate experience. They will ruin your trip and beyond.

name: TK
title: Save your life FRAUD VRBO STAYZ
text: Save your life, close this fraud business VRBO, one booking cancelled without any reason, second one no check in instructions provided host says on phone to me no booking for you, chasing customer service for 2 days after my booking still saying we are sorry and someone will email or call but nothing happens,  No refund Yet FRAUD BUSINESS , 3 days still no email from you guys and FRAUD business sends email thanks for your stay where you can't even provide check in instructions,  no response no refund when your host clearly states no booking for me, where is my refund and 1,000 dollar compensation,  FRAUD DISASTER NEVER use VRBO save your trip and life

name: Ron Wheeler
title: wil never use vrbo again, no accountability
text: Had used vrbo for years in the US with no problems. Went to Paris and it was a disaster. The address on the link was wrong so we ended up 2.5 hours standing in the cold messaging and finally talking on the phone with them so that guest ready eventually could give map coordinates to get us where we needed. Couldnt even hold them accountable to the point of booting them off the site if they continued as they were. Will never use vrbo again

name: Mary Melstrom
title: VRBO refused to pay me what was due.
text: VRBO never collected the 2nd payment and allowed the customer into my property without full payment. They never notified me of the outstanding payment due and gave the customer access. I pay them to book the property and collect the money. They say it is up to me to get the customer to pay. They stated they gave the customer 3 notices of late payment and I only found one that was made 40 days prior to planned occupancy.This has happened twice in the last 60 days. The first customer was unaware and made the payment.They thought there credit card would automatically be charged. The 2nd customer is currently in my unit and his phone on the app has been disconnected. VRBO says I need to handle this. They said I could call the authorities and have them removed. I have posted the paperwork with the overdue  notice on the door of the unit and requested payment and informed them they would be locked out as this is a condo hotel.. VRBO offered to cancel the booking which would not get me my money so that would be useless.I highly recommend that you as an host owner  never allow split payments. I am out $$$$$ for allowing it.Customer service agents have no idea how to fix anything and moving the issue up the ladder is worthless. I have spent hours and not resolved anything.Also note, they are not a member of the Better Business Bureau.

name: robert dick
title: VRBO team members untrained and…
text: VRBO team members untrained and useless.Called VRBO because host didn’t submit any paperwork to get HOA approval after accepting our reservation. Host then threatened to delay our trip 2 days before we left and after our car was shipped.VRBO team member didn’t know what an  HOA was .25 minute wait to speak to a supervisor who offered a 1 ( up to 3 night) stay while host waited for HOA approval which of course did not prevent host fromGiving us access. They follow a script and in general don’t know their own policies or procedures. Also ignorant of laws pertaining to renting.They ( as usual) are ALL foreign so u need to speak slowly and spell things like your emails.Who owns this absurdly poor company. Why can’t the Feds shut them down. Why no class action lawsuits? This is what happens to quality of life in a country like ours where most companies sacrifice customer service for short term profit. If you are older like me you remember a day when a call to customer service got you a quick response from an American who was highly trained and actually fixed problems without an hour of waiting.Agh!!!!

name: Ms MJ
title: VRBO let guests stay without paying and deny any liability!!!!!
text: VRBO has allowed guests stay in our London house without paying.  I discovered this when reconciling my books at the end of the year after which VRBO were a useless pile of scrap at every contact.  Guests stayed in May having booked in February.  VRBO had not collect the rent from them before they arrived and I did not have any king of notification that notify me in any way that the rent had not been collected or was overdue.  This meant the guests have stayed free.  When I contacted VRBO by phone they told me to chase the guest myself and collect the rent as it's nothing to do with them, even though I don't have the guests details (nor the means to accept credit card payments should they want to pay) so we have lost thousands of pounds and VRBO say it's not their problem.  Then VRBO also sent me an email saying they've asked for more info from me from an email they sent to previouslyand the case will be closed if I don't supply this information. They do not specify what the information requested was and in fact have not sent me any emails, and yes, I have checked my spam file.  Every time I call customer service I just get the call centre person saying 'the payment is overdue' and 'we emailed the guest and they haven't replied'.  Do they think this is acceptable? I'm never, ever using them again.  Appalling!!!!!  Airbnb never has problems like this.

name: Dorji Wangchuk

name: N Baldwin

I have called a few times, each time I get a different story; I have no faith in Vrbo, too many mistakes and misinformation.

name: Leo P.
title: Dishonest, manipulative company, with horrible customer service
text: On August 4, 2024, my property was booked via VRBO without my permission / authorization / prior agreement, which resulted in a cancellation. As I explained to VRBO on multiple occasions (in September, October, and December 2024), I had never agreed to my property being booked without my prior review of the visitor, and my personal authorization.  Instead, VRBO system set my account to allow for immediate, unauthorized acceptance of reservations.  All my attempts to resolve the issue with VRBO have resulted in nothing more than canned responses.  VRBO keeps sending me invoices threatening to suspend my account, which makes no sense, since I removed the property from their listing myself, after this most unpleasant experience. I have requested assistance in preventing VRBO from further harassing me with their past-due notices by filing complaints with the FTC and BBB.  I'd strongly recommend any property owner to never get involved with VRBO.

name: Lorraine Green
title: I will never book again with VRBO
text: I will never book again with VRBO. My booking for a holiday July 2025 was booked, confirmed and deposit paid 500 euros in Oct 2024. Then I discovered 2 days ago that 9 days after my booking our dates were changed but without any communication. A one time pass code had been activated but not by us.When we contacted Host they didn't say we had changed dates but that their agent had booked someone in for our dates. Suspicious. Although our booking had been guaranteed they choose a longer stay wirh another customer over our booking. Had I not noticed it would have ruined our holiday next year. VRBO was not very helpful. Not risking booking again with them.

name: Colin Murray
title: Booked an apartment at 23 Rue De La…
text: Booked an apartment at 23 Rue De La Reverence Brussels for first Christmas away.On arriving greeter was unfriendly/unhelpful, basically handed us the keys and left us to it.The apartment was large but five floors up(75 steps).The decor was minimalist, white walls black wood floors.Kitchen light was broken.Shower was broken.Fridge door broken.Lounge settee(large L shaped)and its throws/cushions were filthy.Smelt and looked really bad.Dining chairs, lifted cushions to discover crumbs/nuts etc.Bedroom one, mattress is to small for divan and constantly slid about as did the sheet which was to large for the mattress.Water for bath was somewhere between lukewarm and a few degrees higher.Pressure was so low it took ages to run a bath.We had asked for a tree as it was Christmas and we had our 5 year old Grandson along.A tree was present on arrival put no pot or stand for it and no decorations(despite telling us we would have both).The heat in the apartment soon dried it out and the needles fell.We ended up buying a small imitation tree locally.This could be a great apartment but sadly is neglected and dirty.We continually tried to address issues with the owner but clearly he had no interest.He just wants the money and no fuss.I strongly advise you do not stay at this apartment.We presented our concerns to Vrbo but they also showed no interest whatsoever.

name: Toni and Kevin and family Riga
title: Arapawa Island, Gunyah homestead, Arapawa Seafarms
text: Arapawa Island Sea Farms holiday rental was wonderful in many ways.  The location was magical with views to the mouth of Kura Te Au (Tory Chanel).  Two beaches offered safe swimming within a short stroll from the old homestead house, Gunyah.  The hosts warmly welcomed us on the wharf and efficiently transported us with our belongings to the house.  The house was spacious and well equipped, including an ample supply of towels,  and had a log fire.  The children enjoyed the freedom of the  grounds around the house,  feeding the resident eels and fishing off the wharf.  Historically it was interesting with the ruins of the old Perano whaling station within easy walk. Whekenui Bay is where the great explorer Kupe killed his pursuer the octopus.  The tui, weka and kererū were plentiful and the pōhutakawa trees put on a magnificent show of red flowers. The Picton Water Taxi (Beachcomber Cruises) service was excellent.

name: Troy
title: I booked an apartment in Portland Maine…

They have been advertising her listing for the 2 YEARS since she has been in Japan.  What a joke this company is!!!  I will never use them again!

name: Lucinda Robins

The apartment resembles a prison cell.Reference number - 25133516

name: Kenneth Barber
title: Worst experience ever!
text: I booked a house for my wife, kids and I. I never received any information from the host at all. Now I have to find another rental. The virtual assistant is a joke! I just keep getting the run a round. This is the worst APP to use. I should have done my research.

name: jmac1975
title: Villa Luna Playa Blanca Lanzarote
text: Avoid at all costs!!!This is the first and last time I'll book a property via VRBO. I've been to playa blanca many times before and stayed at both hotels and villas and never before have i experienced anything like this. On this holiday, i travelled with my family, including children. Firstly the photographs of the villa on the advert were a complete misrepresentation of the villa itself, which bore little resemblance to what we saw when we arrived. We were absolutely the street speechless at the state of it. To say the villa was filthy would be an understatement. It was covered in flies, the rooms were run down and in need of repair, the main doors wouldnt shut properly, the curtains were all dirty, bathrooms were dirty and main bathroom kept flooding, bedding was disgusting, furniture was old and in need of replacement, there was a smell of urine in the main bedroom and it was dodge the coakroaches at night. The only thing going for this villa is the pool. I did raise concerns when we arrived, this was not an easy process and we were offered an alternative villa next door which was in a similar state, so we did not accept. We did try and seek alternative accommodation, however, anything decent was already booked. We were eventually reimbursed a small part of the booking but this did not make up for the overall terrible accommodation. This experience ruined our holiday and i will not be rushing back to this resort as a result.

name: Peter Axton
title: There can be no stars for this company
text: There can be no stars for this company.I booked a stay in a ski resort from boxing day til the 2nd of January. Paid for the stay on the 29 of November. Booked all the Travel arrangements since then. Christmas night, 7 hours before I  was due to begin my journey,  the host cancelled my reservation! I must now book and pay for alternative accommodation (nothing guaranteed at this late stage) and then face having to find emergency accommodation if I proceed with my travel plans. Vrbo will take 15 days to process the refund, airbnb.co.uk will be similar. Effectively I now face paying 3 ski holidays before any refund.  Vrbo, you need to step up. Considerably!

name: WB
title: I've removed my apartment from VRBO site because they're a disgrace
text: My experience of VRBO is from the opposite side than most reviews on here. I rent out a holiday apartment. It is fully booked for the next 12 months (no bookings through VRBO) and the VRBO availability calendar was up-to-date. Yesterday on Christmas Eve I was notified that a guest had booked my property for 6 nights arriving on 28th December!As my apartment is fully booked it should not have been possible for anyone to book it. I checked the calendar and was horrified to see that it was completely empty and showing all dates as being available. I messaged the person who had booked and explained something had gone wrong with the VRBO system. I had to cancel his booking and I ordered a full refund (hosts don't get the payment until VRBO send it). I spent Christmas eve trying to sort it out with VRBO, who said I had to send a photo of my calendar from before his booking to prove it was already booked!! How am I supposed to do that?!? All my bookings reappeared later, then disappeared and reappeared again in front of my eyes.VRBO said I am going to be charged a cancellation fee for cancelling this booking and they are not going to offer any compensation to the man who booked.It's an absolute disgrace. I have removed my apartment from the VRBO website and deleted my account. My guests are very important to me and I feel terrible knowing  that this poor man probably hates me for what has happened even though it was not my fault and VRBO couldn't care less.My advice to hosts and guests..... Do not use VRBO.

name: Lona Manning
title: Hundreds of dollars down the drain, miserable experience.
text: I planned a trip to Boston in October ahead of a conference in Cleveland. I found a cozy one bedroom suite to recover from jet lag and work on my conference presentation and speech.  I waited at the airport for the host to give me the address. When we finally got the address and got there, it was clear it was not the property I had seen and rented on VRBO. Bait and switch. Further, although we were tired from our flight, we couldn't check in until after 6 pm because it was still being set up. We had to leave and wait for another two hours. When we did check in we discovered there was no internet. I mean no server, there was nothing there. No chair, no table, no desk, not even an end table. Exhausted, we fell asleep. The next morning we left the property, I said I would pay for that first night but wanted a refund for the next two nights. I had just three nights in Boston but I was supposed to contact VRBO and then wait for them and the host to resolve the issue. With no internet and no international data plan on my phone. The host later messaged me he was going to "replace" the server as though there was a repair that needed to be done, but there was no server there. The place had just been set up and was half-furnished. Since my experience in October he has gotten more bad reviews but VRBO is standing behind him, not me.

name: Chris Morgan
title: We will never use VRBO again
text: We will never use VRBO again! The first 2 places we booked through them cancelled on us last minute to tell us they already had reservations after dozens of family members came in from out of state. VRBO finally found us a 3rd place, only for the rental property to have different booking dates and try to kick us out a day early. The customer service reps at VRBO were helpful and did their jobs extremely well. But the company as a whole needs to get their crap together. Would not recommend to anyone.

name: Jon Eversett
title: Terrible organisation
text: Terrible organisation. We booked a three bedroom property through Vbro only to find out it's listed elsewhere as two bedrooms - it actually only does have two bedrooms. Called Customer Service on multiple occasions and received stalling tactics. On the most recent call they told us we had to take it up with the managing agent even though the details of the property were incorrect only on the Vrbo site. We're still trying to get our money back. Avoid!

name: Gabriele
title: VRBO exclusions

name: LIAM BURNETT

name: Alison Hillman
title: Terrible. They cancelled last minute and by e mail
text: Terrible! I booked rental accomm 4 months ahead- all confirmed- but the host cancelled it. I did not find out until I arrived there. I was left without accommodation - totally stranded, the Sat before Christmas, with chilled grocery shopping I had done, nowhere to put it, and no way of using/ cooking it. There had been other issues with this company and host before that.   it said ‘pets go free’ and the host, once I had booked and paid for it, then told me it was £35 extra. When I said it said ‘pets free’ she suddenly stopped answering and Vrbo sent me messages telling me I need to pay £35 and if I don’t pay it my booking is at risk. To cancel a booking by e mail at the last minute leaving guests stranded without anywhere to stay is unforgivable! Ruined my weekend which was supposed to be a really special occasion with family.

name: roma mosmer

name: Peter
title: “Homes all to yourself”?!!!
text: So much for offering homes “all to yourself”. Maybe the most unsafe uncomfortable travel experience of my life and when I called vrbo they told me I needed photo proof of the random guy staying in the house to issue a refund. What a miserable business.

name: John Stevens
title: I am extremely disappointed with VRBO…
text: I am extremely disappointed with VRBO and will never use this site for travel plans again. I booked a property three months ago, only to receive a call yesterday (December 20) from a company called Distinctive Beach Rentals (DBR), claiming they were canceling my reservation. The person who called spoke poor English, was dismissive, and left me questioning whether the call was even legitimate.When I sent a message through VRBO for clarification, they forwarded my email to DBR, who then emailed me back stating that the reservation wasn't canceled but that I would need to move to a different property. The "alternatives" they sent were up to 100 miles away from my original booking, which is completely unacceptable.This is not an isolated incident—this is the third time a booking has been canceled through VRBO. The lack of reliability and accountability is appalling. If you want peace of mind for your travel plans, look elsewhere. VRBO has proven to be completely untrustworthy, and I will never use this service again.

name: Kirsty Hunter
title: Christmas booking cancelled 2 days before traveling
text: On the 29th October I booked an expensive country cottage via VRBO for Christmas. I live in the Netherlands and wanted to spend Christmas in the UK with my family. I paid in full on the day of booking and received an email confirmation. Today 2 days before I get on the ferry to travel to have Christmas with my family VRBO sent an email canceling my booking - I am absolutely devastated and disgusted that a company (and the owner - who ignored all my messages) can treat consumers with such disregard and disrespect. To top it all off I have to wait 15 days for a full refund!!

name: Ibro Gulamov
title: Bad experience
text: Bad experience. Fraudulent moves from hosts. No control under service. Don't recommend to use stressful ervice.

name: Sarah Shabanie
title: Muhammad was wonderful and he helped me…
text: Muhammad was wonderful and he helped me resolve an issue I had with an owner. He is very professional and his customer service is over the top. Thank you.

name: Guillaume Paturel
title: extreme caution.
text: A few months ago, I opened a VRBO account without realizing that the rental calendar was automatically open to bookings. To be fair, the option to manage the calendar is far from intuitive—finding it feels like solving a puzzle, which seems intentional. You practically need to be an expert to figure it out.The worst happened: my house was rented without my knowledge. When I tried to log into my account to fix the situation, I found myself locked out due to endless security procedures. It was an incredibly frustrating experience.After multiple attempts, I finally managed to contact VRBO. I asked them to close my account, and they were able to cancel the unauthorized booking. But this morning, I received yet another blow: a $1,900 bill, due immediately.This whole experience has been nothing short of a nightmare. VRBO’s system feels designed to trap users. If you’re considering using this platform, proceed with extreme caution.

name: Lars Pedersen
title: Not at all as it should be
text: We hired a castle in France for the 2024 family summer holidays. All looked wonderful on the pictures on VRBO.com and matched the seemingly fake reviews.Unfortunately the very first moment of our stay showed to be symbolic for how this magnificent property has been taken care of during the last 10 years or more. There were no host to receive us on the agreed arrival time, and the host did not answer his phone. All doors were locked and prior to this we haven’t received any information apart from the arrival time. Imagine the frustration and panic in our group of 36 guests. We managed to get into the property via Vrbo support during a 35 minute long phone call. Ridiculous when you have paid 20,000 euros upfront for one week stay.The add on Vrbo.com said “…. Castle in perfect condition”. That is a lie. The castle is falling apart on the outside and the same picture is taking form in the basement, some of the rooms and all of the windows. The surrounding areas have not been taken care of apart from 5-10 meter surrounding the castle. I could go on. The overall cleaning was limited to the main corridors and staircase, leaving dust and filth in almost every corner of every room.Such a shame for such a wonderful property. We tried to get the host to reason on a refund on some of the paid rent but he newer bothered to answer any of our messages. Afterwards we got a really bad review as a guest from the host, and since July 2024 I have tried to get VRBO.com to post our review of the property and host. They keep ignoring us and instead I can read new reviews with perfect ratings on the property from guest who apparently have stayed right after our visit...Stay away from VRBO.comBest regardsLars PedersenNB!Just to prove my point regarding vrbo.com, I have inserted a copy of the e-mails I have recevied from vrbo.com after I published this review on Trustpilot on December 19, 2024 and gave vrbo.com the required details about my booking and trip.E-mail from Vrbo Support on December 23, 2024:"Dear LarsThank you for reaching out to Social Response TeamThe Social Response team has received your concerns about your previous booking complaint. We're empowered to help with escalations of this nature.Please be assured that we’ll look into this immediately and get back to you as soon as we've completed the necessary research.To make sure any replies to this email remains linked to your open case, please don’t remove the subject line or reply in a separate email.Thank you for the opportunity to assist with your concern.Regards,JainzVrbo Social Response Team"E-mail from Vrbo Support on December 27, 2024:"Dear LarsHi,I hope this email finds you well.As we further investigate, it seems that your booking is already a post-stay. However, we would like to request proof of your misrepresentation claim at that time. We need this evidence so that we can proceed or look for possible ways to help you with your concern. We will wait until December 30, 2024, for your response along with the requested proof.I hope everything is in order now.Have a wonderful day!Regards,JainzVrbo Social Response Team"E-mail from Vrbo Support on December 30, 2024:"Dear Lars,Thank you for your continued patience and understanding as we addressed the concerns you brought to our attention.We have ensured that a comprehensive summary of our discussions has been communicated to our Leadership Team, ensuring they are fully aware of the situation and your valuable feedback.We deeply regret that we cannot provide you with further assistance due to the lack of responsiveness to our emails, and we extend our sincerest apologies for any inconvenience this may have caused.Should there be any additional documentation that necessitates a re-evaluation of your case, we encourage you to respond directly to this email to ensure continuity.Please understand that without new documentation, we will not be able to revisit the resolution for this issue, as all options have been fully explored. For any new issues or assistance required, do not hesitate to reach out to Customer Support at 877-202-4291 or visit our Help Center for guidance.Regards,JainzVrbo Social Response Team"

name: Anna Jackson
title: Dreadful company as a host AVOID
text: Dreadful company. As a host they currently owe me almost 5,000gbp. name: Adrian Bullock
title: Refunded my money Poor host partners
text: This is my first experience using this app, it appealed as it was the platform where I found a very nice property for my xmas get away.  I booked months in advance and was definitely worried about paying in advance.  Fast forward to 3 days before travel and no information from the host, no answer to my in app message or direct text message.  Spoke to the online customer services who also tried to contact the host (total 3 times I spoke with them and they tried to contact the host) now hours before I fly and 1 day from check in I have asked for a refund so I can source alternative accommodation.  This has been agreed to and confirmed by email although the money has yet to land.  I expected the worst given all the reviews but am happy they have refunded the money but very annoyed one of their partners! Has caused me so much hassle hours before I travel……

name: Suzette
title: Vrbo not honoring booking and not refunding
text: I booked accommodation on Expedia and paid in full; last week I wanted to check the details of the property and it shows on Expedia, but the details could not be accessed. Expedia then informed me it was with Vrbo. I contacted the host as well as Vrbo but my booking (still on Expedia) did not exist on Vrbo. According to the host Vrbo was not suppose to advertise it. I have spent a lot of time and money to phone Vrbo (I am in South Africa) and have sent numerous emails. I do not get any reply/feedback as to how they are going to refund me.On Thursday they told me that they could not see the payment on their system and I had to provide them with a ct card statement to proof that I have actually paid!! This after I have sent them the receipt as well as the confirmation of the booking.I have thus lodged a case of fraud via my bank which results in the ct card being cancelled and replaced (again at our cost). We also had to book and pay for another accommodation option as we are leaving for Dublin on 22 December.I have never had such a bad experience and I regard this as either a case of fraud or plain theft.

name: Richard Ganley
title: First booking cancelled
text: Signed up and made my first booking. It's was cancelled a couple of days later with no explanation as to why. Seems to be a pointless waste of time to me and won't bother using again! Pretty offended.

name: Graham Logan
title: 1 star is the lowest you can award
text: I have been a Vrbo host, and it's previous name since 2006. It used to be such a good company, now it is disgraceful. Terrible system, pitiful support, no system to complaint about them, and no way to recieve a refund from them for a new listing that has not worked since it was set up. Shocking to see how unprofessional they have become-

name: JEANETTE
title: Customer service is non existent
text: I had a reservation at a property in Bali, which said 7 minute walk to beach and it was incorrect as it was in a mountain.I contacted host via vrbo who was happy to refund me but says he has not received the payment.I have been in contact with VRBO via chat, several times, as I  cannot call using my phone in Bali and keep getting told to go through the host. I am going from host to vrbo and still no closer to the refund back to the card I made payment on.It is an impossible situation and they do not have a complaint email either.The host is having the same difficulty trying to contact them.I would avoid VRBO as a host or traveller

name: Julien Brungard
title: Do NOT use them!
text: Do NOT use them!Luxury penthouse in Hills Road, Number 9 The Levels (City View Terrace), Cambridge, was an awful experience. Cleaning not done, half of what they advertised for didn't work, even the wi-fi, for which we got the owner to provide a mobile wi-fi, but he didn't want to top it up himself - he tried to get us to do it with the promise to pay us back later. name: Luke Moore
title: Is there a zero stars option?
text: Is there a zero stars option?Booking made for a property in Birmingham (host Mariam Alvi under the name brightside properties). Had a message on the day of arrival saying it was booked in error. Requested refund. No replies and 2 weeks later now about to take further action. Vrbo customer service non existent. Utterly shit.

name: Lida Maria
title: THEY CANCELLED MY RESERVATION AND DID NOT FULLY REFUND ME!
text: I received a cancellation from the owner because the house had some damages but then I di not receive full refund! I have been trying to find a customer support line BUT THERE IS NONE! How is it possible to have a booking platform where too many things can go wrong without a support line?! Really not recommended!

name: Jalla Hertoghe
title: Terrible experience!!! Scammers villa didn’t exist
text: Terrible experience!!!! We lost 20.000 euros and the villa actually never existed. We have been scammed and VBRO did not do anything, no reimbursement, they never took the responsibility of contacting us back. They did not respect their engagement and we didn’t get our money back. Be careful and don’t be scammed

name: A. Hudson
title: Customer support for hosts doesn't exist!
text: Customer support for hosts doesn't exist! It is unclear what number to dial if you even find that information. I had a problem with a reservation, I was finally able to talk to somebody in english who could not help me. He said that it will be forwarded to a "concern" department and that they will get back to me. I never heard back from anybody! I talked to 4 more persons who could not speak english and also could not transfer me to english speaking service agents. How can you trust working with a company without customer service!!!

name: Amy Ziegelmeyer
title: Beware! Owners can make strange requirements!
text: We are currently dealing with VRBO over a last minute rental. We booked a cabin in Gatlinburg, TN a week before check in. After booking, the property owner called and forced us to have an hour long conversation on all things Gatlinburg (even though we told her we had been there more than 30 times). Once we completed the conversation to her satisfaction, she sent us her contracts to sign. There were lots of unreasonable things required in the contract. All giant red flags so we contacted her and asked to cancel since we did not agree or the terms of the contract. She refused. I explained that had she disclosed these “requirements” on the property listing, I would not have booked but she still refused. VRBO also refused to assist us and lied, saying the contract is available on their page. I checked again, and it is not. We have used VRBO without incident for 20 years. We will never use them again. So beware. They protect the property owner, not the consumer.

name: Sue Thompson
title: VRBO endorses rogue hosts
text: VRBO allow rogue business to operate on their sites as hosts and endorse them promising “ trust and security”, “ VRBO has your back”, “price guarantee”. total rubbish. Host took thousands from me then “cancelled” a booking they never made. I have no holiday and no refund.AND VRBO STILL DO NOTHING. There appears to be no consequences for the host and no support or money back for me. I am truly appalled.I will never use them again and suggests no one else does until they clean up their business.After posting this review I was contacted by VRBO social media team who apologised and sympathised with my position.Funnily enough …… they still have done NOTHING to help me regain my money or find me alternative accommodation. It’s a big con.

name: Nigel
title: DONT STAY AT LUXURY OASIS HOUSE : SPECTACULAR 5 STARS RETREAT IN LAS VEGAS
text: Booked a place in Las Vegas called Luxury Oasis via Vrbo. Place stated views of the strip. True if you had military grade binoculars as this place was 10 miles away! We didn’t stay there. Owner not refunding us anything. Suggest payments should go to Vrbo and when clients pleased with the stay the money is then moved to the owner.

name: Alex
title: Shambolic customer service
text: If I could give this company, zero stars, I would. We booked an apartment through Expedia who used VRBO to source the property. First the property was listed In the wrong location (10km away from listed location) and this was only found out on arrival at the airport. The property was listed falsely on bookingcom and Expedia. When we arrived the appartment was run down and in need of repair. There was an inspection going on as we arrived to the room as the bath had been leaking into a property below.After going through Expedia to be told our complaint needed to be taken up with VRBO themselves. We were given a refund that was arranged by the hotel themselves and not the providers, VRBO then agreed on a further amount of compensation to be credited our account for future holidays, so far it’s been over 40 days and approximately 15 hours on the phone. Majority of that being put on hold. This company falls so short of customer service they should be embarrassed. We have emails to back the issue and hope that it is resolved soon. But for now the situation has been more than frustrating.

name: Miki Heinrich
title: Horrible customer support and host…
text: Horrible customer support and host support! I used to like this company and it went down the hill with horrible support app bugs and overcharging customers and hosts. This company will bankrupt in no time with the way they run business . I used to do 95% business with vrbo now I avoid . The support lies constantly create own rules , lie about waiving cancellation fees so they can  push you to cancel reservations that is agains your cancellation policy and then suspend your 5* listing !

name: Catherine Chen

name: Lou
title: Suspisciously property I had booked was no longer available
text: I recently booked somewhere and then after a few weeks got a phone call from the company that rented out the property who told me it was no longer availble and offered me another place with a £500 discount. They sent me through a link to this other property directly to my email address. I phoned Vrbo as I thought it seemed suspiscious but all they did was confirm that the link was valid. name: Barry o connor
title: Booked and paid 1850€ for a camper van…
text: VRBO subsequently contacted me and tried to blame everybody else for their short comings.Ultimately there service was deplorable and it is not good enough to blame the banks when they take 5-7 working days to return funds.Albeit that they said the funds leave their account immediately when the cancellation is enacted, this does not take into account the 1 week my funds were sitting in their account prior to cancellation. Multiply the interest on that by how ever many transactions do not get to completion and you have a lot of interest accruing (2 million properties is advertised).Worth considering (as some companies do) keeping the customers card details only yo secure the boking and then take funds after cancellation period has expired.However, I don't think this is part of the business plan.Regards, Barry.Booked and paid 1850€ for a camper van vacation in Tenerife. Money taken immediately.No confirmation or receipt email which I had to go chasing!Then camper owner won't reply so I get on Chat site (AI bot very frustrating) and eventually vented to agent.Agent says they will offer alternative which they did at nothing less than 3500€!!Cancelled booking then they tell me 5-7 working days for return. Absolutely outrageous and ordering on illegal I imagine (I'm gonna find out through my solicitor).Now I have no chance of a Xmas alternative booking in 5-7 days time and don't have the cash otherwise.Horrible shower of cowboys and I will be going legal for interest payment on my money which they will have held for over 7 days by the time I get it back (I have my doubts as to whether I will get it back)Absolute fly by nights...stay well clear folksIrish guy

name: MIchael Indelicato
title: Why would anyone host with VRBO?
text: Why would anyone host with VRBO? I just removed my listed because as others have said their customer service sucks. Their fee's are higher than other vendors, but the amount of bookings I get from them are far below their competitors.  If you are new to their platform they hold your money for at least 30 days, which is a scam because hosts have real costs to cover. Of course their competitors don't follow this horrible practice.  Not only won't I use them to host but after reading the other reviews I'd never book with them either. Glad to be free from their horrible business practices.

name: Bass Reeves
title: Consumer ALERT
text: Consumer ALERT.  There are no words to explain how I feel about VRBO and this homeowner. Betrayed! Scammed and Ripped Off!...are good starters. This stay should have cost us approximately $2500. *WHICH HAS NOT BEEN RETURNED TO ME. Last minute reservations at hotels cost me over $4000.  VRBO help center-Completely LAME and USELESS!  Their response-“NOT OUR PROBLEM! They used another software on our website for your booking-Good Luck getting your money back!” I WILL NEVER! Use VRBO again! name: Sara
title: Disgraceful customer service
text: After 3 previous positive experiences booking via Vrbo my latest booking now confirms why other reviews are so poor. Booked an apartment (Smartflats Midi) in Brussels for myself and children to experience the Christmas markets, wish I hadn’t! I was meant to receive check in details from the host 48 hours in advance, when these were not received and I was unable to contact the host I contacted customer service at Vrbo, initially the agent was understanding and apologetic but unable to do anything, my case was escalated to a manager who refused to refund my money so I could book elsewhere and advised I still had to travel to Brussels, arrive at night with 2 kids and hope by then I had received check in details… absolute disgrace! I won’t be booking via Vrbo again. I eventually got check in details 28 minutes before I was due to check in, however had the host done what they advised (sent them 48 hours before) or Vrbo been more understanding of the situation, they were unable to contact the host as number was unobtainable, I wouldn’t have spent the 24 hours prior to my trip stressing about where my children and I would be sleeping when we arrived in Brussels on our first night. My advice… avoid Vrbo

name: Iza

text: We are very dissatisfied and would not recommend with them as they confirmed the booking we then booked a flight but after half a hour they cancelled the booking and we are left with tickets as they don't have any properties in the time that we booked the flights for and they said the best they can do is to keep checking the apps to see if they have any to book for the dates that we booked for.

name: Shannon
title: Terrible experience

I expected they would have funded us a room for the night or at the very least found us one. Very stressed, tired and unhappy

name: john
title: vrbo sucks
text: 1. vrbo sent me a bill before i had booked.2. the listing was in US$. the bill was in euros.3. the bill shows “1 traveler”, which is correct, but the bill details include a charge for “extra guest”. i checked another listing to see whether vrbo would do the same thing. yep.4. i have to log in multiple times and get sent a code, even though im trying to navigate the same listing.5. i would have given up but for the fact that the host has been super responsive and pleasant.6. airbnb isnt saintly but by comparison vrbo sucks. this will be my first and last experience with vrbo.

name: Clearwater Beach Bunny
title: VRBO seems ripe for scams!
text: vrbo seems like it’s just a ripe platform for scams preying on travelers desperately searching for places reasonably priced! All the response replies in trustpilot from vrbo seem to just be “canned auto responses” not directly regarding the specific customer. I only have exp booking thru Airbnb so I guess I’m spoiled. Airbnb has host profiles listed w/ at the very least a first name. most of the time there’s a photo of & brief bio of the host. Airbnb has a Clear policy of VERIFYING host IDENTITIES & legitimacy BEFORE allowed to list a property. Reviews of Airbnb properties are easy to view & star ratings listed in the title of the listings. But when I searched VRBO I don’t see any reviews, or host profiles connected to the listings? everytime I try to contact a host thru the “contact host” button the app freezes? I finally logged into the desktop site. I found a listing & had questions about the property pre-book. ive sent 3 messages to host over the past 2 weeks & not heard back at all from host!!?!  I don’t feel confident the listing is legit or even a real host?  I also don’t like how vrbo doesn’t show a history of messages I’ve sent in the “messages” section of my account?!  This whole system is very shady. I called vrbo & spoke w/ a cust rep who was very difficult to understand? I wanted to find out if property was listed by a real host & if vrbo verified identity of hosts & legitimate properties? She first told me the host was a real human & the property was using the platform thru a partner site. Then she said the property owner didn’t have a profile bc he still needed to submit tax/financial paperwork to vrbo?  I asked how he was eligible to post a listing if the site hasn’t even verified their identity?  And why does the listing have the option to immediately “book now” if they didn’t have all the tax ppwk required to accept  money from travelers? Other listings have the option of “request to book” which is not immediate so why was this listing immediate booking? she then told me the host was fully verified which is why he could post & she kept giving me different answers about their identity verification process & what the policy was for renters to be protected from scams. She was just saying anything until I received an answer I liked?!  I’m basically just posting this review to warn other travelers about this site! It doesn’t appear they have systems & processes in place to protect travelers? Based on the reviews here I can see that’s true :(  my heart goes out to all the travelers who had a bad experiences. I just want to let ppl know there are “other platforms” you can to book thru, who are trustworthy & make it clear who the hosts are & verifiable identities.  And who make reviews clearly visible & Airbnb has actual host profiles. There’s no way to post a review about a property unless you’ve actually stayed there. That helps to avoid fake reviews.  I’ve had Amazing experiences w/ Airbnb every time , 10 bookings! I’ve also used booking.com & Expedia for vacation rentals (they list more than just hotels!) I’ve also used actual property management companies who specialize in vacation rentals.. you can do searches on google & just do research to verify they are legit. Vrbo doesn’t seem trustworthy or has reliable cust service. Please please be careful & do your homework if you book thru vrbo!!  And trust your instincts, if it doesn’t feel right!

name: Miami Vacation
title: As a host
text: As a host, renting to strangers can be intimidating. While most guests are great, occasionally you encounter a difficult person, and it can quickly turn into a nightmare, with no real support. The customer service experience is incredibly frustrating, you’re passed from one representative to another, with no resolution in sight. It feels like they don’t understand the issue, and each person gives you a different answer. In the end, it’s a complete waste of time, leaving you bitter because they profit from your efforts but don’t provide the protection you need when things go wrong.

name: Marie Smyth
title: Avoid VRBO
text: I booked a holiday cottage via Vrbo that wasn’t as advertised and I actually fell ill because of the condition of the property and subsequently had a bad fall in there due to poor maintenance. text: We booked a round-trip flight from Calgary to India through FlightHub for ourselves and our infant. Due to a visa issue, we couldn’t board the outbound flight on March 20, 2025. We resolved the issue and continued our trip a day later, assuming the return leg was still valid.On the day of our return from India, we were shocked to learn at the airport that our return tickets had been revoked. We were never informed by FlightHub or Air Canada. We reached out to FlightHub customer service via chat, who told us that “Air Canada took control of the tickets” — but failed to notify us that a new PNR had been created or that our return booking was cancelled.As a result, we were left stranded at the airport with a 9-month-old baby and had to purchase new tickets for $4,200 out of pocket, along with additional hotel costs.FlightHub has completely refused to take any responsibility, despite being our booking agent. They have no formal complaint process and offer no escalation route — only chat agents who pass the blame.We trusted FlightHub to manage our booking and communicate critical changes. That trust was misplaced. I strongly advise others to avoid using FlightHub for international or multi-leg trips. If anything goes wrong, you’re on your own.

name: N Redpath
title: I will never use ASAP Tickets again
text: I've used ASAP Tickets for several years for my groups, and used to have fairly good experiences. Last year the airlines canceled a flight for 9 people and it took me many phone calls and emails over more than a month to get a solution from Customer Service. The airlines couldn't help me because ASAP "owns" the ticket until it's used (upon check-in or departure, when the airlines takes over). That's one problem. The other is that their Customer Service is the worst I've ever experienced in many years, both personally and running a business. I was never able to speak to a supervisor or manager. I've asked countless times by email and my request was just ignored. When I finally got someone on the phone, three different agents said there are no managers available to speak to by phone, nor can the CS agents ask for a manager's assistance.Now this year is much worse. I nearly went elsewhere, but was contacted by one of the sales agents who promised her honesty, reliability, and support throughout the process and our travel. She said she COULD contact her manager to intervene if necessary. I believed her, and could almost always understand her accent, so we started booking with her. I got my ticket first, and the other members of the group (10 at that time) would quickly book through this agent to ensure they got my exact itinerary (but could pay with their own credit card). Well, she wasn't available when she said she would be, and the passengers started panicking after a day and a half. So I called the main phone line and asked for another agent who could help. The one who answered promised all the same things - he said he would personally take excellent care of our group. I provided my tickets to use as a template, but he booked the wrong flight for 5 other people! The others in the group trusted him - and me - to book the correct tickets, but they were frazzled by the long online payment process and in their confusion all five of them accepted the online itinerary. ASAP is disavowing all responsibility, and I felt obligated to fix this for my friends, at a cost of $2680+, which I couldn't afford. To make matters even worse, instead of booking a new single flight for the one leg that was incorrect, the agent charged us a change fee AND the cost of another flight. If he had been helpful or competent, he would have suggested the $150 fix (per person) rather than $447 per person!Now I've found that there's a new wrinkle - we are double-booked, because this agent said to "just ignore" the incorrect leg of the round-trip ticket and use the new one-way ticket. I've only just learned that if the airlines sees that you have two flights, they will cancel BOTH and you'll be stranded.I haven't even brought up the fact that one woman was just diagnosed with cancer and she and her husband had to cancel. She also is battling the ticket cost for her insurance claim (which she shouldn't have to do at a time like this). The agent had promised that the ASAP travel protection was FREE as part of a promotion, so she should accept their protection to get a better ticket price. But when she needed to get an invoice from ASAP for her claim, ASAP deducted the price of the insurance, and claims that her ticket cost much less than she actually paid. So she is screwed.When repeatedly contacting CS with an issue, they claim to investigate, then come back with a statement that when reviewing the phone conversation logs they found that the agent did nothing wrong. I have asked for an audio clip, but get no response. Today I've been on hold for more than an hour today, and my calls keep getting dropped.It appears that many agents at ASAP are not only incompetent, but also dishonest. It must be the pay structure. They probably get paid on commission and get extra when they "sell up" with travel protection products. , and I will never, ever, use ASAP Tickets again.Please reconsider before using ASAP, especially for expensive international flights.

title: Pathetic Experience
text: I had a deeply frustrating and disappointing experience with Priceline that disrupted a major life event and left me stranded with my family in the middle of the night.I booked a prepaid, non-refundable car rental through Priceline (Confirmation #: 780-975-535-16) for pickup at Atlanta Airport on May 3rd at 1:00 AM, ahead of my graduation from Georgia Tech. I was traveling with my wife and two kids and needed to be at the ceremony early in the morning.Despite having a confirmed reservation, no car was available upon arrival. I contacted Priceline support, and they assured me the reservation would be canceled, that a refund would be issued, and that expenses for Lyft/Uber and the inconvenience would be reimbursed. We were stranded at the airport and had to book a hotel and use Lyft—all at my own expense.After waiting 36 hours, I returned to the airport and booked a new reservation, but the rental company mistakenly applied the pickup to the original reservation. Priceline then denied the refund, claiming the original reservation was used, even though I had no vehicle for 36 hours.To make matters worse, Priceline has refused to issue a meaningful refund, despite the fact that I had no car for a significant portion of the reservation. Every time I call, I'm told that the best they can offer is a 10% coupon for a future booking which is completely unacceptable given the circumstances. This doesn’t even begin to address the inconvenience, added expenses, or the disruption caused on a milestone day for my family.This was not my fault, yet I’ve been left with the burden of extra costs, lost time, and poor service—with no accountability from Priceline. The handling of this situation was misleading, inconsistent, and completely unfair. I expected better from a major travel service.I do not recommend using Priceline for car rentals—if anything goes wrong, you're on your own.

title: I used Priceline to get a refund from Air France
text: I used Priceline to purchase a ticket on Air France from Morocco to Columbia round trip.  Air France denied boarding due to an unstated policy requiring a transit visa for Moroccan citizens passing through DeGaulle airport to a 3rd country.  The french government doesn't require a transit visa in this circumstance.  Air France refused to deal with the issue and referred me back to Priceline.  I contacted Priceline to discuss a full refund.  The agent was great!  She was knowledgeable and courteous.  She told me that Priceline would request a refund from AIr France and to call them back in 10 days.  I did so and spoke with Daphne, a supervisor at Priceline.  While she didn't have the answer yet, she stated she would contact Air France to authorize the refund. She asked for my phone number to return the call.  I received a call back from Daphne at Priceline within a few hours with the very good news that a full refund would be issued.  She stated it would be 7-10 business days for it to be received in my account.  I received the full amount of the refund yesterday (about 5 days)!  Kudos to Priceline and its staff for their service...I really appreciate it!

title: Priceline Took My Money with No Confirmation and No Way to Cancel
text: recently reserved a hotel for my son’s soccer tournament and was explicitly shown that I could cancel until July 30. Since we hadn’t received the tournament schedule yet, I wasn’t sure we would need the first night, so the cancellation policy was important. While booking, the website froze and refreshed, saying the reservation time was no longer available. Despite this, my bank was charged, and the hotel confirmed a reservation existed.However, I received no confirmation email or booking number, and the hotel confirmed that no email was tied to the reservation, meaning I had no way to manage or cancel the booking. Because it was booked through Priceline and I had no reservation number, the hotel couldn’t help me further.To make matters worse, Priceline has no way to look up a reservation without a booking number, and their automated phone system kept hanging up on me. When I finally reached a real person, they told me the reservation was nonrefundable unless I could provide a screenshot of the cancellation policy shown before booking, which, of course, I don’t have.They’re now charging me the full amount (nearly $900) whether or not I stay, even though the site showed a free cancellation window when I booked.Priceline’s system is broken and sets customers up to fail. There is zero accountability when something goes wrong. Don’t risk booking through them, especially for time-sensitive or expensive travel. I’ll be warning others on every forum and everywhere I can.
