title: BIG SCAM! NEVER AGAIN!!
text: I booked a rental car on Priceline.com. The name of the car rental agency they assigned me was AMERICA CAR RENTAL on 5124 W Cypress St, Tampa. Fl 33607, (also known as) SONIC ENTERPRISES LLC (aka) CAR RENTAL CONSOLIDATED.  Priceline charged me $108.00 for 6 days for a mid-sized car which I thought was a great deal.  I arrive at Tampa Intl Airport and I had to take an elevator to the ground level, go outside and call AMERICA CAR RENTAL  to send a shuttle to pick me up and take me to their rental agency.  I get there and I am like 3rd in line.  I hear the woman at the counter complaining because they did not take her auto insurance which required her to purchase THEIR insurance. Then the guy in front of me was yelling and complaining because they wanted to charge him an extra $500.00 for auto insurance. He walked out.  I said to myself, "what am I in for?"  Sure enough I get to the counter after waiting in line for at least an hour only to be told they don't accept my auto insurance (Amica),  plus I had to pay a $500.00 security deposit, plus I had to purchase the toll package. They said if I refused the toll package then they had to charge me an extra $25.00 for not purchasing it.  What started as $108.00 for 6 days ended up to be a $294.00 bill.  After at least an hour and a half later I finally was able to get my rental car.  The only good thing I can say is although the car had a huge dent , I liked the ride and had no problems with the car.  Also the drop-off experience was seamless.   I received a survey from AMERICA CAR RENTAL. The survey had no link to click on and some words in the survey were misspelled.  Something else to note is  there are multiple companies in this agency.  My advice is to contact your car rental agency to make sure they take your insurance and there are no other hidden fees.  Very unprofessional.  Next time I will rent my car directly through Enterprise or another reputable company.  I will never go through Priceline again or rent a car through Sonic or America Car Rental.

title: Warning to Priceline Users – This is a SCAM and Priceline is Enabling It
text: I rented a car through Priceline in April 2025, opting to use my own insurance coverage as I always do. The pickup was at Economy Car Rental, 3356 Elmbank Rd, Mississauga, ON L4V 1A6 — and the experience was an absolute nightmare from start to finish.First, the counter associate was extremely unprofessional and dismissive. Then they hit me with a mysterious, bogus fee, claiming it’s mandatory even when using your own insurance. It’s not an insurance fee — it’s just a money grab. When I asked, they told me “Priceline should’ve disclosed it.” But I read through the entire Priceline itinerary and disclosure — and there is ZERO mention of this ridiculous charge.I spent over two weeks and more than $100 on my cell phone bill trying to get someone at Priceline to help. I called multiple times, spoke to multiple agents, even asked to speak to a manager. I begged them to at least issue a letter so I could dispute the charge with my credit card company — and they refused. I was left stranded with no support, no resolution, and no accountability.I urge Priceline to start vetting the companies you promote. A quick glance at the reviews for Economy Car Rental at that location shows over 100 one-star reviews — filled with frustrated, disgusted, and scammed customers just like me. This company uses bait-and-switch tactics, lures customers in with low prices, and then slaps on fraudulent fees at pickup, knowing you have no other choice.The fact that Priceline continues to list them despite this mountain of negative feedback tells me everything I need to know: Priceline doesn’t care about its customers. If this is how you operate — by giving shady businesses a platform — then I will never be using Priceline again, and I’ll be warning everyone I know to do the same.Shame on Economy Car Rental for running a scam, and shame on Priceline for turning a blind eye.

text: Dear Priceline Customer Service,As a Priceline VIP and long-time Expedia Elite member, I never imagined I would be compelled to write a letter of such deep dissatisfaction. But after what I endured during my February 14–17 car rental reservation (Trip #741-208-965-16, Confirmation: NUPES7), I feel obligated to not only express my outrage but also warn future customers of this vendor and the shortcomings of your platform.Let me be absolutely clear: I was treated with utter disregard by your rental partner, Flexway. And despite raising this issue promptly—on February 14 and 15—I am still waiting, over three months later (as of April 30), for any meaningful resolution or accountability from Priceline. If this is how your VIP customers are treated, I can only imagine what everyday users go through.Here’s what happened:Attempted Cancellation at Pickup:Upon arrival at the rental location, Flexway tried to cancel my reservation without explanation. No professionalism. No courtesy. Just confusion, stress, and delay. Only after protracted discussions was I begrudgingly handed a vehicle—not the one I booked, and certainly not one that met my needs.Filthy, Unsafe, and Unsuitable Vehicle:The car was in unacceptable condition—dirty, unkempt, and potentially unsafe due to worn tire tread. I had to take the vehicle to a car wash immediately, costing me time, money, and the start of my important trip.I am attaching:A car wash receiptVideos and photos of the car before and after, found here: Photo/Video EvidenceFalse Advertising and Mismatch of Booking Details:I reserved a 7-seater suitable for transporting VIP guests—what I received was not fit for purpose. The back row was cramped and inappropriate for adults, forcing my guests to arrange alternate transportation. The embarrassment this caused during a first meeting with investors is beyond words.Mileage Restrictions on an “Unlimited Mileage” Rental:The car came with a 200 km/day limit—completely unacceptable given I explicitly selected a vehicle with unlimited mileage. This felt like a bait-and-switch tactic that misrepresents what Priceline advertises.Refused Early Return Credit:I returned the car the same night—less than 6 hours after pickup. The Flexway staff acknowledged the return but refused to process it, insisting on billing the full 4-day rental until February 17. This means I paid for a vehicle that was unused and sitting outside their office. It’s exploitative, and frankly, dishonest.Why This Review MattersThis was not just a bad experience—it was a breach of trust. Priceline, by enabling vendors like Flexway who misrepresent services, treat customers poorly, and ignore accountability, you're complicit in damaging your own brand and user trust. If your team doesn't act on repeated customer complaints, then your VIP program means absolutely nothing.Let me be perfectly clear: I will never use Priceline again. And I strongly advise others—especially professionals and international travelers—to think twice before trusting your platform. This experience was humiliating, inconvenient, and completely preventable.I am requesting a full refund for this trip and a formal response addressing why this case has remained unresolved since February. I expect this to be escalated to senior customer service management

title: False Promises, No Accountability – Regret Using Way.com
text: I used Way.com to reserve a parking spot in San Francisco, hoping to avoid the stress of finding parking in a busy city. I booked and paid in full in advance, got my confirmation, and even contacted customer support before my trip to confirm everything. They reassured me the reservation was valid and that there were no in-and-out privileges.But when I arrived at the location on the day of my reservation, the lot was chained shut. No access, no attendant, no signage, nothing. I waited for a while, tried to see if anyone was around, and then finally contacted Way.com support. After a long wait on the call, their representative confirmed there was an issue with the lot and that they could not provide parking at that time. I was told to go find parking elsewhere—no assistance, no alternative arrangements, nothing.Stranded in the middle of a busy SF street, I had no choice but to use my hotel’s valet service, which was significantly more expensive. I thought at the very least the refund would be straightforward, given that Way.com could not deliver the service I paid for.But instead, what followed was an endless, frustrating back-and-forth with their support team. I provided:A photo of the chained-up lotA transaction charge from the hotelScreenshots of the call log showing my attempts to contact them while I was at the lotThey still denied the refund, saying it wasn’t enough and that I needed to provide check-in and check-out times from the alternate parking (which obviously I didn't bothered to through hotel valet). Even worse, they tried to spin the situation as a “courtesy cancellation” and offered Way Bucks instead of refunding the actual amount to my card.Let me be clear: this was not a cancellation on my part. Way.com failed to provide the paid service, admitted it during a recorded call, and still tried to shift the responsibility onto me. The dismissive tone and refusal to take accountability made the experience even worse.At this point, I’ve lost money, time, and patience—and I’ve made it clear I will never use Way.com again. What should have been a smooth part of my travel turned into an unnecessary ordeal.If you value your time, money, and peace of mind, think twice before trusting Way.com with your plans.

title: Very untrustworthy business that suppresses negative reviews and ignores customer complaints
text: I will never use Way again.  I've used them several times previously with overnight parking lot reservations and such and had no issues.  But the one time I had an issue, they were completely unhelpful.  I don't blame them necessarily for the bad experience at their contracted parking lot company, but I very much blame them for (1) being completely unable and/or unwilling to remedy the issue (a non-running pickup shuttle) and (2) suppression of negative reviews on their site.After my poor experience with one of the parking garages advertised on their site (Express LAX Long Term Airport Parking) I still pinned most of the blame on the parking garage and not Way, despite Way offering nothing in the way of real assistance.  That said, I was confused as to how a garage with a sterling 4.6/5 rating from nearly 600 ratings and 60 reviews somehow left me and those waiting on a shuttle with me with the completely opposite experience.  I thought maybe we were just very unlucky considering no one in the reviews made mention of the shuttle or non-responsive staff being a problem.  Even if my situation was a weird, poorly timed one-off, I felt that other travelers should be made aware and attempted to leave a negative review of the parking garage on the Way.com site.  The post was pending review and I got a bit suspicious.  Sure enough, the review didn't post after a few days.  I thought, well maybe technical difficulties...and tried again a couple of times to leave the same review.  Again, the review never posted.  So then I checked Google, and as I begin to suspect, the parking garage had a very subpar rating (2.3/5) with many recent reports of the same exact experience that I had.  It became obvious to me that Way was intentionally suppressing negative reviews (and perhaps even adding fake positive reviews).  I have no other potential explanations of the disparity between the positive reviews on the partner site and the many negative reviews on the independent site.What is really unfortunate about this violation of business-consumer trust is that in my opinion it is unnecessary--there are *many* other parking garages in the area on their platform.  If one garage had a poor rating, I would simply take my business to a different facility on the same platform.  This breech of trust and violation of what I consider to be good business ethics is unforgivable and I will never use the site again, and I will discourage anyone that I know from utilizing the service as well.

text: I have been using globalairportparking.com for many years as I travel (fly) nearly every week. They never showed up after quite some time... upon call back, the hotel employee said that they thought we were an airplane crew, so the shuttle van never showed up.  They said we could wait 45 minutes or call an Uber.  So 30.00 and an Uber drive later, finally got into our car on the hotel property.Upon calling GlobalAirportParking's phone number to tell them about this incident, they initially said that they would "investigate," and then said that they have to call the hotel to verify and go through a process.  I learned that they did call the hotel, but the employee that made the error already left for the day and they asked us for the name of the person we spoke to that made the error.  Are you kidding me?  How would I know or remember that for a shuttle ride?  Why would I ask this person's name during the phone call and why would it matter?  Now I know better.I had to send a string of emails and go back and forth to finally receive notification that they would reimburse us only 25% of our total cost of parking, which was only 17.87, which was whopping $4.27!  We were out the 17.87 AND the 30.00 for the Uber... when I told them that wasn't fair, they offered 15.00 in "Way Bucks" which is basically credit toward a future parking reservation.It's not the money, it's the principle of it of course! So I'd like to share this bad review to the public to make sure you get the person's name who made the mistake, write multiple emails and phone calls to this company (over 2 hours into this so far) to only gain more frustration and grief.Tessa was the customer service person who I dealt with via numerous emails, but maybe she is not allowed to refund money, but nonetheless, they could have done a much better job.Buyer Beware... normally good, but not this time!

name: Robert
title: Fraudulent Change Fee When Airline Changes Schedule
text: JetBlue changed the flight schedule for our departure flight from Jacksonville to New York to meet our international connection.  JetBlue and Royal Air Maroc both notified me of the change directly and did not mention a need to re-issue the ticket.  I received an e-mail from AirTkt.com asking me to confirm the time change for the flight, to which I responded.  AirTkt then charged me $25 per ticket to "reissue" the confirmed tickets. The ticket was issued as a through ticket on Royal Air Maroc ticket stock, and JetBlue was perfectly prepared to honor the original ticket without re-issue.  In other words, AirTkt baited me into authorizing an unnecessary re-issue with their e-mail stating that "If you will not reply to the email you may miss your flight."  The email did not mention a fee involved with confirming that I was aware that the airline had changed the flight time.   Finally, AirTkt completed the fraud by claiming that they needed to re-issue the tickets, but no actual re-issue was done.  The ticket numbers remain exactly the same as when first issued in December.  So, AirTkt charged me for something that not only was not "required", but no service was actually provided for the payment extracted.  UPDATE:  AirTkt kept responding to my e-mail with boilerplate pablum about their policies and nonsense word salads.  This morning  I was informed that they would be "making an exception" and refunding my $50.  So, to prospective buyers, I say that you can, in fact, get a good deal on business class tickets from AirTkt, but remember that you are dealing with a consolidator, not a regular travel agency.  Read and understand what you are buying.  Buy separate travel insurance from a third party to cover the price of your non-refundable, non-changeable tickets in the event of an emergency cancellation.  Realize that until you check in for your flight the airline can do nothing with your ticket, except maybe give you seat assignments.  After you check in, the reverse is true.  AirTkt is completely out of the picture.  BUT, as this episode has demonstrated, AirTkt is a sleazy outfit that will try to game you for unearned fees on the back end.  There are other reliable consolidators out there:  Buy from one of them.  If you buy a ticket from AirTkt, my advice is to follow up on the airline's web site to ensure that the airline has the reservation and then never communicate with AirTkt again about that reservation.  Caveat Emptor, and travel on.

name: Deepak Seth
title: Misleading Pricing and Poor Customer Support – Disappointed
text: I booked through SmartFares for the first time after finding it via Google. The fare was shown in euros (€580), and there was no mention that the charge would be processed in US dollars. After payment, I received an email showing a $688 charge—higher than expected due to currency conversion. I accepted it reluctantly but was already concerned by the lack of pricing transparency. Later I noted €623 was already reserved on my credit card for this booking.The next issue was even more frustrating: I was told the booking wasn’t confirmed yet, only reserved, and I’d get confirmation later. If nothing came within 48 hours, I was advised to call a number—which turned out to be unresponsive. Other numbers didn’t work either. The email address on their site bounced back. Only the US-based number connected, where I was told to wait until the office opened. I also sent out a message via chatbot. Finally I reached a representative who told me the booking had failed due to one flight segment being unconfirmed. He offered a confirmation if I would pay another $20 and informed that he has already discounted the higher price by applying a coupon.At that point, I requested a cancellation which was done in the system while I received a message to urgently call back due to an issue with my booking. Finally spoke to someone very responsible, who confirmed the cancellation, assured me a refund would be issued, and emailed the confirmation.While one or two agents were helpful, the overall experience was poor—misleading pricing, broken contact details, and delayed or missing communication. It took a lot of effort to get basic support. I was left feeling misled and frustrated, and I won’t be using SmartFares again.

text: I am facing a medical emergency and have obtained a letter from my doctor stating that I am unfit to fly. When I contacted British Airways (BA), they informed me that they could assist in changing my flight if I provided the unfit-to-fly letter, as my booking was made through SmartFares. BA confirmed that once they received this document, they would remove my flight from the system, allowing me to rebook at a later date.However, when I contacted SmartFares, I encountered shocking and unprofessional treatment. Despite explaining my situation and providing the necessary documentation, I was told that they could not remove my flight from the system. Instead, I was informed that if I did not provide a new flight date immediately, the flight would be marked as a no-show, leaving me liable to pay additional fees.I explained that I could not afford to pay for a new flight at this time due to the costs I have already incurred for medical care. Despite this, I was pressured to provide a new travel date, even after explaining that my medical treatment was ongoing and I could not determine when I would be fit to fly. When I submitted the required documentation, including a handwritten letter from the attending doctor in Jamaica, I was accused of fraud. The agent dismissed my valid documents, spoke over me, accused me of lying, and suggested I was attempting to deceive them and stated that I was commiting fraud.To make matters worse, I was given three unacceptable options: pay £700 to change the flight, risk flying despite the potential threat to my life due to a blood clot, or cancel the flight entirely and purchase a new ticket. I even provided SmartFares with the direct contact information for British Airways so they could verify the airline’s willingness to amend the booking without charge. Despite this, SmartFares refused to contact BA or offer any assistance.The treatment I received was appalling. The representative, who identified himself as Jim, was rude, dismissive, and unhelpful to the point that I felt compelled to record the conversation. At one point, he stated that unless there was a death, they would not assist me. This experience has left me extremely distressed during an already challenging time, and if I could give a rating of -5 stars, I would.

name: Bruce Richardson
title: Predatory 3rd party Priceline.com service
text: The 3rd party service, GuestReservations.com I am told by an IHG hotel is owned by priceline.com.  This said, Priceline.com customer service has no record of reservations made on this site.  The site's predatory practices should have you blocking guest reservations.com along with priceline.com sites because as the following example will show, they are clearly a sleazy and predatory organization.  Now let me explain why.  After using them twice, I made a 3rd reservation in 3 weeks on guestreservations.com that needed adjusting.  The hotel told me that they were locked out of the reservation and that any changes had to be done by the third party. I waited for over 1.5 hours on hold with guestreservations.com, listening to the most annoying music loop followed by a repeating message telling me that my call would be answered in the order that it was received.  I finally hung up, understanding that they were never going to answer the call. The hotel advised that since they were locked out they had no choice but to recreate the reservation and that I would need to get hold of guestreservations.com at some point soon to cancel the incorrect upcoming reservation flat.  They advise that upon receiving my request that the 3rd party should contact the hotel to verify and then should process the cancellation flat.  I finally got a hold of the website's customer disservice dept the following day, speaking to somebody clearly located in India.  She advised that their policies allowed no option other than to process a cancellation retaining roughly 80% of what was paid.  She was immovable on this subject, continuously repeating the position.  I then explained what my policy would be... To never use their service again and to educate others in advance to avoid being taken advantage of in a similar fashion.  She didn't care.  I told her to feel free to diary my information and check back in one month, 6 months and a year to confirm what their lack of customer service has cost them.    Ironically, I found their pricing is also higher than what I have been offered by the hotel the last few times that I have compared rates for curiosity's sake.  Anyone that chooses to still use them, has been warned and does so at their own peril. I hope this helps save others from being taken advantage of in a similar way.  Best of luck!

It comes in. on a $500 hotel bill for 2 nights, they charge $200 in "fees". This is above and beyond the hotel taxes and fees.Obviously, by not sending a confirmation email, they do not alert the customer that they have mistakenly booked through their website-which is their intention.This is completely fraudulent practice.I wish I could feel bad about being scammed, but there were no signs. I arrived at hotel and as previously advised would happen I was asked for credit card, I thought this was for incidentals although the charge was high but I thought it would be reversed on check out. On check out the hotel charged the full amount for the stay, I still thought the transaction would be reversed. After I left the hotel I realised that there was no reversal of the charge.  I contacted Ritz Carlton who said the booking had not been prepaid.   After some considerable difficulty I managed to contact guestreservations.com who "handed" off my complaint to Priceline.   A check on line shows that my booking was made through the guestreservations.com, fulfilled by getaroom.com, confirmed by hotelvalues.com and my complaint is now being managed by pps.priceline.com.  I am currently out of pocket by UK £930 for a booking which I paid at the hotel despite having already paid this organisation  believing it was at very least acting for and on behalf of Ritz Carlton when taking the booking. Priceline have twice asked for proof I made the payment at the hotel which I have provided and now have passed on my complaint to "escalations"at Priceline but there has been no response.  I have contacted "legal!" at Guestreservations but they have not replied either.   I want my money back it should be a simple operation for whomever made the hotel reservation to confirm they did not pay for the reservation and to refund my money to me.   There is another issue in that the original charge included an element of "taxes", if guestreservations has not paid the funds to the hotel then they have not made the necessary tax submission so they must be in breach of tax laws and regulation.

name: Emily Franklin
title: I made an IHG hotel reservation through…
text: I made an IHG hotel reservation through a third party who call themselves “Guest Reservations” for dates 6/26 - 6/30. When I booked, I chose the ‘pre-pay’ option because it was slightly lower cost. I did not realize, nor did they make it clear until after booking, that it was 'nonrefundable'. Additionally, Guest Reservations clearly intend to deceive customers by appearing to be the hotel website, which is what I thought when I booked.Fast forward a couple months and my travel plans changed. The email confirmation said to call x number if I need to make any modifications. But when I called and explained that I will only be staying for two nights instead of the original four, they told me that they cannot make any modifications and that my only option was to cancel my reservation WITHOUT a refund, and then rebook with the correct dates. What?? They told me there was nothing else they could do for me, and that I’d have to reach out to the hotel to change my reservation and to get a refund because Guest reservations had “already sent the money to the hotel” - that is a QUOTE from the person I spoke to.I called IHG, and the person I spoke to was was able to resolve the issue, so I thought at first, by calling Guest Reservations and asking them to cancel my original reservation and refund me the full amount. They agreed to do this (according to the IHG person I was speaking to). IHG rebooked me for the correct dates. in the meantime, 6/28–6/30.The issue is that Guest Reservations never actually cancelled my original reservation, nor did they refund me the $1600+ that was promised. When I called IHG they told me Guest Reservations is the only one who can refund me the money. So Guest Reservations lied to me, saying the hotel would have to refund me. Then they lied to IHG, saying they would cancel and refund me.This is a terrible business model and they make their money by deceiving customers, and then lying to them when any changes are needed.

text: This is a classic scam of a company.if you see them - run away!Otherwise you risk of paying 50-100% more than what you saw on the reservation page for your accommodation.It is a absolutely astonishing that no consumer protection agency is dealing with these scammers.They trick you with the deign of a page to make you believe you are at the hotel’s own reservation page - beware you’re not!You see price per night - that looks reasonable or attractive and you never see the total sum to be charged or those junk fees they add up before you click the pay button - once you click pay - all of a sudden you realize that you’ve been charged a total sum that is significantly more than the price per night that you saw on the reservation page.Upon booking, I did not receive the booking number or invoice - all of this is designed so that it makes it difficult for you to realize what has happened and why were you charged so much.When you try to call them - it is difficult to bypass the automated messaging system - but once you manage to speak with the real person - they put you on hold, pretending to be “checking your reservation” and keep you on hold for more than 30min - they do that deliberately so that you just give up.I spent an hour on the phone from two attempts with their “customer service” - they just repeat the same script - and the operators there know they are working for a company that tricks people paying junk fees on top of actual hotel room cost.Look it up on YouTube and google - massive number of people complaining about how they operate.From outside looks like a legit company - but it’s all to trick you - don’t fall for it.Remember - NEVER EVER book with them!

text: On the 18th of November, 2024 I googled "High Wycombe Hilton" and clicked on one of the first results expecting it to be the official Hilton site, I reserved a room for the 18th of December to 27th of December, 2024. A few minutes after booking after I got the booking confirmation (booking number 98171798 and getaroom booking R5277865375) I called on their helpline to try and cancel. They told me that the booking was non-refundable and cannot be changed or canceled, I informed them that I had looked and can see the exact same room listed on the hilton official site at not only a lower rate, but also 100% refundable if canceled before December 12th. The customer support rep suggested that I make another booking for the refundable room and they would try and talk to their Hilton rep (Tobais I believe) and if Hilton approves, they would cancel my original booking and I could keep the cheaper and refundable one, If Hilton doesn't agree to a cancelation, I could cancel the fully refundable one. They asked for my credit card information again and booked another room (Booking #93218550 and getaroom booking R5277913129).. The very next morning I got a notification from my credit card app that my card was charged $2500 for a Nikon camera and I had to reach out to Nikon to have that reversed. On further correspondence with their support I was repeatedly told that my original booking which was non-refundable was canceled and since it was non-refundable, I had to forfeit the amount and only had the newer booking (93218550) active so I had no option. I reached out to hilton support and was informed that both bookings were active and I managed to get the newer booking canceled, however, Hilton informed me that since this was booked from a 3rd party, they will not be able to issue a refund. I filed a dispute with my credit card company and the next day got an email from priceline (getaroom) stating that a refund has been issued (I am yet to see the refund hit my account)After more than 3 months of fighting and trying to get a refund I had to file a dispute with my credit card company - The company has still not issued me a refund, but given all the evidence I shared with my credit card company, they issued me a creditthis is a horrible company - BEWARE

title: SCAM/FRAUD - Avoid!!! Settled with FTC in 2017 for fraud and has not stopped
text: Made a reservation for 4 nights in a London  hotel costing a total of 1572. The site added unexplained additional charges of 1150. Making the total bill over 2700. A cancellation fee of 1900 was added to this. None of these charges were explained prior to paying with the credit card - see below for similar experiences. Buyer beware. Expensive mistake!The site appears first on the search engines and looks like the hotel webpage - do check that it is in fact the hotel's website where you are booking.Upon further investigation I called the hotel and they told me that the booking have been done through Booking.com! Not even directly with the hotel.Whilst the hotel and Booking.com were willing to provide a full refund on the booking, Guest Reservations would only allow the refund if I paid the 1,900 cancellation fee. In other words they would take 1,900 from me even though they would not be out of pocket! This of course was not an option as I would still have to pay for the hotel on top of the cancellation fee. Whilst the hotel and Booking.com tried to do the right thing, GUESTRESERVATIONS.COM will ensure that there is no escape.Don’t be fooled, called 6 times to have the issue resolved to no avail.The site has responded below and provided their customer 'care' email address supposedly to try to resolve the issue. Let's see if they actually do the right thing...For the time being AVOID like the plague.Checked the site for fraud and lo and behold they have had to settle with the FTC in 2017 - I wish I had checked sooner. I hope this review helps others to avoid my faith. I may have lost my money but I don't want others to unwittingly fall into the same trap.

text: DO NOT BOOK THROUGH THIS COMPANY! I was charged $639 for a reservation for one night at the Madison Beach Hotel - a Hilton property in Connecticut. text: After the distressing experience below, I contacted the customer care team as instructed and they have issued a refund.I wish i didn't have to jump through so many hoops to get there though, this should have been sorted when i contacted them over the phone.Still kudos for actually listening and getting it sorted in the end.=======================================ALWAYS DOUBLE CHECK THE WEBSITE YOU'RE USING TO BOOK TRAVEL/HOTELS EVEN IF IT LOOKS LEGITIMATE!These guys are true con artists in a digital age.Booking #R5416273985I am UK based and I booked a hotel in Munich using what i thought was the hotels website directly - I quickly realised i had booked the wrong room/dates as soon as i pressed 'OK' - so almost immediately got in contact with the hotel to say i had made a mistake and to cancel the booking so I could re-book - it was then the hotel told me the reservation was done via a booking agency and I needed to contact them... I checked my confirmation email and only then realised I had used a company named 'guest reservations' and that the cost was significantly more than I thought I had paid thanks to the now infamous "Tax Recovery Charges & Service Fees" that had been added at some point- these fees were the same cost as a night in the hotel room!!!This company is based in the USA and i called them (costing me who knows much in phone charges) and explained that I had just booked the wrong date and needed to cancel so I could re-book - the lady on the phone was somehwat sympathetic but told me in no uncertain terms that I could not get a full refund, the hotel had no power to cancel it on my behalf either, and if I were to cancel the booking this would cost me 90% of what I had paid (£600!) - absolutley scandalous.I feel like such an idiot for falling for their underhanded tactic of disguising their website and search results to look like the legitimate hotel one and for missing the 'hidden fees' but it's at least somewhat comforting to see i'm not the only one who's been duped.Have now had to raise a dispute with my credit card provider to try and recover costs, insane.as another reviewer has stated; Under the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 (CPRs), businesses in the UK are required to provide transparent pricing information. Failing to disclose significant fees until after a customer has entered their payment details may constitute a misleading commercial practice. Furthermore, this lack of transparency contravenes the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which requires that terms and conditions, including pricing, be fair and clearly presented to consumers before a transaction is completed.This "business" certainly fails almost all of that criteria.what a distressing situation. Avoid these charlatans like the plague.

name: Hannah
title: Beware of fees when paying
text: Beware fees are not clearly identified when entering credit card. This site shows hotel rate but hides the tax recovery charges and services fee - I initially booked a two-room stay for a total rate of £298, only to discover after entering my payment details that an additional £174 in taxes and service fees had been applied. This was not clearly communicated on your website during the booking process.Under the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 (CPRs), businesses in the UK are required to provide transparent pricing information. Failing to disclose significant fees until after a customer has entered their payment details may constitute a misleading commercial practice. Furthermore, this lack of transparency contravenes the Consumer Rights Act 2015, which requires that terms and conditions, including pricing, be fair and clearly presented to consumers before a transaction is completed.This situation has caused me significant distress, both emotionally and financially. A surcharge of £174, representing a 58% increase on the original booking amount, is excessive and unreasonable. Had I been aware of these additional costs upfront, I would not have proceeded with the booking.I kindly request the following actions:1.	A full refund of the £174 in hidden fees.2.	A detailed explanation of why these charges were not transparently disclosed during the booking process.3.	Assurance that your pricing practices will be reviewed to prevent this issue from affecting other customers in the future.Please treat this as a formal complaint under your complaints procedure. I expect a response within 14 days. Should this matter remain unresolved, I may escalate it to the relevant consumer protection authorities or pursue other appropriate actions.Update - customer care team responded and as gesture refunded fees which was good but definitely need clearer labelling of fees.

text: I have been exploring options to ship golf clubs as well as other specific luggage and came across Shipsticks.  I decided to try Shipsticks for the first time in May and it proved to be a great experience overall.First the website and app.  I did prefer the app over the website for a variety of reasons - most significantly the workflow in the app is more intuitive than the website.Second the service.  I checked multiple vendors for shipping, including UPS and FedEx and the cost for 3+ day ground service was cheaper through ShipSticks.  I traveled from the east cost to the mid-west and was surprised at the difference in price for ground services.I also chose to add insurance and those rates were very similar to other insurance rates.Once I printed my shipping labels and attached to my golf shipping bag, Fedex picked them up and delivered to my destination well within the delivery window provided.  Same experience for my return trip two weeks later.  I will also note that  my shipping bag was delivered in covered locations at both destination and return locations.The convenience factor was worth the extra expense to that of checking in my clubs in at an airport and transporting at my destination location.Providing the cost remains optimal with Shipsticks for this service, I will be using again in October.

The next day there was a different pool concierge, and she was very attentive to our needs. Cesar, the pool bartender, was beyond fabulous!  He always made my mango margaritas quickly and super delicious! We absolutely loved our butlers - they always greeted us when we went out to the elevators, and they managed to obtain dinner reservations for us every night when the application said there were no tables available - we loved that!  We were so sad to leave paradise, but we will definitely be back next year!!

But what happened? Zero response from the Headout team. No one picked up, no chat support, no assistance whatsoever.As if that wasn’t enough, my second booking for KL Tower Sky Terrace was also a disaster. It rained in the evening, and visitors were not allowed on the Sky Terrace for safety reasons. Again, the KL Tower official politely asked me to speak to the agent to amend the ticket for the indoor Observatory deck. And again — no response from Headout.Both bookings were ruined, my money and time wasted, and the entire experience soured — all because Headout’s team is unreachable, unaccountable, and completely unprofessional.Avoid Headout at all costs if you value your time, money, and travel plans.They’re happy to take your money but disappear when there’s a problem.

text: Visiting teamLab Phenomena Abu Dhabi was like going into a living, breathing artwork. The installations responded to my presence—lights shifted, sounds echoed, and spaces transformed as I moved through them. In one room, a massive black sphere floated mid-air, gently drifting when touched before returning to its original position. Another space featured glowing orbs that lit up and chimed upon contact, creating a symphony of light and sound.The architecture itself felt organic, with flowing forms that blurred the lines between walls and ceilings. Each room offered a new sensory experience, from interactive digital butterflies to immersive light sculptures. The entire journey was both surreal and grounding, inviting introspection and wonder.It's more than an art exhibit; it's an exploration of perception and interaction. Whether you're an art enthusiast or simply curious, teamLab Phenomena offers a unique experience that lingers long after you leave.

title: Avoid at all costs
text: Avoid at all costs — misleading, overpriced, and completely ruined our Eiffel Tower experience.I booked a "hosted entry" tour to the Eiffel Tower through Headout via paristickets.com, paying €262 for 2 adults and 2 kids. The website explicitly states: “Meet your host at the designated point, get escorted through queues, and let your host line up to validate your tickets on your behalf. Then, head to the elevators and enjoy access to the 2nd floor or summit, as you explore each floor at leisure.”None of this happened:We were not escorted through queues — we stood in line for 2.5 hours, with two young children.The host did not line up on our behalf — we waited the entire time just like everyone else.We did not explore at leisure — the host gave a full guided commentary, which I had deliberately chosen to avoid.Summit access was closed, and we’ve received no meaningful compensation for this.What’s worse, the entire experience ruined our expectations and impression of visiting the Eiffel Tower. The kids were exhausted and just wanted to sit on the ground — the moment was completely lost.In the end, we got what the Eiffel Tower sells for €58, but paid nearly five times more. I requested a refund of the difference between the official tariff and what we paid — they refunded just €32, which is frankly an insult. This service is deceptive, overpriced, and shows zero respect for customers.Book through the official Eiffel Tower website — or, if online booking isn’t available, just go and stand in the line yourself.And the truth is: you end up standing in the same line anyway — whether you have a host or not. It’s just much cheaper without them. You’re basically paying extra for nothing.

title: My visit to Dolmabahçe Palace and Hagia…
text: My visit to Dolmabahçe Palace and Hagia Sophia was truly unforgettable. Dolmabahçe took my breath away—the palace is incredibly grand, with crystal chandeliers, marble staircases, and beautiful European-inspired decor. It was fascinating to walk through the same halls the Ottoman sultans once did. Hagia Sophia was just as powerful, with its unique blend of Christian and Islamic history—seeing ancient mosaics alongside Islamic calligraphy was deeply moving.However, I do have a few comments. First, while the ticket included “skip the line” access, it didn’t cover security checks, which still took time. It would be much more efficient to have a fast-track lane for that, especially for people who book online.Second, I feel the price is getting too high. Hagia Sophia used to be free, and now it's quite expensive for tourists. I believe such historically and spiritually significant places should be more accessible, like the Blue Mosque, which still offers free entrance. These are treasures meant to be shared and appreciated by everyone, not just those who can afford it.Still, the experience was rich in history and beauty, and I’m grateful I got to see it. Just hoping for a few improvements in pricing and entry logistics.

name: Taimoor Siddiqui
title: Beware of this scam
text: Beware of this scam. The company is very misleading with its pricing. At first, they don’t make it clear that there are additional charges to be paid when picking up the car. Once you make the booking, you receive an invoice that shows a significant amount owed at the lot.They use terms like “Pay Now,” “Pay at Lot,” and “Grand Total” in a way that suggests you’re getting a better deal by paying upfront. However, the reality is that you’re required to pay both now and again at the lot—a highly deceptive tactic. The “Grand Total” only reflects the online payment and does not include what’s due at the lot, further adding to the confusion.When I called customer service for clarification, the experience was terrible. I asked for the representative’s name; initially, he refused to give it and later said it was "Diego," which I doubt is even accurate.Wish I could give 0 stars.

title: Just pay to park at the airport
text: Hampton Inn & Suites had the warmest desk staff who gave me clear parking and shuttle information on my Tuesday morning arrival. I parked my car and was promptly greeted by the shuttle driver and taken to Southwest departures. I left assured I would have an equally easy experience when I returned. Not so.A deeply unfriendly staff person took my call for the shuttle when I returned late Saturday night. I was coldly told that I would be waiting at least 45 minutes and could call back around that time to get an ETA. After a 6 hour flight I really just wanted to get to my car and go home.I parked at Hampton in an attempt to spend less than I do parking at Harry Reid. Between the online booking fee (even with a discount), tip for the shuttle driver and the overpriced cab ride I took to pick up my car rather than wait an unnecessarily long time for the shuttle, I ended up spending more. The complete change in my treatment by Hampton staff on Saturday night just added insult to injury. Lesson learned, I’ll stick with the Harry Reid overpriced lots the next time I fly.To Hampton Inn - Some of your staff could use a refresher on customer communication and rudimentary manners; they do work in the hospitality industry after all.

title: Disappointing Experience with Outdoorsy…
text: Disappointing Experience with Outdoorsy and PayPal Payment Option.I rented an RV van through Outdoorsy for a holiday trip and decided to use the 0% interest payment option through PayPal, allowing me to pay off the rental in four installments. To set it up, I linked my credit card to my PayPal account, expecting a smooth transaction. However, I was unexpectedly charged interest on my credit card.When I contacted Outdoorsy for assistance, I received no support. They simply directed me to PayPal, stating they received the payment from PayPal and that the issue was not theirs to resolve. They also mentioned that other customers had experienced the same issue with this payment offer. If that's the case, why is Outdoorsy still offering a payment option with these known issues?While I understand that PayPal may be at fault, Outdoorsy is the one offering this payment option on their platform. As such, they should have taken more responsibility in resolving the problem. Instead, they passed me off to PayPal, leaving me frustrated and without any resolution.Additionally, Outdoorsy should have made it clear on their platform that customers choosing this payment option must first be approved by PayPal. When I selected the payment plan, the process appeared seamless. But when I called PayPal, they asked if I had received an approval email. I had received an email authorizing the payment to Outdoorsy, Inc., but it turns out this was not the approval email they meant.It’s incredibly disappointing that Outdoorsy, a company that provides services to customers, showed no interest in addressing my concerns once they had received their payment. The lack of customer service and accountability is unacceptable. I will not be using Outdoorsy again and strongly advise others to be cautious when selecting payment options on their platform.

What is the point of requiring this if it's not even part of their process during conflicts between host and renter, at a minimum? text: Outdoorsy is the best! Neverending customer support and a user friendly website make listing my Winnebago View painless. Outdoorsy is a leader in RV rental sites.

name: Master Disaster
title: Outdoorsy is shady and unscrupulous.
text: Our RV got wrecked and had $22,000 in damages, the claims process took well over 9 months to get settled and they low balled the estimate  they do not cross check their renting customers insurance like stated they broke their very own policies by allowing someone without RV insurance coverage to rent my RV. The renter's failed to pay anything and moved from their address  to avoid prosecution . Outdoorsy did every snake move in the book and we had to cancel $16,000 worth of reservation bookings due to their lack of timely fix..    don't expect to get your RV fixed  in timely or professional matter if it's damaged.   The claims dept. adjuster low balled the estimates denied the claims . They get a chance to reply to this . I Dont care I got the lawsuit court case documents and text messages with their claims agent texts . And pictures that show how shady customer service really is. We still use this questionable website....

name: NL
title: OUTDOORSY are TERRIBLE
text: I rented an RV through “Outdoorsy” in BC Canada from the 9/2 to 9/19.  The Owner’s  name is Natalie and the Host’s is Jason Bashnick.  The entire experience was terrible.   The RV was ok but in a fairly poor state given it’s only 5 years old.  There were screws popping out of the bodywork here and there, a chipped windscreen, wardrobe door hanging off and every draw was full of the owners clutter leaving nowhere really to put our stuff.  Nonetheless we took the RV and had a great first part of our holiday. Then the nightmare began.   The breaks on the RV failed on Sunday 9/15 at 1pm.   We managed to pull into a gas station and called Outsoorsy for help…..eventually they told us help was on the way….then they called back to say it wasn’t but if we wanted to pay for a mechanic to come out we could? hello???.   They suggest calling the host who basically said not his problem call Outsoorsy……to be fair to Natalie she texted a few times to tell me to try this and try that but nothing corrected the fault.   Outdoorsy continued to be pretty useless by constantly telling us we had help on the way.  Eventually a breakdown truck arrived 27 hours later after we spend the night at the gas station.   The RV was towed back to Vancouver and we had to check into a hotel for the remainder of our trip.   Since then we have been trying,  unsuccessfully, to claim for the loss of the last four days of our vacation and our unintended hotel expenses.   Outdoorsy have been frankly utterly useless.  I would never recommend anyone use this company to book anything.   The owner basically blamed us for destroying the brakes in her vehicle…..I drive heavy goods vehicles regularly so I know that this is not the case.   Even if that were the case they should have insurance to cover that and the renters loss…….but seemingly they don’t want to even discuss a settlement……and as I said OUTDOORSY are useless DO NOT USE THEM. I am not going to have to use lawyers to fight this as I am not going to be rolled over as a matter of Principle.

name: Angela Jackson
title: New to hosting on Outdoorsy
text: I am new to hosting on Outdoorsy. Each time I call with a question, I am treated with respect and dignity. No question is too dumb and every representative I’ve dealt with is able to help me.

name: James Kisiel
title: Excellent application
text: I am extremely satisfied with this application. Customer service is top notch. My only suggestion would be to allow host to see reviews on potential renters. Host have the most on the line since campers cost several thousand dollars. It would be helpful to know if the renter has a past of not treating the RVs with respect.

name: Jerry Zaabel
title: Irresponsible Company
text: I have a campground in Northern AZ. at my horse ranch.  A person rented an RV from Outdoorsy and had it delivered to my property for their visit while participating in a horse clinic.  The renter was flying in from out of state.  The RV owner called me several times while driving to my ranch asking for directions.  She was having a hard time with directions and by the tone of her voice was getting more and more angry.  When they finally arrived at the ranch she pushed the entrance button to open the gate. When the gate opened half way.  Her husband who was driving the pick up truck pulling the RV attempted to drive through the partly open gate and struck the gate causing damage to both his vehicle and the gate opener.  The woman (RV Owner) was extremely upset and jumped out of the truck and pushed the gate causing the already damaged opener to total destruction.  The cost to repair was twenty five hundred dollars.  Outdoorsey's insurance refused to pay for the damage saying that type of damage didn't fit their policy.  They went on to say their policy covers Malicious Mischief or vandalism and/or direct collision.  Both of which were the case here.  After several weeks of "investigation"the insurance sent me a denial letter.  I would not do business with this company.  They are irresponsible and I wonder what they would have done if someone was injured.

name: Rylan Anderson
title: Worst experience I’ve ever had in my life
text: Renting a vehicle from outdoorsy was hands down the worst experience ive ever had dealing with a company, ANY COMPANY. Not only was the cost astronomical, they downsized us from a van to an SUV 2 weeks before our trip was supposed tk start, meaning we couldn't fit everyone we had originally planned. The truck broke down on our 2nd day, no refunds were ever provided for the money we had to spend to fix someone else’s vehicle. They booked us for the wrong dates and then used that as an excuse to keep our damage deposit. The owner used foul and harsh language towards me, calling me all kinds of names and awful things because I asked to get reimbursed for the money we had to spend to fix his vehicle that he rented us, not to mention losing out on multiple days of our trip and not being able to do what we wanted to do on the trip in the first place. And then after all that the owner is trying to charge me 1500$ in damages that were already there on the truck when we got it. This entire website is a scam for con artists trying to bleed money out of people and get repairs done on their vehicles for free. No matter what, DO NOT USE THIS SITE! You will regret it. Everyone I know who’s used this site has had the same experience or worse. Rent from literally anyone else and it will be better and cheaper than this.  I tried to apply for a partial refund, got denied. I had to literally go change my banking information to stop them from taking money of out my account without my permission. Sketchiest most awful company ever. Id rather poop in my hands and clap then give these guys another dollar.

name: Neil Charlton
title: A great partnership!
text: Outdoorsy has allowed me to rent my multiple trailers to customers in a seamless fashion, while helping me to maintain communication and customer service throughout the process!

name: Cat Smith
title: Westfalia campervans
text: I've enjoyed using this platform to find renters for my campervans. The experience has been very positive, I've had the pleasure of hosting renters from Europe, United States and Canada.The payments arrive on time. I feel confident that my Vans are fully insured.I do wish the platform was a bit more user friendly. I find it difficult at times to quickly use the platform to find information, such as my reviews and downloads for forms I need like the contract. Don't often know which Outdoorsy site I'm suppose to be using.Overall a very good experience so far.

name: Curtis  Scott
title: Outdoorsy makes it simple to rent out…
text: Outdoorsy makes it simple to rent out our travel trailer. Take some pic's, Complete and post the listing and the messages start coming.

name: Bréhier Chloé
title: My trip was a full success
text: Thanks to Harry my trip was a success !He took away my stress and got me everthing I needed : good tips, good camping Gear, good tire, good communication. First solo trip was lush! Made me want to do it again !

name: Cam Bogan
title: For Outdoorsy C-Suite
text: First of all, full transparency, I have never booked through Outdoorsy. What I have done is researched the internet universe to find an affordable place to live for a bit less than a year, because I am temporarily homeless. I specifically included the term "long-term" in the Google Search along with "RV rentals" and Outdoorsy came up close to the top and stated there on the Results page, "So unless you're looking for a 6 month rental..." , so I decided to see what was available on your site. I used your filter to choose my price range (by the way, you really need to add a Sort option to list RV's from least to most/most to least expensive option, because without it, you're wasting your customer's most important and non-renewable resource, their time) and realized that there was no option for long-term rentals with a reasonable monthly charge option. And thanks to the lack of Sort option for price-grouping, I had to look through 50+ options that were in my area. Since listings are ALL by the night and most for over $100 a night, that would make my legitimately long-term need of a 7 month rental (specifically 11/1-05/31), at $100 a night, $22K. The people that have the kind of money that make this amount seem reasonable, would likely just buy an RV, that way they can use it then put it on here for their entertainment subscription fund. I'm not asking you to stop being a predatory American company, I'm just asking you to be more honest and direct with your offerings. And, if you're already missing me before I sign off, don't despair, I will be doing another one of these reviews  for your unbelievably manipulative process by which you require customers to run around in figurative circles to close their Outdoorsy account. Toodles!

name: Chris Kutensky
title: I have been a long time host and renter, with Outdoorsy and others
text: I have been a long time renter and host, for 8yrs with Outdoorsy, as I recall. I'm my experience, they have a fantastic website and process. At days end, they are middle men. I felt that they handled CV19 when business was ten fold, smoothly when they were likely under staffed and many inexperienced renters, we're on the road renting RVs because airplanes were shutdown. I host in CO, a tourist state and if I had 20 Airstreams, I could have rented them all, easily. I can only imagine how hard Outdoorsy and other RV vendors worked to try to keep millions of units and millions of personalities Happy! It's a law of averages, and you'll always have some negatives, but as you can see it's 5% and when I was a kid, 95% was an A+.  Having rented and hosted for years I've learned any negative review is just like anything, it's based on personality and expectations, unless there is a blatant neglect of communication. Otherwise, personality plays a role, and I'm just as guilty of having too high expectations and no different than a dating website, every profile has a certain effort to market, whether price point, or allowing Pets when other do not.So, I say, always look at the big picture and the % of positive stars as some people post negatively based on emotion, or one-sided points of views, for example, host or renter. I recommend you consider the RVs age first, as age has wear/tear, and match that age to the competitive cost. Photos are great on sewing the design and general unit, but it doesn't show parts and like an aged car, truck, computer, what have you, age plays a role. Personally, I am thankful for Outdoors, introducing me to some fantastic, renters and I truly enjoy RVs and love being a Host, seeing renters come home after their journey and family vacation, all relaxed and happy. You can see the stress that has left their shoulders from PickUp to DropOff. BUT that said, there will always be certain personalities that you just can't live up to their expectations, and as a Host, you just tell them, text me, call me, let me know how I can help. We will handle any issues that comes up, if any, work with RV repair vendors, pay them, and upon drop off, if determined it wasn't Wear/Tear, we have deposits to reimburse us, but we just want you to enjoy, and so does Outdoors. It's a vacation, time to relax and enjoy and avoid making Mountains out of MoleHills as they say, as it's all comes out in the wash.  And over many years, I have issues as both renter and host, always minor but even issues with Brand New trucks or Rvs, it can happen, so keep comms open, that's what I recommend. No one wants a bad vacation for anyone, and that certainly not why Outdoorsy and Hosts option this industry. I saw this as I've had 1 or 2 personalities who tend, finding to complain whether RV, other industries / business they get involved in, they just tend to demand and it's just characteristic, no matter who the vendor may be. In today's world, it's hard to connect with this persona as they communicate one-way, and talk at you, instead of with you. I've seen very very few, but it's exaggeration and characteristic of the submitter, but to submit 1 star, even start to a middleman vendor, seems more emotional, than offering readers the positives. Why blame Outdoorsy unless the entire vacation was unruly managed start to finish, canceled or destroyed, at their direct blame. I just think emotions are not good reviews. With a great of Tv experience, I know some folks get upset about small things where others accept that "life happens". Wear and tear exists when you rent units over 5yrs, it's part of Rv life, there are tons of forums you should look into, per model you wish to rent, as that can help too.  Life is short, enjoy your vacation and just know that the older the "rental unit" it's more likely to have some small glitch occur, and don't try to fix or work on a Hosts Rv, without working with them, as I've seen people break things trying to Google How To, so let your Host handle it. And if an RV repairman need to get involved, hand it off to Host, they need to know who's working on their unit, and they know their Rv best, or either way, let them pay direct, hand it off to them, so you can go back to enjoying your time with family, friends or your journey.Two way communication is the answer. As long as there is two-way communication, there is no issue that can't be resolved. And no need to blame Outdoorsy or other vendors in general, your our Guest(s). Just work together and you will be in the 95%, I say, from my years in Rv works. Hope this helps!

name: Modoka
title: I was a Host on Outdoorsy
text: I was a Host on Outdoorsy.The hosting process just to get started was aggravating to begin with.  It's like no-one was serious about helping me get started.  You had to send them the same documents multiple times and they just kept passing you to the next customer service representative. The customer service was crap... After 2 or 3 weeks of trying to get set up, I was finally able to.  Skip to my first and only renter..  After their trip, they returned the camper late, and I understand things happen.  However, the Toilet/Tank was full and clogged first off.  I had to pay for the state park to let me empty it.  Next I noticed on the outside of the travel trailer there was duct tape across the arms and the main beam of the awning, Stretching the entire length.   Last, one of my slide outs were stuck in and and wouldn't go back out.  Mind you I emailed outdoorsy the photos plus receipts and I had to hire a mobile RV Mechanic to make the slide out work again.  They did a review and said they can't use the customers deposit for the damages.  (EXCUSE ME!) I understood that's what a deposit is for.  So that if something breaks that the deposit will help pay for the damages.. HUH, I guess not.  Either way Ive emailed back and forth with the piece of crap company and gotten nowhere.  They refuse to take the money out of the customers deposit and not pay me back for the mobile mechanic or the waste fee.  To me it's just the point of it all.  I do not recommend anyone using outdoorsy for your RV rental hosting needs.  BEWARE!!!

name: Consumer
title: Worst experience and will never use…

We had a minor chip in the windshield and just worked directly with the owner to have it fixed and paid them for the repair. Outdoorsy created a claim against me and is holding my deposit even through both the owner and I sent emails saying we don’t want a claim. name: rocio sanlop
title: Garbage DON'T rent from outdoorsy they…
text: Garbage DON'T rent from outdoorsy they miss representing vehicles in good condition and then hide facts to customers outdoorsy they falsely advertis in vehicles that get on road to be safe when their not they don't keep up good with their clients maintenance on their vehicles. name: JEFFROW
title: An absolute disaster and a vacation…
text: An absolute disaster and a vacation planned a year in advance ruined! The RV we rented broke down 900 miles from home, outdoorsy told us they would come pick up the vehicle and left my wife, our 7 month old baby and myself stranded. They said we should figure it out! There was no replacement rental and we had to rent a vehicle that would not fit all our camp gear (coolers, stove, and more)so we were forced to abandon it also lost $400 worth of  groceries that was in the refrigerator.Being stranded over night and more than 16 hours of trying to resolve the matter we were just defeated 😞 after we got home we called outdoorsy and they offered us $100 for our next trip with them. The most inconsiderate disrespectful customer service you could imagine. Imagine being stranded 900 miles from home in an RV you spent $3000 to rent and when it breaks down they come pick it up and leave you, your family and your gear in some random neighborhood on the side walk and they assure you that you can figure it out!!!Please don’t let this happen to you.

name: Julia Soh
title: Rental went well until return with minor damage.
text: Rental went well until we returned the vehicle with a minor damage. Repair costs were outrageous! Outdoorsy tested my credit card for reauthorizing my card on the deposit without letting me know with a suspicious identity. I cancelled my card and had to deal with all that hassle before finding out Outdoorsy wanted me to pay the insurance deductible. Sending a check instead of giving my new credit card number was complicated because they insisted on a USD check.

name: C. Flint
title: HORRIBLE company
text: HORRIBLE company. NEVER do business with them, unless you want to be stuck holding the bill for an accident. They denied a simple claim with a mechanic statement indicating it was a "freak accident" because Outdoorsy claimed it was a mechanical issue. It wasn't, clearly stated by the mechanic. They would rather you run the RV off the road and cause thousands of dollars in damage. Avoid their "Peace of Mind" Insurance package at all costs - they are just going to deny everything anyway. You're better off returning a damaged RV and making them take you to court than bothering trying to make a legitimate claim.

name: kerriecameron
title: At a loss for our holidays because customer service did nothing to help us
text: After booking an RV we tried contacting the host to set up arrangements.  The host wasn't responding. I emailed host once 3 weeks and a second time one week before reaching out to customer support for help.Customer supports response was that they give hosts 24-48 hours to respond because "we understand life can throw your routine off".  I replied with our timeline of trying to contact the host and asked that they help us reach the host. I haven't heard anything back from customer support after this.I emailed multiple times and I called multiple times. No one would answer the call, and once I was on hold for 30 minutes (no exaggeration) to only be disconnected after a recording told me no one was available to take my call.I reached out on social media with my situation and got a response to call or email customer support for assistance... really?!  That response just added more to my frustration.I had to cancel my reservation one week before our holidays because of the unresponsive host and lack of support from the folks at outdoorsy.  Thankfully the amount was deposited back into my account.Now aside from this frustrating experience with outdoorsy and their host, I am $80 out of pocket for the "service fee" that wasn't refunded... Really?!  What service did I pay for??  A whole lot of wasted time on my end for trying to get service, I should charge outdoorsy for my time, not the other way around.But the worst part of all this is my family and I have been looking forward to this, our annual holiday that we work very hard to afford and now we don't know what we're going to do.  We have a campground  booked with nothing to bring with us. So to quote your customer service I guess "life can throw your routine off" but replace "life" with "outdoorsy".From this experience, my take away is outdoorsy doesn't care. At no point did anyone on your end try to resolve this matter.  You have profited off my service fee and my family is now at a loss on what we will do.  An appropriate action on your part would have been to 1) Respond to our concerns first and foremost 2) Try to resolve our concerns by helping us contact the host 3) If the host remained unresponsive, find another solution if possible.  Would there have been another rental you could have helped us manage? We even would have paid more for a bigger camper if necessary.  But unfortunately none of that happened.No one wins from this experience! Outdoorsy, sure you made money from my service fee, but you had to refund $800 and our holidays are one week away and we don't know what we're going to do.Outdoorsy if you do care about the people you are providing services to and making a profit off of, you still have time to make this right for me and my family. I have little hope, but at this time I have little options.

name: Justin Pintler
title: Funds take too long to be deposited
text: It takes a little long for the funds to be added to my account. Especially if the funds are released on a Thursday, I typically won’t see them in my account until Monday.  Which, considering all the technology out there with banking doesn’t make a lot of sense.I also don’t think there should be fees on any add-ons or damage damages that are taken out of the security deposit.  I know it’s a small amount, but every penny counts considering the amount that is taken out of the rental.Overall, I would say I’m happy with using the service, but I am looking at other options as well.

name: Brett Johnson
title: Do not use Outdoorsy
text: Do not use Outdoorsy.  We rented an RV and it was not as advertised. It was wrecked and had several things on the RV that did not work, such as hot water.  Outdoorsy did nothing stating “buyer beware” and the owner is non-responsive.

name: Jay Celina
title: Owner canceled 3 days to trip! Summer ruined!
text: The owner canceled 3 days before trip. We were left with tons of food, camping grounds fees, loads of other expenses. They ruined my and my kids summer. Outdoorsy, never again!!!Update: outdoorsy reached out to me via email for no purpose other then to say the same they have been saying.

name: Darrell Hunter

text: My rental got canceled 5 days before our vacation i will never ever ever rent anything from them again it ruined our vacation and got nothing in return... what a show they are

name: adrian romero

text: AVOID AT ALL COSTS, they will rip you off and their customer service couldn't be worse!

name: Scott Ford
title: This is the worse company they won't fight for there customers. I am a customer and you did nothing to protect me
text: This is the worse company. Be careful renting anything. They believe the hosts when the host is ripping you off. My word with proof that the host lied, cheated and stole from me and my family.
