name: Zach Klimko
title: Giant red flags
text: Giant red flags. We rented a trailer that had a completely dead battery, and we were given no idea by the owner.We provided Outdoorsy time stamped photos of the battery going dead within 45 minutes, even after hours of running a generator to charge it. We lost all our food overnight, we had no heat. We had an incessant beep that kept our dog and family up, and the only way to stop it was by running the generator at all times, which clearly isn't an option in the middle of the night.After weeks of internal review outdoorsy sent us a photo of their terms of service with yellow highlighting on the line saying "failing to use the vehicle in compliance with all instructions and warnings provided by us and hosts." Not sure how we could have better used a dead battery that was not disclosed. We did buy additional propane as the owner did disclose that he didn't even check if they were filled. And we weren't given a key.Hideous experience and clearly Outdoorsy is going to back their owners over the customers. Buyer beware.

name: May L.
title: RENTER BEWARE
text: Since Outdoorsy refuses to post my negative review on their site I will post it here.Backstory -Outdoorsy provides a 14 day window to provide a review. I was about to post my review on their site at 11pm on the 14th day and it said I was no longer able to post as they operate in central time and it was already 1am the next day so I missed their window by 1 hour.I was then asked if the review was positive as they could manually post a positive review for me but not a negative one.Can someone please explain how this is a fair policy that they can manually post a positive review but not a negative one? It’s screams scam all over and fake positive reviews.Here is my review of my RV rental experience:RENTER BEWAREAs first time RV renters, we were extremely disappointed with our stay and the treatment of our group. We had to depart a day earlier than expected and had called the host to let them know. I asked what we needed to do before leaving and he said just make sure to turn everything off and close the door. They never mentioned anything about cleaning the RV before we left, nor was it mentioned to us when we checked-in. Later that evening, we received a message saying we had left the RV in a ‘state’ and that there were stains on the cushions and blinds and they were charging us $775 for excess cleaning and to replace the items that were supposedly stained.We were honestly shocked by this message and offered our apologies and even to come back and clean the RV due to the misunderstanding of what the prep fee covers as we were under the impression it covered the cleaning (it literally states on Outdoorsy that the fee is to cover professional cleaning and required maintenance checks).We were told that they were unavailable and had already cleaned half the RV. We explained that we were under the impression the prep fee covered the cleaning but then the host began to scold me telling me they had left cleaning supplies and that I was making excuses as to why it wasn’t cleaned.They did not care at all that it was a misunderstanding and that if we had known we were supposed to clean it, we would have done so.We feel taken advantage of as first time RV renters as there is no way it would cost them $200 of time to clean the RV, $431.15 to replace the dinette cushion with a tiny yogurt drink stain or $144.45 to replace the blinds that we had supposedly stained.Hopefully this review can help the next person renting so they do not get scammed like we did. Make sure you read the paperwork before you sign it and do not be too trusting of hosts. Also make sure to take photos and document before and after as we forgot to take photos before we left and therefore had no evidence of our own to dispute their claim.

name: Sad Camper
title: Same day cancellation by owner
text: Our host/owner cancelled at the last minute on the day of the rental.  He was very nice and apologetic, but that did not help our camping trip.  He had a known medical condition that he did not make accommodations for.I give the company two stars, rather than one because we did get all of our money back, from Outdoorsy, and the company did make an effort to find another camper, but due to the last minute notice, the few available did not fit our needs.

name: Kelly Martin
title: We rented an RV June 2022
text: We rented an RV June 2022. The person we rented the RV from was great. However, the awning fell off during our travels. We had purchased an insurance policy and paid the thousand dollar deductible. Then outdoorst proceeded to essentially harass my car insurance company for additional damages for which they paid out an additional $3000. We're not even sure how the awning fell off but we were considered responsible. My insurance company said that there was a clause in the rental agreement stating that although the insurance was purchased through outdoorsy, they had the right to pursue further damages from the car insurance. I would never use this company again. it was an awful experience.

name: Gord Nuttall
title: Average SaaS company
text: Better roadside assistance needed.  I feel they only care about bookings, a typical SaaS.  And how they get away with taking 40% is beyond me. They charge the renter and host both around 20% per booking.  Way to high imho.  Should be more like 15% like airbnb and VRBO.  That's a finder's fee, not 40%.  Competitors are the same.  It must be the insurance companies.

name: Christoph Mischke
title: International transaction fee. For what??
text: There is an international transaction fee of 3% of all payments, although I paid in Canadian dollars. There is no effort at all for the company, so I feel completely mucked.So I paif two times: a fee to my bank because I had to pay in a foreign currency, and this unnecessary "international transaction fee". Will never rent there again.

name: Graham
title: Probably won't be trying Outdoorsy again
text: I have used Turo to rent cars on vacations and thought Outdoorsy would be similar.  I submitted my "application" to rent a very attractive van, using the Outdoorsy website, selecting from the calendar for available days.  I also sent a supporting message to the owner, giving some information about me and my wife.  I did notice that many of the postings by other owners and this one had no bio: "Host bio coming soon! **** is committed to providing great stays for guests."  Strange that they don't even care to offer information about themselves.  I received a message from the owner saying that our requested dates were taken and the van was being used by the owners family.  I let them know that the online calendar still indicated availability.  They have still not updated that.  I am sure there are other options but I just could not be bothered struggling with the back and forth.  Will use a commercial business next time.  Similar pricing.

name: scott
title: Great times
text: I would leave no stars but that is not an option. Our trip went great trailer was wonderful everything went smoothly

name: Elizabeth Brooks
title: Outdoorsy reviw
text: I do love the ease of use of outdoorsy. The website and app could be improved. I am not thrilled about the emphasis on renting to who ever inquires. In the beginning i had a few people who misrepresented their situation. I cancelled with them and i was given to understand it was my fault and i could face a penelty. Now i interview the potential guests before i accept them as renters.  I am nowvery impressed with the quality of people that rent my camper. It has been a good experience all the way around with these renters.I have one issue about issuing a refund to one guest that outdoorsy has not resolved.

name: Anita
title: The host scammed us
text: Booking an RV through Outdoorsy was straightforward, but our trip was plagued with issues that led us to request a refund. Unfortunately, Outdoorsy was unable to resolve the matter with the host and redirected us to a third party. Since January 2024, the host owes us $2,000 in compensation, yet Outdoorsy has not taken responsibility. Even worse, the host continues to rent out the RV. Despite numerous calls, I’m always told, 'We will contact you in 48 hours,' but no one ever follows up. This level of service is unacceptable. Save yourself the hassle and book elsewhere!

name: Joseph  Cooper

title: Look elsewhere
text: As a host with Outdoorsy I’ve found several inconveniences doing business through this company. Navigating their website/app seems convoluted and illogical. I have to click through too many other menu options to get to my calendar to update my availability. The app only allows you to upload up to 5 photos for the pre- and post-trip inspections and also requires printed inspections which take up a lot of time. The company is pretty paper-heavy. Hosts are required to print out the 28-page rental terms & conditions in addition to roughly a dozen pages of pre-arrival checklists, walk-throughs, booking documents, and post-trip inspection FOR EVERY GUEST. These things should all be available through the app but that’s not an option at this point. The company takes 25% of each booking payout, which is the most I’ve seen among the 5+ RV rental platforms I’ve researched. Plus they charge the host a cancellation fee of $50-$100 (after the 2nd cancellation within 6mos) even if the host has to cancel as a result of a renter doing damage to the RV or if a guest bails but doesn’t officially cancel. Why should the company, who suffers no inconvenience, get a cancellation fee? I’m giving them two stars instead of one for the fact that they seem to have a large pool of guests & hosts to connect. However if you’re looking to rent out your RV I’d look elsewhere.

name: Stephanie Peoples
title: JUST STAY AWAY FROM OUTDOORSY-READ THE REVIEWS AND THE FINE PRINT
text: JUST STAY AWAY FROM OUTDOORSY!Today is 7/29/24 and I am still dealing with a bogus scam claim from 7/4/24, 25 days later!  I have spent several hours over many many days trying to communicate with Outdoorsy and I deeply regret using them.We are experienced campers.  We decided to rent an RV this time to make things easy (ha!).  We paid about $400 (in addition to rental, insurance, and Outdoorsy fees) to have it delivered and set up. During our rental over the 4th of July, the power cord + surge protector failed...resulting in a smoking, melted plug.  We were left with no power, no A/C, and we are in Texas in the middle of Summer. To our surprise, the the owner filed a damage claim against us which resulted in many headaches and countless hours of wasted time-with no real help from Outdoorsy. In fact, whenever I called, I could only speak with someone in the PHILIPPINES-never the same person, and never a last name.  Sometimes someone would respond via email, but would not be available by phone.  There was always a promise to escalate, but no follow-through.We had actually purchased the stationary insurance (also called excess insurance), which we learned that they defer to YOUR PERSONAL AUTO POLICY FIRST.  When I went back, I eventually found this in the fine print, but had to click through several pages and links to get to-essentially a rabbit hole. After the owner was told by our insurance company that this was not a qualified claim (and subsequently denied), he then pursued it with the Outdoorsy stationary policy-which was also denied. He told our insurance company that he would pursue it through the security deposit. They then emailed to ask us to approve a charge of $400-to pay for their faulty equipment-even after 2 denials stating that we were not responsible for their equipment failing. We declined. We cannot get anyone at Outdoorsy to help us with this, though we have reached out via phone and email multiple times. Today we learned that Outdoorsy has charged our card for ANOTHER $750-the original amount of our deposit.After another call and another request to escalate-they are telling us that they have released it.  I have yet to confirm that with my CC company, but will need to make sure that all future attempts to charge us will be denied.A side note of the stationary/excess policy-they also add an additional charge for roadside assistance-which you should not need if you are not towing the vehicle.  In fact, the policy becomes null and void if you move the camper for any reason on a stationary policy.We would never even think of trusting Outdoorsy again-it's really just a platform, taking a cut, and cheaply outsourcing their customer service.There is no protection and no one to call who can do anything to help.

name: Wanderlust AV
title: I've rented my vehicles via Outdoorsy…
text: I've rented my vehicles via Outdoorsy for three years now.  On a recent rental, one of my clients had a minor issue with their rental.  We discussed and decided a small refund would be best suited to resolve the situation.  Outdoorsy instructs you to call them if you would like to refund your client for something other than a cancellation.  When I called I was told that Outdoorsy would keep their 25% cut of the refund.  That's right, Outdoorsy keeps their 25% "host service fee" on the amount of money you REFUND as the host.Outdoorsy is not much of a service but provides a great disservice to both the renter, to whom they charge exorbitant fees and force the sale of often redundant insurance products but also the owner, from whom they take a 25% cut, even when the owner didn't ultimately keep those funds.I would love to see another business disrupt Outdoorsy and provide a quality, peer to peer, platform for rentals.  Most renters already have adequate auto insurance that covers their rental. Most owners need little more than a platform/market on which to rent their rigs and a payment processing service that allows for security deposits to be held appropriately.   What nobody needs is Outdoorsy in the middle of it all, bilking all parties for every penny they can.Follow up to Outdoorsy's response- yes, that's correct, you are keeping 25% of money the owner does not keep.  There is no confusion here nor is anyone implying that an additional fee is charged.Folks, this is why Outdoorsy releases 100% of your payout after handoff; it ensures they are keeping 25% of that money no matter what happens during or after the rental.  No other platform keeps their fee, particular a 25% one, on money you don't actually net.  In this case I wanted to refund my renter $750.  Trouble is, Outdoorsy only paid me $562.50.  I can't refund money I never received and Outdoorsy refuses to return their $187.50 cut of those funds that, again, are not in my bank account, to the renter.  They refuse to explain what they are keeping that $187.50 for and I don't know a soul who could rationalize why that money wouldn't be refunded to the renter.I can't post images here but would love to share a breakdown of a trip with the public to shed light on the exorbitant fees Outdoorsy hits both renter and owner with.  It's classic gig economy corporate shenanigans where a real service/platform is provided but everyone gets ripped off in the process of utilizing it.The fact that they want a 25% cut of money you don't get paid really says it all though.

text: Hi my name is Hunter Anstine Outdoorsy is a complete scam. They set up my deal, the renter flaked on me and I was still charged $3,072.19 for a rental I never received. I had to rent a separate vehicle from Enterprise. Don’t trust anything you see about Outdoorsy it’s all clever marketing to cover up scandalous behavior. To be clear Outdoorsy is not hearing me. The owner did not communicate with me appropriately and the did not deliver the vehicle. He told me he was leaving it somewhere unlocked with the keys in the cup holder and a contract to sign. That is sketchy as heck. And after that Outdoorsy took the sketchy owners side. Shame. I was not a cancellation or a no show, the renter was.

name: carolyn
title: If there were zero stars
text: If there were zero stars, that would be appropriate.  Rented an RV. Picked it up and drove 20 miles to learn the leaf spring broke and it could have been catastrophic.  In a nutshell, we got the run around.  My husband and I were both calling different departments and Outdoorsy literally did nothing.  Said they were sending roadside assistance and never did.  We were on the side of the road in the dark for two hours before we left the RV to find a hotel.  Next day we were told to call our own roadside assistance.  They were then going to help us find another camper...nope.  Nothing.  No reimbursment for our hotel because they only do that for trip interuptions.  HUH? We went camping and didnt have a camper anymore.  If that isnt a trip interruption, what is? We spent double what we budgeted bc we had to get a hotel room.  All our camping food spoiled and Outdoorsy did squat.  They did offer ten percent off our next camper.  Why would we rent from them again.Our acct number was 5258431 Under my husbands name. Jason

name: Ashley
title: Outdoorsy is a purposefully difficult…
text: Outdoorsy is a purposefully difficult service. Luckily I was able to talk w the owner directly for most things. The water tank leaked, there was no heat (in the mountains) and the driving conditions of the vehicle were questionable on the interstate. We drove for 14 hours in a terrible storm and found a small crack in the windshield upon returning home. Thought, no big deal, the insurance paperwork I read said they cover windshield cracks. Owner was very understanding. Since I paid $359 for MANDATORY insurance and then $500 extra for a security deposit, the owner and I figured getting the crack fixed would be a breeze. I have not been able to speak to anyone from the US to help me. I am a firefighter and my husband is a retired NAVY SEAL. We want to do the right thing for the owner and also have this company honor the insurance. They have directed me to a long contract that was “signed” but NOT by us. They’ve also changed the terms of the insurance agreement multiple times. This is fraud. They take good peoples money and then will not do the ethical thing by fixing the crack for the owner. After paying $850 in addition to the rent and fees, this more than covers the owner being able to get his RV repaired and for me to not pay any more money out of pocket. I paid $1500 to rent. $850 for insurance and security deposit. The owner only received $829 for the week rental. This is not morally or ethically acceptable. They do not want to serve their customers, the owners or respect that hard working Americans and veterans do not deserve to be manipulated and abused.

name: Brad
title: I rented a travel trailer that stated…
text: I rented a travel trailer that stated was "brand spanking new" that had too much to list here wrong with it. Broken awning, bathroom vent, etc. Through observation, video, and photos this was not new or even close. But what really turned things was me being alerted by someone at an intersection in the midst of returning vehicle that one of the tires was making a "bad sound". My wife and I rolled down windows and could definitely hear what she was saying. Tried to see if I could determine the cause. Thought it might be one tire that looked like missing something. At that time, I messaged owner rep to say something was wrong and asked if I should stop or continue to return. Was told camper had always had an issue with a tire and that I should be fine. A few miles later the tread on the tire separated causing a massive blowout and damage to the undercarriage. Was told in this process that there was no visible evidence of outside damage and tire appeared to be faulty. Also, through this process was told that tires were new by owner (worded in such a fashion as if to release her of any liability because this doesn't happen to new tires, while failing to recognize this is where they happen the most). Was also told that there had been a blowout on the same tire 2 months prior. Was told that is why "I" have insurance and within hours my $500 deductible was taken. I disputed the deductible because I am to be given a safe and reliable vehicle to rent. Was not provided a safe and reliable vehicle, and then when something on the camper failed, the expectation was of me to fix it or pay for it. This would be the final response from my dispute...Hi Bradley,After an investigation and careful consideration of the evidence provided by both parties, we have decided in your favor.We believe you should be refunded $250 from the security deposit claimed. While we uncovered that the tires were over 5 years old already, we believe you should shoulder $250 since the damage was incurred during your rental.And here is my response and reason for 1 star....Think I will consult with someone on this. Aside from a contradiction within your response which has to leave someone lying by stating they were outdated tires when I had multiple people state tires were new (with one very important individual stating they were new and faulty), it is the holding the renter accountable due to the actions of an owner that finds this resolution appalling to me.If what you state in your resolution is correct, then the lack of action by an owner to provide safe and reliable tires has taken place. If what the owner and her handyman stated (and documented) is correct in stating the tires were newly purchased, it was they who purchased and installed an inferior product and not myself. Had I punctured a tire, went to purchase a new tire on my own, the tire then exploded causing damage, I would most certainly be singing a different tune. But your resolution seems to state that I must pay 250 dollars because someone provided me with an unsafe and unreliable vehicle for rent. It's hard for me to not think of a thousand scenarios at play here that would represent the same type of conclusion. Such as, what if an owner has an engine failing?  Was repaired with substandard or improper parts that result in complete engine failure while on the next rental. Would the responsibility of the renter be to replace the engine? If so, then there are no protections from the owner's doing whatever they want, with WHATEVER they want, because of no consequence. And I have a significant issue with this because the initial response from the owner of my rental was just that. And I quote, "that's why you have insurance".As far as I'm concerned, the first and foremost priority from the owner is to provide a safe and reliable vehicle for rental. The fact this did not happen should instantly render any contract null and void and prohibited anyone from obtaining my deposit. I seem to believe most people would agree with me. And what adds insult to injury is that you have a host who is falsely advertising a vehicle that is not as it is portrayed.What also bothers me greatly is the fact that I reached out to the owner's representative prior to any damage occurring to state there was an issue. Specifically asked him whether to continue or not. Only to be told they have always had an issue with a tire and I should continue.I will say basically the same thing I said to the owner. This is absolutely about principle. I do not believe I should pay 500/250/or even 5 dollars. The responsibility of repairs needed due to faulty parts and equipment provided by an owner should not rest on the renter in any shape or form but that of the owner.

name: Nigel Bell
title: Abandoned by Outdoorsy
text: I hired a RV through Outdoorsy through August 2023 (20 nights). They sub-let to another company in the days/week before commencement - being told the campervan I booked (5 months earlier) was no longer available. A 'similar' vehicle was available when I arrived (same price, same conditions).  Wrong.No stealth camping as few curtains (!), no pillows (!), limited stove or utensils (!), no outdoor seating or  cover (!).  Not what I expected or paid for ....But worse was the developing problems with the two-year old automatic vehicle (a Mercedes van!).From Day 1 it had problems - wrong gear, shuddering forward, over-revving - which was increasingly dangerous when driving on US freeways at half the set speed.  Stop-start - stop - shudder - stop - start - stop altogether - so multiple calls to the intermediary company, then Outdoorsy.Outdoorsy provides intermittent phone calls/call-backs during the afternoon, leading to a request to drive (!) to the nearest specialist repair workshop (30 miles away).  Tried on back-roads .. but same problems and the vehicle again died half way, leaving me at the edge of the road in 108F degree heat in the middle of no-where ... for 15 hours /overnight!Many Outdoorsy phone calls - no action - before next morning the tow vehicle was sent to the previous (wrong) address!Eventually, towed away to the repair shop.  Long wait before they diagnosed the problem.  Meantime, Outdoorsy told me I was one my own - they wouldn't supply an alternative vehicle.  I was expected to start all over again with a new hire (whilst marooned in the middle of nowhere!)."Not good enough, we have a paid contract" I said - and let me speak to the manager.  It took a week before a manager sent an email back, asking about my problem !!!!And fortunately for me, the dealer found and fixed the 'drive' cables/electronics that had been chewed through by 'varmints' prior to my hire.  So after two delayed days of hassle I was able to continue.LESSONS:Outdoorsy would not meet their contractual conditions when it got hard....they made their vehicle replacement problems mine ...Outdoorsy is better at PR and marketing than delivering ...Outdoorsy subsequently made it very difficult to get a refund for the lost two days of travel ...Don't believe their promotional spin .. my experience says you're on you're own if there's a vehicle replacement problem.

name: Umar Chouhdry
title: Beware of Outdoorsy's Misleading…
text: Beware of Outdoorsy's Misleading Cancellation Policy and Poor Customer ServiceI recently had an incredibly disappointing experience with Outdoorsy, a company that seemed promising for RV rentals. My ordeal began when I booked a van for a trip in June, well in advance. Realizing the costs were too steep for my budget 10 days later, I decided to cancel, expecting a reasonable refund considering the trip was nearly 5 months (June 2024) away. To my shock, I discovered that Outdoorsy had a hidden trap in their cancellation policy, costing me over $1000 in cancellation fees, for a service I never utilized.The van owner, under the guise of convenience, persuaded me to switch from Turo to Outdoorsy, which I suspect was a maneuver to exploit Outdoorsy's cancellation policy for his financial gain. Outdoorsy's policy, which mercilessly penalizes customers for cancellations made outside a narrow 48-hour window post-booking, is both unfair and predatory, especially when cancellations are made well in advance of the booking date.Their defense? A rigid adherence to a policy that favors hosts at the expense of customers, trapping hard-earned money with no service provided. The fact that this trip was months away and the rushed booking process facilitated by the van owner makes this policy even more egregious.Outdoorsy's lack of transparency and customer empathy has left me feeling cheated and disillusioned. Their policies do not protect the interests of the customer but serve to enrich themselves and their hosts at our expense. I caution anyone considering using Outdoorsy for their RV rental needs to think twice. You may find yourself, like me, out of pocket for services you never received, entangled in a web of unfair policies designed to profit from your change of plans.Final Rating: 1/5 StarsAvoid Outdoorsy if you value your money and seek a fair, customer-centric rental experience. There are other platforms out there that respect and protect their customers' interests far better.

name: Laurie Aaron-Chodoronek
title: Our family of 6 got scammed by Outdoorsy!!
text: Our family of 6 is planning a 10 day road trip this summer and wanted one vehicle comfortable for us all. I found the perfect vehicle on Outdoorsy, absolutely stunning! We were all so excited. The booking was glitchy and instead of charging a deposit with the reservation I was charged the full $1,300 for the trip that doesn't start for 5 months! I contacted customer service, they fixed it and charged me $757 in Feb. for a Jul. trip, balance later. I never received a confirmation from the vehicle owner, just from Outdoorsy. A few weeks later my daughter inquired about vehicle features and found out the vehicle was sold a year and a half ago and the owner can't get Outdoorsy to remove it. I contacted customer service to cancel and refund all my money. I was told they won't refund my money unless the vehicle owner verifies my claim. Now the vehicle owner has become unresponsive too. If you try to cancel the reservation on Outdoorsy they keep a service charge of $145. It's a total mess and Outdoorsy accepts no responsibility in validating a reservation, or vehicle availability or promptly refunding my money. For a finish, I'm now disputing the charge with my credit card company under fraud protection. Outdoorsy took my money, won't refund it, for a vehicle that isn't available. These people are scammers! Watch out!

name: christie
title: Avoid at all costs!!
text: Edited to add that following my review outdoorsy have finally sent us on the 'invoices' from the owner which is a screen grab from Amazon and a shopping cart for another website! The owner hasn't even ordered the parts they've charged us for and outdoorsy have still taken the money from us!Steer clear!! We visited LA and hired an RV through outdoorsy for ten nights to see some sights and enjoy a family holiday.On delivery of the RV the owners told us they'd been up all night trying to fix the slide out after the family that rented it and finished with it the night before our trip has broken it and we need to be extra careful with it as it was not fully fixed, handed us a screwdriver and sent us on our way. Should have run a mile then!First night we struggled with the slide out and the over cab bunk wouldn't work, asked owners for help and they said they'd work it out and let us know the morning after!! So 3 beds down and no where for the kids to sleep we finally found a you tube video on how to over ride the system and bring the beds down.Long story short we had several issues with the slide out and the owners advise was to not use it, but since we'd rented the RV as a family of 6 we needed the slide out working in order to have enough space to sleep. Ended up having to stay in one place so that the owners who were exceptionally rude and aggressive over the phone could come meet us to try fix the issue, they managed a quick fix but told us we'd only be able to perform one more slide action and so we couldn't visit anywhere else in it and had to drive in one from San Fran to LA. During one of our drives an awning over one slide out actually came loose and on advice from the owners my husband and sons had to climb up on to the roof of the RV to remove it!! We stayed in touch with outdoorsy via email during the trip so that they were aware of the issues we were having and they continually reassured us that they would help us claim compensation on return to the UK.The owners also advised us that the TVs in the RV didn't work without dvds (despite advertising that it had an outdoors TV entertainment system and two indoors) so we never used the TVs.When we delivered the RV back to the owner she herself didn't turn up and instead sent her husband who rushed us out saying he was late for a school play (they chose the collection time) he wouldn't do a walk round but verbally confirmed happy with the RV and zoomed off within five minutes of us arriving back.On return to the UK they've claimed $1300 of our deposit and have only started 'TV and slide out topper' as the reason. We've asked them to confirm what was wrong and what they mean by that but got the response 'tv and slide out topper'We've gone through outdoorsy internal review and they took over a month to decide that they don't know who's at fault and cannot provide us with evidence or proof of even a basic description of what they've claimed the money for as they say the money was taken by the host and not outdoorsy (shows as outdoorsy on our statement)They do not want to know. I'm not sure how money can be taken without any proof as to what for or why.Were assuming the slide out topper means the awning they actually told us to remove and was also missing from the other side of the RV so I'm certain somewhere another family have been charged for that and it's never been fitted or replaced.I've warned outdoorsy that this owner needs removing from the platform but as long as it's making them money they don't seem to care.Do not book with this company please save yourself the hassle. A month on from our holiday we're still chasing our money back.When the initial claim was made on our deposit outdoorsy told us it was just a hold whilst the internal investigation was ongoing and that it wouldn't actually be taken but a few days later it left our account.Dishonest, unreliable and unhelpful.

name: Aaron
title: Beware
text: From the very beginning the people we were dealing with were less than up front about various maintenance issues.  They knew exactly how many miles we were traveling and that we were using the unit to move our 97 year old mother, who had just had a stroke.Basically there were several things that would fail, cause further damage and even perhaps cause injury that we had to fix.  When we returned the unit the owners claimed there was damage from a slide out unit that, to our knowledge, was working when we dropped the unit off.  We just walked away from the $1500 deposit and then, after dragging things on for a month they want more money.  I billed them for the work we had to perform and hope they just leave it at that.The impression I got from the process is that leaving things that will cause further damage is a strategy to have an excuse to grab the deposit from unsuspecting renters.  At this point it feels like they are trying to pick us up by our feet to shake all the change out of our pockets. We have already paid thousands of dollars and the maintenance of the vehicle should not be our problem.Just beware, I can't speak about all the owners, but these seem to want to take advantage of us.  The extra insurance we purchased has proven unresponsive and the Outdoorsy customer support is offering to try to bring resolution, so will see if this can end any time this year...Update: The interior damage insurance we purchased did come through, but it took quite a while.  To their credit Outdoorsy did give us a token credit to express good will and acknowledge our inconvenience with the issues we experienced.  Maybe through the process the owners, who are young, will learn about maintaining their equipment.Just beware, don't make assumptions and ask questions about the condition of the equipment.  According to the Outdoorsy policy, if the owners disclose a problem and you accept the rental, you become responsible for the problem and any further damage it may cause while in your possession.  If you experience issues with the equipment that require attention, if the owners are not cooperative, you are stuck on the side of the road and may be financially responsible for getting repairs done.

text: Before using BravoFly for the first time I read many negative reviews here to see where people had experienced issues. People have so many issues these days ;-]Keeping a close eye on the total amount that would be charged at all times I made my way through the searching and booking process for a flight with a transfer in ABU DHABI. There is a soft up sell going on at all times, which I decided to ignore, picking the zero cost option at each step .. looking at the total cost clearly displayed on the right of my laptop screen as I did so.Once nice touch by BravoFly, they asked if any assistance will be needed *before* payment is made, I just had surgery so I opted for WCTG.BEWARE people who can/do not read, at the very last step I was again offered the 'opportunity' to upgrade to some flex plan, the wording is honest but tricky. If in doubt click the button that is NOT encouraged, just like always, for decades !-/I entered the CC info clicked PAY, verified using my bank app that the TOTAL AMOUNT was indeed the amount I expected .. how can anyone get this wrong ? Back from bank app to BravoFly payment confirmed and I was reminded I needed to wait up to 24 hours [maybe more because of assistance request] while BF agents worked feverishly on my behalf as I slept.Went to bed .. woke up .. got up [mofg ouch *!* surgery] .. checked email account I had given to BF .. yes all good, flight booking complete, logged into BF account with the email address I had given and checked everything looked ok, got the Airlines booking code from BF website.Logged into my previously registered Airline account which uses a different email address [cute] enter the BF supplied code and .. voila .. there is my booking along with the assistance request.I did update my contact details on Airlines system as the phone number got muddled [the country code was merged into the local number].Any changes to the flight booking must be made via BF, I can add secondary services via Airlines' site if I wish.What can I say, post Covid I stuck to booking directly with the airlines, this time I thought I'd be adventurous. BF saved me over 20% which is enough to matter IMHO.So far BravoFly are worth 4*s .. only magicians get more. If things go South, rather then East, I will update here.

title: SCAMMERS: Avoid Bravofly!
text: Misleading Policies and Terrible Customer Service.I had an incredibly frustrating and disappointing experience with Bravofly regarding a refund for my roundtrip flight from Australia to Costa Rica. I purchased their Full Flex service, which supposedly guaranteed a 90% refund for cancellations. Unfortunately, this service turned out to be a scam hidden behind convoluted fine-print terms and overcomplicated policies.Misleading Full Flex Policies:I received an email from Bravofly on May 5, 2024, confirming that my Full Flex insurance was active. However, Bravofly later claimed this email was sent in error, despite the terms stating:“The Voucher is valid for 12 months from the date the customer is notified of its details.”This means the service became active on May 5, regardless of an earlier refund. Bravofly refused to honor this, stating that a technical error absolves them of accountability.Poor Communication and Lack of Accountability:It took more than six months of emails to finally receive a response from someone with a name, rather than generic replies from their "Customer Care" team. Their responses consistently failed to address the core issues or provide any meaningful resolution.They ignored their responsibility for misleading communication, instead blaming me for not “confirming” whether the service was still active. Why should customers need to verify the validity of an email sent by the company itself?Nonexistent Escalation Process:Their representatives repeatedly refused to escalate my complaint. I was told the resolution would not change, even though their internal error directly caused my financial loss.Fine-Print Policies:Bravofly’s Full Flex service includes hidden restrictions, such as:Cancellations must be made before the outbound flight.Refunds do not apply to one leg of a booking.These terms were buried in the fine print and were not clearly communicated during the booking process. Instead, Bravofly relied on technicalities to avoid honoring their advertised services.Outcome:I was only refunded $120 for a $4,000+ ticket, which is insulting and unacceptable. Bravofly’s lack of accountability, refusal to escalate, and reliance on technical errors to deny claims make them a company I cannot recommend to anyone.Final Thoughts:Avoid Bravofly at all costs. Their Full Flex policy is a scam designed to mislead customers, and their customer service is one of the worst I have ever experienced. They do not answer calls, provide no clear escalation paths, and fail to resolve legitimate claims. If you value transparency and professionalism, book with another provider.

text: A Two-Year Struggle for a Refund;Booking id: 1893426462Date of booking: 14th dec 2021Ryan air flight: FR4769PNR: T8ZHHSReturn flight : VY1265 PNR: QIW6KNI am writing this review to share my deeply frustrating experience with Bravofly, which has been nothing short of a nightmare. Over two years ago, I booked a flight through Bravofly that was subsequently canceled. Despite their initial assurances that I would receive a refund, I am still waiting.From the onset, communication with Bravofly has been abysmal. After my flight was canceled, I immediately contacted their customer service to inquire about my refund. Each time, I was met with vague responses and empty promises that the refund was being processed. I was assured multiple times that my case was being prioritized, but these claims have proven to be hollow.The company's lack of transparency and accountability is staggering. For over two years, I have been caught in a frustrating loop of automated emails and unhelpful customer service agents. Every interaction feels like starting from scratch, with no one able to provide a clear status update or a concrete timeline for when I might receive my refund.Bravofly’s handling of this situation has caused me significant stress and inconvenience. Not only did I lose the money spent on the tickets, but I also had to deal with the added financial strain of rebooking flights through another provider at the last minute. The customer service experience has been frustrating, with long wait times and representatives who seem either unwilling or unable to assist effectively.It's clear that Bravofly’s systems and processes for handling cancellations and refunds are severely lacking. A two-year wait for a refund is completely unacceptable and speaks volumes about their disregard for customers.To anyone considering booking with Bravofly, I urge you to think twice. My experience has been an ordeal that I wouldn't wish upon anyone. The promise of affordable travel quickly becomes irrelevant when you are left fighting for a refund for years, with no end in sight. Save yourself the trouble and choose a more reliable and customer-focused travel service.

text: Overall, my husband and I had a wonderful time on our trip to London and Paris.  The tour was advertised as 3 nights in London and 3 nights in Paris.  Shortly before our trip began, they changed our flight to London to a later flight so we basically lost a day there.  Two and a half days in London was not enough time.  We were able to do all of the tours scheduled for London, but we would've liked to have more time exploring the city.  I also would've liked if airport transfers were included in the tour.  On our flight to London we were seated in the very last row (57!) of the plane right between the two restrooms on the plane so it was hard to get any sleep with people going back and forth to use the restrooms.   I had trouble getting a time for one of the tours as it wasn't on my travel documents I received from Great Value.  Luckily there was someone in the office in the US when I called them from Paris! They were able to email me my "final" documents with the times for the tours, but that should've all been done BEFORE we left the US! Train from London to Paris was nice.  We were disappointed to find our hotel in Paris was a good 30 minutes from the city center.  It took us 55 minutes one afternoon to return to our hotel because the traffic is so bad there.  We would've preferred a hotel right in the city center so we could just walk out and go to the attractions in the city.  Instead, we had to pay for an Uber every day to get into the city.  The hotel was very nice, almost looked new, but we wish it was in a different area.  We didn't feel comfortable walking around at night, at all.  Again, overall it was a fabulous trip, but I would never choose the hotels we stayed in.

name: L. D.
title: Italy is Beautiful
text: Italy is, of course, beautiful and ITA Airways was incredible.  The location of the hotels were not so great. Best Western in Venice was right across the train station and made sense. PopArtment in Florence was not so greatly located, but at least was close to a tram but staff was rude and not welcoming. B&B in Rome was absolutely the worst location.  Away from everything and the Metro was a 12 minute walk in a not so great area. If the hotels are going to be located this far from a train station, there should at least be expectations on what trams/metro would be needed. The Metro didn't start until 5:30 a.m. and our flight out of Rome was at 9:20 a.m.  and we were 1 hour away from the airport,  which meant we had to take a $70 Uber at 4:50 a.m. to the train station and then catch an additional train to the airport.  The itinerary could use some help and needs to be more thought out from a tourist stand point. Even when asking locals it was hard for them to explain to us where to go because it was multiple trams/metro to get from the train station to the hotels and from the hotels to the attractions.

name: Jerry Wallace Brinson
title: Horrible London Hotel Booking
text: As part of our London/Paris trip, GVV booked us into the Zedwell Underground Tottenham Road hotel in London.  This hotel was absolutely the worst hotel experience our group has ever had when traveling.  Rooms are four/five levels below ground floor, with no windows, no pictures on the walls, no closet and no space to accommodate luggage, no hair dryers, no nightstands or lamps, no chairs or desk, no TV or telephone, no safe, refrigerator, no carpeting.The "bed" was a basically a mattress on the floor with filthy bedding.The room was not serviced our entire stay with the exception of two clean bath towels each day (no washcloths or hand towels). We had to specially request that they replenish the toilet paper.Because there were no hair dryers or clothes irons in the room, we were forced to go up to another floor to use communal hair dryers and irons in a "beauty/ironing room".The bathroom had a shower that left water all over the bathroom floor and an extremely tiny sink. No tissues or other amenities that one might expect in a four star hotel. The shower wall was moldy and unclean with hair on the walls. One morning we had no water. The plumbing was extremely noisy with various sounds during the night. Although this hotel boasted that the rooms were soundproof, noise from the subway trains were heard constantly throughout the night.But perhaps the most concerning issue to my party was the feeling that our safety and health were at risk by staying in this facility. The subterranean floors including the reception area in this hotel all reeked of sewage and stale air. In the event of a fire, there would be no way to escape. One of our party became ill during our stay and had to have EMS from the NHS come to evaluate her and transport her to the hospital. The EMS stated that the air in the hotel was very unhealthy due to no circulation and that it would be impossible to evacuate a patient by stretcher if necessary. Fortunately, the ill member of our party was able to walk out. It is possible that the unhealthy conditions in the hotel contributed to her illness. Three of the remaining members of our party ended up with severe head colds.GVV refused to compensate us in any way for this disgusting hotel.  Our travel voucher said that our stay included an “English breakfast” but the hotel had no food services.  GVV did refund us $10 per day per person for the missing breakfasts, but this amount is quite laughable to think that one could eat breakfast in London for $10 (7£).  GVV insisted that the hotel delivered on their online description.  Only if one considered a “curated playlist” to be constant subway train noises and “soothing scents” to be reeking sewage.Because of this horrible hotel experience, I cannot be comfortable ever using GVV again for travel and will definitely warn my friends from using them.  Their failure to offer us any compensation for this bad experience shows that they do not “Value” their customers, only their bottom line.In response to your response:It would still behoove your company’s reputation to offer monetary compensation for our unsatisfactory experience.  And I DO NOT mean in the form of a future travel credit, which is no more than you offer for all of your customers in the form of a $100 off pp travel voucher on any future trip.  I believe one of my co-travelers suggested that a $100 refund pp would be appropriate and acceptable to us.  But I guess you would rather receive a one star rating for your customer service.

text: We thoroughly enjoyed the Magic of Northern Italy tour. Our tour director was incredible! She made the trip so enjoyable and relaxing with her organizational skill, knowledge of the area, thoughtfulness, attention to details, and overall positive attitude with our group. We recognized the extra time she spent after hours to enhance our vacation. The overall itinerary was fabulous too! It was a great mix of bigger spots and a few smaller, more quaint towns. The itinerary was quite full, and we seemed to be on the road more than I expected. We were prepared having toured with larger groups in the past, that we'd experience more of a "preview" and general impression of each stop. I had hoped for more free time to just soak in the culture on our own. None the less, we made the most of our time allotted in each city with our local guides. They too were very flexible and accommodating to our group's needs or unexpected situations. In the future, I'd recommend starting the route in one city and working the route more linear (example, start in Venice and work west towards Nice and Monaco or vice versa.) That adjustment might eliminate so much time on the road and allow more free time in the beautiful destinations.We thoroughly enjoyed our 10-day tour of Northern Italy. It was our first time with Great Value Vacations. Granted we were so blessed with a great group of tourists that easily made friends and were considerate of each other's needs. That combined with the best tour director really was a game changer for such a positive experience with large group travel. We'll definitely be back!

name: Todd & Anne
title: Central Europe - most educational and surprisingly wonderful
text: Great Value Vacations did it again! Another beautiful destination that was easily adapted to our personal travel needs and interests.Our trip to Budapest, Vienna and Prague (Central Europe) was filled with storytelling, historical drama, delicious local and international cuisine, architectural wonders, arts and culture that seamlessly blends old-world charm with modernity. You really feel transported back in time when you walk the streets and enter buildings that have been standing for centuries, each one telling the stories of the people and events that shape the unique identity of each city. What was previously unknown to us was how much of a shared history this region has, yet how uniquely different the impact and significance on each one - such a treasure! We believe travel presents an immense opportunity to learn and expand one's worldview. Great Value Vacations does an awesome job of making that possible. Whether it's fully escorted packages with planned activities, self-drive options, or last-minute, budget deals that you personalize, they make it interesting and affordable and easy.We have reviewed many other "budget" travel websites purportedly offering "the best packages and affordable destinations" only to be disappointed with the options. Then, we find ourselves returning to GVV and booking an amazing vacation. Travel smart - use Great Value Vacations. We're already exploring our next destination! Thank you, GVV, for consistently delivering incredibly curated vacation experiences!

Public transportation was convenient. Train station in Budapest is very old. Train was not clean, bathrooms were dirty, sat in a six person cabin, no room for our luggage. title: Prices are very good and they get the…

name: Elizabeth
title: The itinerary was terrible
text: The itinerary was terrible.  It included a 12 hour layover in London when we only needed  one more short flight to be at our destination.  We have traveled with GVV 5 times but this one was not a good experience.  We booked this trip months in advance and were surprised by the terrible itinerary.  We essentially lost one whole day of our trip because it was spent at an airport.   The places we stayed were wonderful but we were visiting the highlands of Scotland at category 1places and there were only a few to choose from.  We were not aware of the limited choices or the poor itinerary. Our lodgings were great, but we had to upgrade all of them because there were none available at the package level.  The trip home has been a nightmare due to poor communication with British Airlines.  We had invited another couple with us and were quite embarrassed about how the additional things added up.  We did not know all of this until after the trip was purchased.  This was our 5th trip with GVV but it will be our last.However, I do want to say that Rebecca from GVV was as helpful as she could be and usually responded to our issues quickly.  I would suggest that you use airlines other than British airlines.  They were difficult and their schedules were crazy.  Who on earth wants a 12 hour layover at any airport?   We would have preferred flying into London and driving the rest of the way but that wasn’t allowed unless we wanted to pay almost $4000.  So instead one of days of “vacation” were spent in an airport.  I don’t usually do these reviews but I wanted to warn others who save their money for these trips that they can cost a lot more than the package indicates.

title: Mismatched Expectations on an Otherwise Nice Trip
text: Overall, the trip was pleasant and we enjoyed many aspects of the experience. The itinerary was well-planned in terms of the sights and locations visited, and we appreciated the efforts of the guide throughout the journey.That said, I believe the value of the trip was a bit misaligned with the expectations set during booking. There was significantly more walking involved than described in the trip materials, which would have been helpful to know in advance for planning purposes.Additionally, one of the buses we traveled on had a very strong mold and musty odor. It was a very unhealthy situation for all of the passengers on board, especially those with allergies or respiratory issues. While our guide did their best to arrange for a new bus, the bus company would not accommodate the request, which made that leg of the journey uncomfortable and concerning from a health standpoint.As for the accommodations, I would personally rate the hotels closer to three stars rather than the advertised four. One particular hotel had a nice main building that was featured in the promotional photos. However, the room we were assigned was in a separate, much older structure behind the main hotel—resembling more of a garage or storage space than a guest room. It was small, very aged, and not at all reflective of the quality shown online. This was disappointing and felt misleading.In summary, while the trip itself had enjoyable moments, a few adjustments in transparency around hotel quality, physical activity levels, and transportation conditions would greatly improve the overall experience and perceived value.

name: Douglas Frick
title: Don't Make Assumptions: Aggressive Itinerary, Questionable Logistics.
text: Overall I had a good experience, but I'd recommend any customer considering travel carefully reads all documents, and reviews and tests the schedule and questions the logistic before booking. I was surprised how aggressive the itinerary was, and there was one location that logistically made no sense.I accepted an invitation to book the same itinerary that my brother's family recently purchased. The booking experience was simple and the information provided did prove thorough and accurate. But were a couple disconnects from my previous experience and expectations that I'd advise other customers to carefully consider, especially if you aren't used to travel packages like this:  1) Seat Certainty: since the airline seat assignments are not confirmed until shortly before actual travel, I had to pursue my own additional coordination and significant cost with the airlines to be able to select seats to ensure I'd have a seat with my travel companion. Ultimately, that was wasted effort and cost, because the overnight/overseas flight was only half full, so there was plenty of flexibility within the cabin on the flight, but at booking you will not have an opportunity to select/secure your seat or upgrade without the extra coordination and additional cost.  2) Travel Insurance Limitations: I opted to purchased travel insurance, but did not carefully read the policy. I had assumed I could cancel and claim against the insurance up until departure, but that was not the case. Unfortunately, my fiancé did have a medical emergency the week of the trip and we were uncertain if she would be up for the travel, but upon closer review of the policy, I realized cancellations would have needed to be made 72 hours before departure, so ultimately the insurance did not provide the flexibility I would have expected for the cost, and in the future, I would not opt in to that service. This may all be very standard, I just assumed the coverage would be more flexible than it actually was. 3) Very Aggressive Itinerary: we covered a lot of ground between cities and I underestimated the amount of time we would be driving- on average 3 hours a day-which left little additional time to explore at destinations. But, I could have paid closer attention to the package details to have been better informed. The hotels were all clean an comfortable but they were not necessarily close to the day's activities which created a lot of seemingly unnecessary travel time and backtracking. For example, the hotel for night 2 was 90 minutes past the next morning's activity, which meant an hour an a half of backtracking to make that activity and the same duration back; so that hotel just made no sense. The extra travel time eliminated any chance for exploring the locale, and the hotel itself was the least special of all lodging; so that location for two nights was totally absurd and the low point of the trip. The other surprise was that my room overlooked a cemetery, not the scenic lagoon which seemed to be the draw. I was able to change rooms for a reasonable upgrade fee. If I could have edited that stay out of this itinerary and stayed closer to the next day's activities, my review would be higher. So overall a good, but not great experience. I would book with this company again, but I would pay closer attention to details.

name: Kate F.
title: Dublin was great, but GVV was challenging
text: Our visit to Ireland was ultimately great, and the hotel was better than expected (plus a great location between airport and downtown Dublin). But I will not use GVV again.The website is extremely challenging to evaluate different trip options, especially dates and flights. You have to continually backtrack screens and "start over." Also, the customer service is extremely frustrating until you get to the final booking agent - they're terrific. But the people prior aren't very helpful or pleasant. And know that the flights are booked somewhat separately, so that process is quite clunky.If you do choose to book w/GVV, buy the insurance. That saved us when we had to rebook for another date. That allows you to switch packages if needed, although not travel companions.I do not recommend the Scotland B&B package - that was our original trip, and it requires you to do hours of work to book the B&B's yourself. I thought it would be fun, but the booking site (separate from GVV) is very antiquated and time consuming. Plus, almost all decent/nearby B&Bs require an upcharge to the package cost.Overall, our trip was good, so if you book a straightforward package, you may be okay. But if you prefer helpful service, I'd advise another company.

The whole experience felt very curated for our group!We are already planning our next trip through Great Value Vacations, and I CANT WAIT!

title: I took my mom to Ireland

name: Diane D
title: Great Value Vacations is far from a Great Value!
text: Don’t use this agency unless you want to pay WAY MORE than what it would be if you just went directly to the hotel/airline/car rental agency and booked it yourself.  Our friends booked the exact same thing as our trip through Great Value and paid $600.00 LESS than we did!  Great value is NOT a great value and everything is non-refundable.  At least when you book yourself, you can usually cancel some aspects of a trip up until a certain date.  Not so with this agency.  So disappointing!  Never again!  I will book everything myself and do the research.To reply to Great Value’s reply below, I would have cancelled the whole thing with you if I could have.  The fact that you “allowed me” to cancel the car, yes you did and I consider that VERY lucky because the girl I dealt with told me they would do it for me this “one time” for this “one” aspect of the trip and that’s it!  As for knowing if I am comparing apples for apples, our friends went with us at the exact same time.  Same flight.  Same hotel.  We travelled together and they booked their trip a week after I booked mine and asked me the details of our trip and booked their exact same apples for apples trip.   I don’t normally write bad reviews.  But I had to tell people about this one because $600 more is a total rip off!  Furthermore, if you are going to pay that much more to use the agency, one would think they would provide as many details as possible about the trip you booked such as with said airline you should book any bags in advance because the day of your trip the pricing doubles.  I will say that we enjoyed our trip immensely.  The hotel was a little dated but good and the airline was stripped down to where they  charge for water but we knew that from doing research after booking.  Everyone was very nice at the hotel and the airline.  It simply wasn’t a good value is my only complaint.  I even went as far as to look up the flight and hotel on my own after I booked through Great Value and it was in fact much cheaper online.  So the extra cost goes to the agency at a hefty price tag.

name: Mel B.

name: Karen Ann Lavery
title: Hotels were unsafisfactory.
text: Referencing a trip that consisted of three days each in London, Paris and Rome. The hotels that we were assigned to were very much subpar  to hotels I usually stay in. First, they were located on the outskirts of the city center and required using a taxi or uber to get anywhere. This added up to quite an additional expense. Second,while they did have breakfast rooms, they did not have restaurants. Third, the breakfast offering were minimal and picked over by 9:00 a.m. even though they served breakfast until 10 a.m.  Fourth the hotel rooms, particularly in London, were tired and worn and needed upgrades. That hotel did not even provide a hair dryer, room safe, in room coffee maker or mini refrigerator.  While the location of the London hotel was in a decent area, the hotels in Paris and Rome were not.  They were in rundown, sketchy areas on dark side streets where gangs of teens and 20-somethings hung out on the street corners. We would not have been comfortable walking around even in daytime.  This was scary!!

name: Lauren Amaturo
title: I go to the GVV website first now before any other sites when planning a vacation
text: I have traveled with Great Value Vacations several times and I now go to their website to look for vacation packages before I make any plans to see what they have available because their vacation deals are always top notch. We most recently booked a trip to LA from NYC and stayed at the LUXE on Sunset Blvd. The hotel was amazing! Clean, exceptional service, friendly staff, a heated outdoor pool with cabanas, free breakfast every morning for FULL meals and free valet service. I have been to Iceland, Italy, Bermuda, San Diego and now LA with GVV and I can't wait to book my next trip soon!

name: Dr. Geoffrey D. Bentley
title: Portugal in April
text: Our experiences on this trip were varied, from excellent to mediocre!  Our flights, transfers and rail travel were great, no issues.  The stays we had in Porto and Lisbon were very enjoyable, other than some occasionally raining weather.However, this was our 4th GVV trip and the portion in Agarve Portugal was disappointing.  The hotel/resort was way out literally in the 'middle of nowhere'.  We normally like to walk around the cities/areas we visit, eat dinner at numerous restaurants and enjoy a few drinks.  This was NOT possible at this location as it was nearly a 2 mile walk to the nearest community.  We did have a rental car which was necessary to get to the Agarve region of Portugal, but I know there were other hotels in the various towns in this region that were closer to city central areas. You DO NOT want to drink and drive in Europe.  I don't feel GVV did enough research on this area prior to booking THIS hotel.Additionally, the Lisbon hotel was quite old and the rooms were small.  I have to question if it was really a 4 star property!Lastly, the rental car was necessary, but prior to someone booking this vacation, customers should probably be informed that the fees for rental car insurance are extremely high at this location.  It may have a bearing on whether one books this trip or looks for another option.

title: I don't know how the hotel is rated so…
text: I don't know how the hotel is rated so high, not happy with it at all. Does one of your employees actually go out and check the hotel out? Our bathroom leaked twice during out stay and got all over everything.  They ran out of different drinks many days.  They considered Jose Cuervo was top shelf booze, so it costs to drink it.  The sushi restaurant was extra so there were really on (2) restaurants.  I have been telling so many of my friends about GVV now I am not sure if I will continue with that.

name: TL
title: Needs Improvement
text: The idea of the experience was great, however its execution on the part of Great Travel Vacations can use some improvement. Furthermore, some of our experiences were not booked in a timely manner as promised and were only booked 1.5 weeks prior to our departure and I spent the entire week up to the day I arrived at my destination trying to coordinate new timing of an experience since what was booked was not feasible. All of these frustrating and stressful situations could have been avoided had things been more organized by GTV.

text: My family embarked on a Spring Break trip to Eastern Europe, “ Affordable Budapest, Vienna, Prague”. Everything started off well as expected until we traveled on our 2nd City in Vienna. Great Value Vacations was not available to respond and when they finally opened, they did not respond to the hotel for a couple of days. Luckily the hotel was not completely booked and we could book our own room with a credit card, even though we had already paid😡 This situation caused our reservation to be compromised and we were given a tiny room that barely fit 2 people let so e 3. We had to continuously call GVV and get the run around, worst customer service ever!! The reservation was finally paid, but of course GVV blamed the hotel… This does not help the travelers waiting around for hours  on their European vacation. We were not offered any compensation for an inferior room and have asked GVV several times for something. They actually asked us for pictures of the “Inferior Room” after we had vacated to the next leg of the trip.. unbelievable!! name: Luis
title: Watch for unexpected luggage fees & 11 hours of no hotel!
text: It appears the airline blames you, Great Value, and you’re saying it’s the fault of the airline.The airline reports since we were booked in group 6 boarding by you, we had to pay an extra $120 US dollars for each flight!Bottom line—you have a family of 4 as upset clients.The package purchased by us should have included all flights with a carryon option (which we would have paid upfront & rolled into the original price) instead of only some carryons included and other flights not—especially since the entry & exit of country visited are from two different locations, so the luggage allowance should be the same on all flights.In addition to this, our connecting flight to Cartagena was booked by you @ 10pm, but we had to check out of our hotel in Medellin @ 11am that day; were we to wander the streets with our luggage for 11 hours?These 2 events of booking some flights in which we needed to pay extra for our carryons, and 11 hours of ‘homelessness’ are unprofessional and show lack of research or knowledge of the travel industry, for which is why we purchased this package from you in the first place. We are extremely disappointed and disillusioned by Great Value Vacations, and hope you take the advice & suggestions to improve your company.
