name: Vlad Miller
title: Faulty Airline, broken app, no customer support
text: Embarking on what was supposed to be a festive journey from Amsterdam to Reykjavik on the 20th of December with my partner, who was wearing a leg brace, quickly descended into a farcical nightmare, showcasing a profound failure in customer service and technological reliability. The added complexity of navigating travel with a leg brace had prompted us to arrive even earlier, four hours before our flight HV 6887, to ensure that the airline was informed and accommodations could be made for comfortable seating. Despite this forethought and our efforts to communicate our needs, what unfolded was nothing short of a disaster.After checking in via their notoriously unreliable app the night before—a decision that would set the stage for our ordeal—we approached the gate, only to be met with a baffling and distressing issue. Our boarding passes, accessed through the very app provided by the airline, were flagged with an error by the gate agent. Rather than seeking a resolution or calling for supervisory assistance, we were marked as 'NO SHOW' right before our eyes, a decision executed with a cold click and no regard for our situation or the additional challenges posed by my partner's leg brace.This heartless action left us stranded, initiating a domino effect of frustration. Our subsequent quest for assistance plunged us into a Kafkaesque nightmare of customer service neglect. Calls to the airline resulted in a surreal exchange with an employee who chose silence over service, leaving us abandoned in our time of need. This ordeal forced us into an unplanned overnight stay, exacerbating the discomfort and challenges faced by my partner due to their leg brace.The following day, our encounter with Viggo, the airline's stand-in for customer support, shed light on the app's history of failures—a fact that, while acknowledged with apologies, offered little consolation for the loss of our holiday time and the physical discomfort endured.The airline's response to my formal complaint further exemplified their astonishing lack of accountability. Misdirecting their reply to my partner's email, they persisted in absolving themselves of any responsibility for the app's malfunction and, egregiously, disregarded EU regulation 261/2004, denying us the protections it affords to passengers in such distressing situations.This entire experience transcended mere inconvenience, morphing into a grievous neglect of passenger welfare and rights. The airline's blatant disregard for our predicament, especially in light of my partner's physical condition, and their refusal to offer any meaningful compensation, starkly illuminated the chasm between their professed values and their actions. Our ordeal, marked by a faulty app, abysmal customer service, and a disregard for passenger dignity, stands as a chilling indictment of an airline culture that seems to have lost sight of its fundamental responsibility to its passengers.

We cannot refund this, I understand that you faced a lot of inconveniences but this decision is final.I am so sorry.". As a I follow up reminding them that according to European regulation I am entitled to reimbursement for necessary items I get this response "Once more, I am writing to follow up on the refund of the new baby stroller you purchased.Well, as I told you before, we have our own rules and we need to follow them. That is the reason why we are not able to refund your baby stroller. I had to remove a number of other passengers' bags to get to our cases.I cannot recommend Greyhound under any circumstances (they are more expensive than other bus lines with clearly inferior service).

text: Hi Greyhound,My friend and I have used you to travel up the east coast for the past month. The general experience has been quite good, but has been lacking in a few areas. The bus A/C is very cold, especially when taking an overnight bus. I wouldn’t say that I usually take notice when a room is cold, but when trying to sleep in the greyhound it has required us both to wear three layers of clothes the whole way. This is not only because of the temperature, but also because of the A/C ventilation speed. It sometimes starts spitting air so much that the noise it makes is enough to keep you from sleeping. And this is all the uncontrollable A/C ventilation, if you want you can open even more vents, but I haven’t seen anyone use this feature, ever. Another thing that troubles me, is the bus leaking water inside the cabin when it rains. This has happened with more than one bus, where water comes in from both the windows and emergency exit dripping onto myself and other passengers. And if that isn’t enough the water also gets into the luggage storage, which has left our luggage completely drenched upon arrival. This I think is unacceptable as valuables like passports, driver licenses, clothes and shoes are left to be completely soaked, which is a problem when you have to use them after getting off the bus.Even though there has been some negatives there has also been positives. The drivers have always been nice and helpful and the bus has always gotten us to our destination on time, even though it has arrived at the pickup late a couple of times.I hope this was helpful insight.

text: Most honest review you'll probably ever read. First off, they do NOT do refunds for any reason, and you will only find this out IF you are able to reach a customer service rep. They may reimburse you with a voucher that is less than half the price of your trip. I ended up getting a 21.00 voucher for an $110 trip. Also, if safety and comfort are two of your concerns, PLEASE scrape up the extra money to ride RED COACH! Greyhound, especially in Tallahassee, has become a 💩show. The "new" location is outside on the corner of a very busy intersection. It is a hassle trying to get into the terminal, that it is also used for the city bus routes to go in and out. As I waited for my bus, I witnessed personally about 5 people get ran over by incoming traffic while trying to access the Greyhound. It is rumored as told to me by one of the GH work staff that the company's "new" owner, who lives in another country, purchased GH with a $1 bid. There are no plans to upgrade or improve its conditions until late 2028. Along the route, there are many other stops that have been turned into merely parking lots, even a few roadside stops, which in my opinion is very dangerous and unsafe, especially in extreme weather conditions such as rain, and currently snow. Most of the availability has been reduced to one route a day. Budget cuts are very noticeable and extremely DEGRADING to even someone who can barely afford a ticket. From a rider who used to be dedicated to Greyhound, I would rather drive or even use HITCH to get to my destination on trips where I just want to relax & dont feel like driving a long distance. Instead of GH being honest and admitting the company is failing and just simply merging or closing the business, like many failing post pandemic businesses, they would rather scapegoat the comfort of loyal clients to save themselves. I am not exaggerating when I say that my last trip with GH was HORRIBLE to say the least. The best terminal I have come across is in Jacksonville FL and this is only because it's terminal is privately owned, yet still scantily clad. If you don't mind having your trip ruined of diminished, by all means, GH is the way to go. Or if you are riding one way to a destination and just MUST make it by any means neccesary, maybe it is OK. But of you have any ounce of dignity and don't want to be waiting outside in wet, cold, frigid, or extremely hot in the summer conditions, please use other means of transportation. Many of the companies stay in business because of complacent sheeple who allow these things to continue or are scared to speak up, but the majority is rarely right.  Only good about GH is SOME of the drivers, that is only if you get on board with the right one. If you are considering riding with Greyhound, please consider better options if you can. It would not let me add a review without clicking on at least one star but even that is way too much.

title: Absolutely Abysmal Experience with…
text: Absolutely Abysmal Experience with GreyhoundI recently had the misfortune of dealing with Greyhound, and let me tell you, it was an experience I wouldn't wish on my worst enemy. From the moment I stepped into one of their facilities, the horror show began.First off, the cleanliness—or rather, the complete lack thereof—was nothing short of appalling. I encountered rats scurrying around the station, making it clear that Greyhound's standards for hygiene are somewhere below the sewers. It's one thing to expect a certain level of wear and tear in a bus station, but rats? That's a leap into the realm of neglect that's hard to overlook.But the physical environment was just the beginning of my ordeal. The customer service was another layer of disgust. When I contacted customer service to address my concerns, I was met with the kind of rudeness that would make even the most patient person lose their cool. The representatives I spoke with seemed trained in the art of dismissal rather than assistance. Each interaction felt like a personal affront; they treated me not as a customer, but as an inconvenience.And let's talk about their refund policy, or should I say, the policy designed to squeeze every last dime from you with no recourse. After dealing with delays, misinformation, and outright neglect, trying to get any form of compensation was like pulling teeth. Their policy is not just frustrating; it's predatory. They refuse to acknowledge their own shortcomings, leaving you out of pocket and out of patience.Even the in-person interactions at the kiosk were a travesty. The staff there were as helpful as a screen door on a submarine, providing misinformation and showing an attitude that could freeze water. It was clear they were there not to serve but to survive their shift, with customer satisfaction being the least of their concerns.In conclusion, my experience with Greyhound was a perfect storm of filth, disrespect, and financial exploitation. If this company were a person, it would be the kind of individual you'd cross the street to avoid. If you value your peace of mind, your health, or your wallet, steer clear of Greyhound. There are countless other options for transportation that won't leave you feeling like you've just been through the wringer.Avoid at all costs.

After the call I went online and booked the ticket for 4 days later, on Friday evening Jan 3, 2025.  As suggested by the bus company agent, I arrived at Lamoni Iowa at least 30 minutes ahead of the scheduled stop (arrived at 9pm and the stop was scheduled for 9:40m).  I waited patiently for 1hr 10 min, and at 10:10pm, I downloaded the Jefferson Bus Lines app and tracked (located) the bus that was supposed to stop - which was approximately 25 minutes past the Lamoni, IA exit!!!  At that point, I checked GPS and found that there was no way I could safely catch up with the bus at the next transfer station in Des Moines, IA, before the next bus departure time.  Therefore, at that point I could only head back home in frustration...needing to drive a vehicle to Miles City the next day.  I was provided incorrect information about the bus driver stopping at all listed stops on the itenerary (or perhaps the bus driver disregarded company policy and decided not to stop when required).  I should have been told that the bus driver may not stop, and I would drove the additional 1.5 hours to KC or just not booked the ticket!!!  TO MAKE MATTERS WORSE, GREYHOUND DOES NOT OPERATE A CUSTOMER SERVICE PHONE LINE AND ONLY ALLOW YOU TO REQUEST A REFUND ONLINE!!!!

text: Okay yall, so First. I paid extra for a seat to myself. Didn’t get that. Someone was actually in my seat. So my first bus ride was from the Norfolk bus station to the Raleigh bus station. At The Raleigh bus station, I wanna say about an hour and a half of being there, I just happen to look to my right and this man is literally getting tackled out of the door by two police officers, causing prompt confusion and panic from everyone at the station. There was then about 3 more police cars that pulled up promptly outside to help with the chaotic scene outside and to help tame the suspect. Still don’t know what that was about but very chilling and caused concern. THEN my bus mates that were accompanying me on the Atlanta Bus were delayed 4, nearly 5 hours, we barely got info why that was , it took other passengers fussing at the staff to tell us what was going on. One of the staff members literally responded to an angry customer by saying and I quote “I don’t care. I got a ride home, I don’t know about you.” We didn’t get any compensation whatsoever for it. Just straight disrespect and nasty attitudes from the staff. You can tell who really cares about their job and who’s just in it for the money. But we finally get on the bus to Atlanta, everyone’s settled in and minding their business and literally out of nowhere, a passenger cries out “He just stabbed me, y’all !” Everyone is so confused, panic quickly settles in and everyone is yelling at the bus driver to turn on the bus lights and pull over. She pulls over at a gas station and as the lights come on, the suspect and the victim are face to face, the victim’s back is dripping blood as he gets in a fighting stance to defend himself while the suspect has blood on his hand and is just cursing, threatening passengers , terrifying the babies who start crying and everyone on the bus. Thank God for two passengers who quickly jumped into action to separate the two and was able to get the suspect and the victim off the bus. The suspect walked off the bus and into the cold darkness which definitely, to everyone’s relief, lightened the tension on the bus and calmed everyone down. Now, How could this happen you may ask? Well I have a simple answer. They don’t do seat or bag checks. I don’t even recall them checking how much each bag weighed, they just allowed everyone to load their luggage underneath the bus. And for smaller bags like mine, they allowed onto the bus. It was absolutely disgusting and ghetto service. The police, the CSI and the ambulance showed up to ask questions, talk to witness, take pics of the crime scene and they the victim bandaged up and taken to the hospital to get Better treatment. I will NEVER be taking another greyhound in my life. PLEASE PLEASE PLEASE. Heed my warning, drive next time to ur destination with ur own vehicle. If you can’t, PLEASE GET ON A PLANE. And to top it off, all I was trying to do was make it back home to my husband. He paid for my entire fare. But couldn’t get any type of refund which was even more infuriating. No refund after our bus ride was delayed 4 and a half hours, no refund after ppl lives were put at stake by some crazy dude wielding a knife and no refund for missing my 3rd bus to Nashville because of that Atlanta delay. They wanted me to stay overnight to catch the next Nashville bus after all that waiting and waiting and everything I had already been through??? NO SIR AND NO MAAM. None of this was any of our fault, this was all greyhounds fault and we didn’t get any type of compensation NOR apology. They just don’t care ! My husband had to drive 5 hrs to Atlanta to comePick me up and 5 hours back to get back home to Kentucky. And they did not refund him even after explaining everything.  That was literally the last straw. That Really pissed me off. GREYHOUND SUCKS!!! And I’ll be darned if I ain’t write a review warning others or anyone considering this mode of transportation after all that I’ve been through. They can’t take accountability whatsoever and it was just a complete waste of money and time. So yeah yall, like I said, me personally I wouldn’t advise this way of transportation to anyone. Very disgusting and ghetto. DO NOT WASTE YOUR MONEY, Y’ALL! AND DO NOT WASTE YALL TIME. PERIODT. GOD BLESS !

name: Wendy Miller
title: connecting bus to get my elderly…
text: I spent 340$ to get my 65 year old disabled father on the bus from Modesto california, to Lewiston Idaho. He left Modesto ca on 12/27. He was supposed to have a lay over in Sacramento, ca; one in Portland, Oregon the following morning12/28; and one in pasco washington before arriving in Lewiston Idaho on the 28th at 8:15 pm. Before my father got to Oregon we got a notification stating that his bus had been delayed over night and he was going to be stuck in Oregon over night. He was told that he needed to contact customer service to change his ticket. It wasn’t automatically fixed for him. I had to call and be placed on hold to get his ticket for the following morning 12/29 out of Portland Oregon, in hopes there would even be room on the next bus out. I got his ticket figured out for him to leave on the morning of 12/29 from Portland Oregon to Lewiston Idaho. Then we had to figure out where he was going to stay over night in Portland while waiting until the following day get on the next available bus. All he had on him was 200$ cash. As you can imagine, no hotel is going to give you a room in cash these days. And to book him a room he would have had to have the card used to pay for the room when he got there.(Impossible as I had to use my card to purchase the ticket online, and again, he only had 200$ cash.) during this layover my father wasn’t the only person to get stuck over night with no way to get a room for the night. There was also a new father with his 14 month old baby that got stuck, along with several others who had no way to pay for a room for that overnight stay. Luckily, my dad offered whatever cash he had to a kind gentleman who was able to pay for a  room and willing to share an uber ride to a hotel. This kind gentleman took not only my disabled, elderly father; but also the new father with his 14 month old and shared a room with two beds with them for the night, while also making sure he and three other people made it back to the bus on time the morning of 12/29. My dad ended up offering him whatever cash he had as gratitude for not sleeping on the streets in Portland Oregon on a winter night. Now, fast forward to the morning of 12/29. The new day my dad was to get on his bus to Lewiston Idaho from Portland, Oregon.. somehow he ended up being let on the wrong bus as the driver  was going  to Idaho; However, he was going to Boise Idaho and did not specify that before letting my father remain on the bus without checking his ticket information. Now anyone who isn’t familiar with Idaho, it is a five hour drive one way from Lewiston to Boise. My father was trying to go visit his son for the holidays for the first time in six years. His son didn’t have a vehicle that would make it to Boise to pick our father up. When I spoke to the driver of the bus on the night of the 29, when my dad ended up stuck in Boise, the driver told me that my dad had asked if he was going to Idaho but didn’t specify which part of Idaho and he must have just let him stay on the bus without double checking his ticket. He then proceeded to tell me that he could get my dad back to pasco washington but from there he couldn’t guarantee that my dad would be let on the right bus to get him to Lewiston Idaho from there, so it would be best if I called greyhound once again to see if they could fix this mess. Not only that, but once again my disabled, elderly father would be stuck in Boise Idaho again over night in the middle of winter. This time he didn’t have cash to fall back on and he didn’t have anyone else who was able to help him. I was able to send 100$ through Venmo to my in laws who were able to call around and get him a room that he would have to find his own way to ( a 20 minute walk; for a disabled elderly, in the middle of winter in a town he new nothing about, while it’s raining and dark). Mean while my dad is now having anxiety attacks, that are causing him to break out in hives, his knees are giving out and he can barely walk, and he just wants to come back to Modesto to see his doctor. I ended up calling greyhound, frustrated because this is too much for any sane person to deal with; let alone  disabled elderly person who is just trying to get to his son one last time, and got his ticket to just return back to Modesto for further care from his primary care provider. My dad literally has bed sores on his a** because of the amount of time he spent on the bus from the night of 12/27 the morning of 12/31. The soonest I can get him in to see his doctor is on 1/6, and he is struggling. Mean while I requested a refund from greyhound only to be told that they could give me the portion of his ticket that wasn’t used (valued at 8$ and some change, but that it could only be used towards another ticket.) Not only did they LOSE my disabled elderly father in transit, but now they are refusing a refund for a trip that was supposed to be round trip 11 days total after literally turning my dads vacation into an ACTUAL NIGHTMARE

text: This was my son‘s experience this past Saturday, December 14th, 2024. He was on the Greyhound bus headed from Tallahassee to Jacksonville to catch his flight home. The bus driver stopped the bus and said you guys have 10 minutes to get off, go to the bathroom get a snack at the convenience store. About 6 to 8 people, some were students, got off the bus and went into the store. Six minutes passed and the bus driver started driving away. The people in the convenience store noticed that the bus was driving away, so they ran out, but the bus driver would not let them back on the bus! The students stood in front of the bus so that the bus couldn’t leave and one of the students called the police. The police came and the bus driver opened the door to talk to the police. The bus driver would not let the students back on the bus. She said it was against company policy. The bus driver said that they could get their luggage because otherwise it would’ve been theft if the bus driver took off with their luggage. The students grabbed their luggage and in doing so took my son‘s suitcase.  My son had $500 worth of clothing, toiletries & guitar accessories in there. He filed a missing luggage report, but I highly doubt he will ever get that back. I feel so bad for the students and other people that were left stranded in Live Oak, Florida for 2 hours!! It is a very remote area and very difficult to get an Uber or a taxi! Some of the students had to call the police and the police took them to the next bus stop in a prison transport van, which was completely dark inside. No lights on.  This bus driver’s behavior was absolutely unacceptable and very dangerous! She claimed that it was against company policy to open the doors to let the people back on the bus?? Is it also your policy to leave people stranded in the middle of nowhere alone without transportation?? I want to be reimbursed at least $500 for the contents of my son’s suitcase. It was an extreme hassle and insult to my wallet to have to go out and buy all new clothes, toiletries and guitar accessories for him. Also, it was pretty devastating for my son to have to see students left behind because of the bus drivers behavior. This all could’ve been completely avoided. This was also my son’s first greyhound bus ride, most likely his last, after this experience.

title: My experience was horrible! They gave away the extra seat I paid for in advance without giving me a refund & threatened to put me off the bus because I didn't want to give up the extra seat I paid for
text: My experience was horrible on my trip from Atlanta to Mobile on route 0602. The driver, Willie Dunbar (That's what he told me his name was anyway), was very rude and treated me like crap in front of everyone on the bus. At the last minute, he insisted that I had to either give up the extra seat I paid for or get off the bus for not cooperating, since the bus was overbooked and there were still people who needed seats. Since I paid for the extra seat, I explained that my paid seat shouldn't have been overbooked and that had to be an error on Greyhound's part. I was not getting off the bus and miss or delay my Christmas plans with my family, so he said I would have to call to get a refund after departure, as I would’ve missed the bus if I got off at that time to sort out a refund with the ticket counter. I called Greyhound while I was in route and the booking department supervisor told me they wouldn't  be able to authorize a refund for the occupied seat I paid for and I would have to submit a complaint and refund request online with the booking #, my name, and a description of the incident. Once he heard me on the phone with Greyhound, realizing he was wrong, he called me to the front of the bus. I asked for his name and he refused to give me his name until my final destination in Mobile. He eventually told me I could have the extra seat I paid for back after the next stop. He then told the man sitting in the seat I paid for to move to another available seat. STILL, my extra paid seat should've never been occupied for any of the trip and I shouldn't have been treated so poorly as a paying customer who had probably paid the most for one person to travel on that bus route. I paid the most for one person to travel, but was treated the worst. At the time of booking, I only bought a one way ticket and would prefer to book another double seat for a more comfortable experience on my 7 hour trip back to Atlanta but I don’t EVER want to experience the horrible treatment I endured on my way from Atlanta to Mobile. It is very bad business to offer customers the option to purchase an extra seat for extra comfort, take there money, but deny them what they paid for at the last minute, and treat them like trash in front of an audience, threatening to kick them off the bus for not giving up something they paid for without an immediate refund. It its a huge inconvenience having to write this complaint and having to wait for my money back, especially at Christmas when I could’ve used that money for something else. Please provide a partial refund for my extra seat since I had access to my extra seat for only half of my trip.

text: I have to say from the very beginning, we had no confidence in galahotels.com but we were very pleasantly surprised!In January this year, we booked to stay at a hotel in San Francisco for 4 nights. Too cheap and absolutely no prospect of getting our money back from the reviews.We emailed gala hotels who replied relatively quickly to say our booking would appear on the hotels system 72 hours before we were due to stay. The response wasn’t in the best of English as Galahotels is based in Turkey, so this added to our apprehension that it could be a scam. We looked up this policy and booking.com amongst others are the same, so didn’t feel totally fleeced. We were still worried though. Between January and September we contacted the hotel directly to see if they had heared of Galahotels.com or had a booming under our name. They hadnt. We stressed ourselves out so much by reading terrible reviews.September came, and I decided to book a hotel with free cancellation just in case everything went wrong. I contacted gala again, 3 days before we arrived. They replied and confirmed our booking was going ahead. We contacted the hotel directly who also confirmed our room was reserved for us. We didn’t believe it until we got there; and we got the key to our room! Also turns out, the urban tax fee was included in our price. So a room, for £600 including tax for four nights was probably the best bargain we’ll ever get!Had we not read such terrible reviews, and panicked, the whole experience would have been smooth and pleasant. Galahotels did nothing wrong but provide us with a great room at a terrific price. I probably wouldn’t book through them again, only because of how stressful the whole situation was - through no fault of their own. We were very surprised and understanbly more than happy that Gala came through! Just make sure you pay on a credit card!

title: Not a trustworthy company anymore
text: I would like to inform fellow travelers about a suspicious issue with Hotels.com. As a decade-long member, I have always considered this company to be reputable in securing the best hotel deals for clients until my recent experience. Hotels.com charged me $629 per night for a 3-star hotel that normally costs $207 per night. During a business trip, I booked my stay through Hotels.com a month in advance from 5/16/25 - 5/18/25 in Boston at the HYATT house in Boston, Waltham, a practice I have followed for years.During my 2-night stay, I was charged approximately $1400, which is significantly higher than the expected rate of around $400 if booked directly with the hotel. Upon bringing this price discrepancy to the attention of hotel manager Alex, I was instructed to contact Hotels.com, as the booking was processed via a third-party channel. I then contacted Hotels.com to request a price adjustment before checking out of the property.During my phone conversation with a Hotels.com manager, I was disappointed to find that they were unwilling to assist in resolving a problem I encountered. The manager stated that by agreeing to the price on their website and completing payment, I had effectively waived any right to a refund. This experience has led me to lose confidence in Hotels.com as a trustworthy third-party booking platform. As someone who travels frequently and has historically relied on Hotels.com for booking accommodations, I regret to say that I will be taking my business elsewhere. To avoid similar disappointments, I recommend that others verify hotel details directly before booking through Hotels.com.

title: ⭐☆☆☆☆ (1 star)
text: ⭐☆☆☆☆ (1 star)Booking through Hotels.com, you would reasonably expect some level of accountability or support when issues arise with a hotel reserved through their platform. Unfortunately, that was not the case when I encountered a serious problem during my recent stay at Hallmarc Studios in Port Arthur, Texas.Despite the fact that the hotel fraudulently charged my bank account $483.00 in error, which caused financial hardship and emotional distress, Hotels.com told me there was nothing they could do, as refunds are completely up to the hotel’s discretion. I contacted their customer service, hoping for advocacy or at least a sense of responsibility since I used their platform in good faith. Instead, I was told they could only relay the message to the hotel and could not intervene when the hotel refused to issue a refund.(See my full review of Hallmarc Studios below for more details on the incident.)Hotels.com’s role should go beyond just being a middleman. If a hotel listed on their platform engages in unethical behavior, they should step in to protect their customers, not hide behind policies. This experience has made me completely lose confidence in booking through Hotels.com. If they cannot support their users when things go wrong, then what value are they really providing?⭐☆☆☆☆ (1 star)I had a reservation at Hallmarc Studios from May 2 to May 4, booked through Hotels.com. Upon arrival, check-in was smooth, and the room charge of $165.83 was correctly billed to the card on file. Unfortunately, what followed turned an average stay into an incredibly distressing and financially disruptive experience.At 5:15 AM, I received a fraud alert from my bank notifying me that an additional charge of $483.00 had been made by Hallmarc Studios. This charge was completely unauthorized and absolutely shocking. I immediately contacted my bank’s fraud hotline and was told that the charge had been reversed, but due to it being a weekend, I would not see the refund for 3 to 7 business days.Concerned, I contacted the front desk right away and was informed by the clerk that the charge was a mistake and had been refunded. When I expressed how this unexpected withdrawal caused an overdraft on my account and placed me in a serious financial bind, the response I received was dismissive at best. I explained that I have limited financial resources, and this error significantly impacted my well-being, triggering both anxiety and depression. The clerk repeatedly brushed it off with, “Mistakes happen,” showing no genuine concern or empathy for the situation.Later, I discovered from the manager that the charge had been made by mistake by her own daughter, who works at the hotel. It became clear that there was an effort to downplay and cover up this serious error rather than take accountability. name: Cory & Katie Freeman
title: A Lesson was Learned
text: I booked two rooms through Hotels.com, and when I called the hotel the day before our arrival, I was told that only one room had been booked. The hotel said it was a problem with Hotels.com so I spent an entire day trying to sort it out with various customer service agents. (The hotel was not answering their phone for the customer service agents in a timely manner. The hotel is not free from blame in all of this.) The last one I talked to said I could cancel the reservation through Hotels.com and she would explain to the hotel that we would book directly through the hotel so that we didn't get charged for the Hotels.com booking. The next morning I got an email from Hotels.com saying that our refund request had been denied, and oh well, that happens quite often. I would not have cancelled if I were going to be charged for extra rooms at a hotel I was already planning to stay at! I called the hotel and found out they denied the refund because the cancellation had never come through, so there was nothing to refund at that point. So even though Hotels.com said my booking was cancelled, the hotel said I still had a reservation, so I proceeded with the vacation as was originally planned. I learned a valuable lesson: when you use Hotels.com and there is a problem with your reservation, you will be left in the lurch. From now on, I will always book directly with the hotel. (Which turns out, would have been cheaper.)

text: Expedia and hotels.com are a scam. Although I have had successful bookings with them over the last decade, they are now horrible. On 03/28 I went onto the hotels.com  app to reserve a room. The next day I emailed hotels.com for an update and they emailed back saying I cannot get my refund. They offered me $25 instead. I paid $305 for a one-night stay at the Omni Hotel at Centennial Park. I did not accept the cheap $25 refund from hotels.com Expedia and hotels.com are both the same company. text: Deeply Disappointed – Hours of Stress Over a Cancelled BookingI’ve just had one of the worst customer service experiences I’ve ever encountered with Hotels.com. title: Hotels.com SUCKS!!!!!
text: I book this place on Hotels.com, right? Figured, easy, done, no problem. But oh, the problem was waiting for me when I got there. First off, the hotel is right next to some abandoned building that looks like the setting for a horror movie. Like, I half expected to see a guy in a hockey mask lurking around. Then, some sketchy characters start wandering nearby, and my gut is screaming, absolutely not. I get the full-body heebie-jeebies.Now, it's just me and my 11-year-old daughter, and I’m not about to play “Will We Get Murdered?” tonight. So we nope outta there real quick and drive to the next town, where we find a hotel that doesn’t look like it’s about to be on the news.And you’d think, oh, Hotels.com will understand, right? Maybe a refund? Nope. Not even a partial one. Just a robotic “sorry, it’s policy” while I’m out here driving at night trying to keep my kid safe. No sympathy, no flexibility, just too bad, so sad.Oh, and let’s talk about the sneaky little fees at every other place I stayed. Because apparently, Hotels.com loves a good game of Gotcha! when it comes to your wallet. Between the sketchy locations and the headache-inducing fine print, I can’t recommend this circus.Honestly? Just book directly with the hotel. Or better yet—wing it. There are a million hotels out there, and at least if you roll up in person, you can take one look and go, yeah, no thanks before handing over your credit card. Save yourself the stress. Trust me.

name: kunde
title: Not trust the information received from Hotels.com
text: Had made a booking for 5 nights at a hotel, but wanted to cancel during the stay. Contacted therefor Hotels.com to ask if it was possible to cancel the reminding days of my stay without paying. While I was chatting with Hotels.com they contacted the hotel, and Hotels.com confirmed to me that I just had to pay for one night and could check out the following day without paying for more than that night. (Have got this in writing from Hotel.com) When I checked out the next day, I needed to pay for all 5 nights. This should be a case between hotels.com and the hotel, but seems like hotels.com is not able to support and the info given is nothing to trust.

name: Ksa Ksa
title: Stay away. No customer service
text: I ordered a quick stay, but with the wrong date 9th to 10th insted of 8th to 9th march. I contacted hotels.com 4 minutes after booking, and it was apparently impossible to fix. If I cancelled i would recive a «punishment» of paying anyways. They blamed hotel policy. Hotel said this was all hotel.com rules, so that was bull… On chat with hotels.com thay just ignored me. Very unprofessional. I have used this site many years in and out of my country. This kind of service made me delete my account today.

name: Julia
title: I will never use Hotels.com again
text: I will never use Hotels.com again. We booked a hotel stay and as soon as I booked I realized the date was off by one day. I called to change the reservation and the customer service agent was reasonably helpful. I received verbal confirmation that the change was all set and that my card would be charged a small amount for the difference in cost, which I approved. Fast forward several weeks to check in day. I called the hotel ahead of time to ask for an early check in. That's when they told me they  had canceled the reservation because I was a no show. Long story short, Hotels.com never updated my reservation, and refused to pay for the new hotel stay. While they did help us find a new hotel, to avoid paying very high last minute rates, we stayed in a hotel much farther from downtown than we wanted. I did receive a refund for my stay, however, it was very unnerving to be on vacation and realize we had no hotel that night.

text: The worst customer service and service in general

name: Mathias Andersson
title: Terrible service and scam vibes
text: Terrible service where they do not let you make changes or cancel bookings if you make a mistake when booking.

name: Jimmy Cinquemani
title: Booking a room that doesn’t exist..
text: Made a booking on the hotels.com app. When I arrived at the hotel, I was informed by the manager that there was no room available and that he didn’t know how this had happened. I got the run around from the hotels.com phone system, then had to go to the online chat to speak to someone. Shockingly enough after an hour of back and forth (it’s now nearly 1am) they finally call the hotel to be told the same thing I told them, for some reason the guy was on the phone for 10 minutes with the hotel telling them to give me a room, to which the manager kept repeating that there were no rooms at all. After another 30 mins of online chat they simply apologise and tell me that I will receive a refund in 7 business days. I’m waiting for another 3-5 minutes for the “supervisor” to come online as I’d like to make a complaint… Hotels.”com”/ Expedia are shocking and overpriced and if they make a horrendous mistake all they’ll do is apologise and give you a refund a week later, quite what good that is for me having to sleep in my car tonight I don’t know…

name: Sal
title: The new "Hotels.com" doesn't care if…
text: The new "Hotels.com" doesn't care if you're been a loyal gold member for 5 years, now they won't process refunds if they don't have to. You can't contact them unless your in USA, you can't even reply to an email they send you. This business has gone downhill since the amalgamation and I'm less likely to book through a third party anymore. Most hotels prefer you book directly to avoid fees lost

name: Chris Darwin
title: I booked hotel Jineswari
text: I booked hotel Jineswari, Kuta in Bali for 1 night. when I arrived at Jineswari, they said they dont have any confirmation on booking. Hotels.com charged me for 1 night and again I had to pay the same amount of money over there. On top of that, hotels.com is not willing to reimburse the month. So, basically I paid 2 times to day 1 night at Jineswari. Not easy to communicate hotels.com and worst experience of my life. Will never use hotels.com in the future.

name: PJ P
title: Chat option is little help
text: Chat option is little help.  Questions not answered.  Far too long a wait (not waiting in queue of 13.......)

name: Laura D.
title: Booked a non refundable room through…
text: Booked a non refundable room through hotels.comWeeks later the room booking is not on my app- nowhere to be found. The online chat help couldn’t find it either. They had taken my money so I contested it with Amex. I also booked the same room on the same night with a different provider. I’ve used hotels.com for at least ten years on their loyalty program- no longer.

name: Alexandra
title: no customer service
text: I've been trying to contact Hotels.com but there is no phone or email address on their website.I am looking at booking a hotel they advertise but the website doesn't let me book, it says link broken.I wish Hotels.com had a customer service to sort this out!

name: Kurt
title: BEWARE OF HOW YOU MAKE A RESERVATION AY…
text: BEWARE OF HOW YOU MAKE A RESERVATION AT DAYS INN AND HOTELS.COMFor a $350.00 reservation, Days Inn, Wyndham Hotels and Hotels.com has lost a customer for life. How dumb is that.I made a reservation at the Days Inn Salado, Texas for my son’s high school sports event. Unfortunately, he got injured so cannot attend. I logged into Hotels.com to cancel my reservation and got a message that the reservation is non-refundable because I tried to cancel at 4pm when the refund deadline was 3pm that same day. I called the local hotel and they said I needed to call Hotels.com as that’s where I made the reservation. While explaining the situation to the Hotels.com rep, she put me on hold to call Days Inn for an “exception”.  After a slight hold I was told that my exception was denied. So I tried to call Days Inn corporate and there is no way to speak to a live person. I simply got a virtual assistant that said I needed to call Hotels.com. Lastly, I went to the Days Inn Facebook page. Not to post or slam as I prefer to give businesses a chance to do the right thing. The Days Inn rep responded quickly asking if I was granted the exception. I responded no and got a message from another rep who said I didn’t qualify for a refund. Now they won’t respond.Here are my gripes and why you may want to choose a different, more customer centric hotel brand and reservation website.1) Hotel.com displayed a message that I wasn’t being charged now which gave me the impression that I would pay at the hotel.  Nope. I was charged.2) Neither Days Inn or Hotels.com were willing to do anything.  No full or partial refund or even a future credit. They basically stole my money.3) I cancelled within an hour of their deadline due to my son’s injury which was 3 days before my check in date.  They make the deadline at 3pm in the middle of the day.4) The Hotels . Com and Days Inn processes make it impossible to get to the correct people to resolve any issues.So I am out $350.00. Lesson learned. But hopefully they won’t steal anyone else’s money.

name: Kate
title: Utterly useless, no help whatsoever
text: I used hotels.com to book a business trip and I have not been able to claim back my trip because they refuse to give a VAT receipt and the hotel don't have one either.  I'm out of pocket because I used Hotels.com rather than booking direct.  DO NOT USE FOR BUSINESS TRIPS!

name: Dakhi
title: Not helpful at all .Would not recommend
text: We booked hotel with hotel.com and I am holding membership but lately we are having a lot of issues and with regret to say that there customer support is not good at all .We had health issue and ask for the refund but not able to get refund but on top of that they did not respond before my check in,if they have said no before that I could have asked my friend to go and stay overnight there but they took so long to respond and we lost money, before that we booked the hotel and on website it’s saying pay at the hotel and we had massage that they cancelled our booking because we didn’t paid so we had to find another hotel at night and paid double the money for different hotel.We lost nearly £200 because of hotel.come.As whole family and friends we were been booked hotel with them for last probably 10 years and in this 2 months we had really bad experience with them and they do advertise that plan do change and they are there to help but with the regrets they are not helping when we had health issues and had to cancel our trip short and provided them the proof of our flight changes details as well and few days before as well.

name: Bubbly
title: Avoid
text: Avoid. I used to book all my hotels on Hotels.com as they had a good reward system but things seem to be going down the drain and the reward system is not half as good in comparison. Today I realised the information (about the hotel I booked) was inaccurate on the system. It states that you need to contact the hotel one day inadvance for check in (I messaged the hotel through Hotels.com 3 days in advance and repeated my message one day inAdvance) and never received any reply. We tried to call the hotel number indicated on Hotels.com and all calls failed). We had to go on google maps to find the hotel’s accurate phone number, which was a mobile phone number. I went on the Hotels.com app to complain about the check-in issue and the chat bot was useless. Finally, after several attempts the woman at the hotel answered the phone and said it was her day off. She wouldsend the information the following morning, which she did not do. She said she does not receive the information from hotels.com and that hotels.com is responsible for the information on the system. The receptioncloses at 4pm and not, as indicated on hotels.com at 6pm. She did not have my contact information either.A leisure holiday that I booked for my husband’s birthday is now becoming sostressful and unreliable. Also, Hotels.com never indicates clearly on the receipt if breakfast is included at booking so, when you book a long time in advance it is difficult to remember what is included, or not. So basically, you are supposed todouble check with each hotel if it is included or not, just after booking, to keep a written track. I think it is time to look for another booking platform.

name: Angus
title: Don’t trust this company with your money
text: Booked a hotel via Trivago. They took an immediate deposit after staying on their website no card payment wound be taken. Their live chat service claimed they had no complaints service and tried to gaslight my concerns. Avoid at all costs. This is a bad business. They did the same to a colleague.

name: customer
title: Swirling the drain
text: Booked 4 nights and added the booking protection insurance for an additional charge.   As luck would have it, My guest needed to leave a day earlier.  The bill was paid in advance, of course.   I call the hotel to get a credit for the day not used  and they refer me to hotels.com.  I contact hotels.com and get directed to “request a claim” which requires jumping through hoops with a lot of unnecessary information.  Clearly, these scammers expect people will just give up on the refund.   I file the claim and have heard nothing about 1 week later.  Hotels.com was my go to, but quite frankly, I will never use these scammers again.   They intentionally set the system up to separate people from their money.  I am flushing this company so they are swirling the toilet drain.  I have no tolerance for thieves.  Use them at your own peril.

name: Mark Coulam
title: Room bookings cancelled last minute… twice
text: Twice I have booked rooms 18months in advance only to have my rooms cancelled just before I am due to stay. Their ‘help desk’ is extremely poor, based in the US and don’t want to help you, I would avoid this broker like the plague. Book direct with the hotels.

name: jjh4yb
title: Hotels.com's hotel description was a work of fiction
text: I recently stayed in what was described as a four star hotel in New Delhi.The room was clean and once in there I felt safe, the hotel also had wifi and the room an ensuite complete with cold shower.There were no other facilities and the advertisement is best described as a work of fiction.My big issue is that after reporting the issue, Hotels.com and presumably their other brands continue to advertise the hotel with the same advertisement as was used to dupe me.I have been promised a full refund, which at the time of typing, I'm still waiting for, however I really want the confidence that when I book a hotel, it will be as described and I struggle to even describe this collection of rooms as a hotel.The customer service philosophy  of hotels.com is sadly lacking. I complained and was offered £25 of loyalty points, which they increased to a full refund, however they just don't grasp or acknowledge that I want assurance that they are trying to stop such bad advertising. This assurance has not been offered in any meaningful way. But apparently I'm one of their most valued customers!

name: Rob Han

The hotel would not change the room but brought up a mattress and put it on the floor.Hotel.com would not support the misrepresentation of the website and would not help us get the $550/night room we paid for.

title: Nanu Resort Goa using wrong location to get customers!

Booked a hotel (Nanu Resort and Spa) which said it was 3.6 miles (used search for closest hotel) from GOX Airport Goa.When the hotel was closer to 20 miles from the airport.Tried to claim back the fee through Hotels.com and they didn't want to know. Very quick to take your money but very slow on assistance!!!

name: Ivan Rivera
title: Did not stand by their own advertised policy
text: I contacted Hotels.com the first day of the reservation for refund of 50% as per the Hotel Dorado Gold Bogota policy as shown in Hotels.com. name: BB
title: DO NOT waste your money with Hotels.com

They have terrible customer service and after many hours on the phone, I was told the insurance company is a third party and they are not responsible for my wasted money.

name: wild bill

Hoping I will vomit all over the front desk and tell them to contact Travel Guard/Hotels.com if they don't like it.

name: George Mendes
title: Hotels.com’s Customer Service is a Joke
text: Hotels.com’s Customer Service is a JokeI recently had a terrible experience with Hotels.com, and their customer service made it even worse. After reaching out with a legitimate complaint, I received a generic, copy-paste response that still had unused boilerplate text in it—proving they didn’t even bother reading my issue.Even after I pointed out their lack of effort, they sent another robotic reply, proving they’re just running through scripts instead of actually helping customers.I did get a chargeback (which was rightfully owed), but Hotels.com made it clear they won’t go above and beyond for customers—no matter the situation. If you have any problems with a booking, expect to get ignored, dismissed, or hit with a generic template response.A company that doesn’t care enough to even proofread their own customer service replies is not one I’d trust with my travel plans again.#Hotels.com #CustomerServiceFail #DoBetter

name: john
title: Great cashback but annoying adverts.
text: If you use a cashback website which offers a discount at Hotels.com, you get a better deal than going direct.  Those discounts are bigger outside the peak travel months in order to drum up business.  Hotels.com paid my cashback of £38 within a week of my return from the trip which I had booked.  That's great - some companies don't pay up!  Just one more thing: Hotels.com adverts on a certain well-known video-sharing site are annoying - I don't want a boutique townhouse with dust-collecting 'antiques' in every room...grrrrhhhh!

name: Em
title: Hotels.com will not help you only keep your money
text: To join all the other negative reviews…Same experience. I contacted them to move a hotel night due to an emergency hospital admission. I was forced to share personal medical documents on the promise of assistance. They then claimed they could not contact the hotel, the 24 hour London Heathrow airport hotel, to confirm my date change.They now want me to book, and pay, for another night at the hotel, in order for them to refund me, instead of just doing what they promised at the time.I will now use them as a search engine only and book my hotels direct. They hide behind not being able to contact the hotel without trying.Hotels.com used to be worth it for the free night every 10, now it’s a paltry ~ 1.6% per booking. Not worth the hassle when you do have a problem, especially a medical emergency. I do not need the stress of dealing with them at a time when I should be healing. Frankly nobody needs their non existent customer service at any time.Do not believe them if they say they will contact the hotel and sort it for you. They will not.

name: Catherine
title: Customer service don't listen
text: Customer service don't listen. You go in circles as they don't understand what you are saying and very little help atall when things go wrong. Absolute nightmare to deal with

name: Andrew Wood
title: hotels.com withheld agreed refund from hotel
text: I had to cancel a hotel booking within five minutes of placing it. Hotels.com refused any refund; when I contacted the hotel directly, they agreed a full refund within minutes and without fuss; but hotels.com still refused to pay it, saying they were unable to reach the hotel (I was able to several times, the hotel were very responsive).It took me a great deal of chasing to finally get them to agree.Have cancelled my hotels.com account and will be closing my Expedia.com account as soon as I am able

name: Laura P
title: Scam and terrible customer service
text: This company has scammed me and lied - avoid at all costs. I made a booking and it took the payment, then sent a confirmation to me for a date with the incorrect month, and now the booking doesn’t show on my account so I can’t amend it using their virtual chat feature. When I finally managed to speak to an agent by trying every possible combination of answers on the virtual chat until it worked, they lied and said they’d spoken to the hotel and the hotel refused to correct the date or refund us. I spoke to the hotel minutes afterwards and they said they’d never spoken to hotels.com and were very happy to change the booking, and they emailed me to say this. I forwarded it to hotels.com and now it’s gone silent and I can’t get a response. They are clearly trying to take the money for themselves and it’s causing a huge stress on my honeymoon. I will never use them again and urge others to use booking.com or another company instead (not Expedia because this company is linked to them).

name: Alan Marsden
title: The hotel I booked did not exist at the…
text: The hotel I booked did not exist at the stated address- it was a private house. I quickly had to find new accommodation late at night. Hotels.com online help was hard to find, cumbersome and generally unhelpful.When all is well, Hotels.com is great.When something goes wrong, their support is weak or unavailable.Very disappointing.

name: Kathi Moore
title: Settings are ridiculously NOT user friendly
text: I have booked hotels around the world thru this app and love the discounts and rewards points. However, I am extremely frustrated that you cannot change your email address!  My old one expired and I have no access. Customer Service said I’d have to cancel my acct. and open a new one. What?!! So all confirmations, etc. are no longer accessible to me. If I get a new acct. I lose all my history…

name: IXUS
title: Terrible experience
text: In keeping with many online companies engaged in "enshitification" Hotels.com have rejigged their order confirmation process to herd people through their app.As such, confirmation emails no longer come with your itinerary attached ready for you to print out and show. Instead every attempt to see your booking directs you to a webpage, which invites you to sign in to the app.Worse, hotels.com seems to have implanted something in their emails which prevents you forwarding them onwards to another email address.The whole process becomes time consuming and frustrating.The message is clear from Hotels.com, they want to own you through their app. This is precisely the sort of thing I run a mile from.  I have no idea what the booking number is. I'll just have to hope the hotel in France keeps good records. I won't be using hotels.com again.

name: Mrs T E Leadbitter
title: Terrible customer service, avoid at all cost
text: I recently had a cottage booked for a weekend away in York, however the owner contacted me 4 days before advising me that there was an issue with the log burner that he was unable to get fixed before my stay, and as it was unsafe he requested that I cancel my booking as he was unable to do it from his end. The booking was actually on a non-refundable basis but the owner said he would confirm to them that it was cancelled at his request and they should give me a full refund. My refund was denied by them, I tried contacting them initially on the chat bot that was not fit for purpose as it is pre-programmed with answers and goes round in circles with no solution, I have sent 4 or 5 e-mails to customer services as has the owner. I have had an e-mail forwarded to me by the owner in which they have asked him to confirm that he instructed me to cancel, and asking him if they should refund me, his reply was very detailed and confirmed that yes he does agree to a full refund as not my fault. At no point have I had a single reply or acknowledgement of any of my e-mails and at this point 2 weeks after starting the correspondence about the cancellation I have also recieved no refund. This is shocking customer service, and for a company of this size they really need to get their act together. I have used them for years, but never been in this situation before of being asked to cancel a booking already paid for, but I will not be using them again, and I will continue fighting for a refund, be aware there are better booking sites out there!

name: RobWilton
title: You cannot trust Hotels.com
text: I booked a hotel for two nights in Delhi, with Hotels.com, well before arriving in Delhi. I phoned The Woodapple Residency before check-in and as soon as I had bought a sim card on arrival Delhi. I told them I was on my way. They told me that they had sold my room to someone else!Hotels.com customer service apparently contacted the hotel after I reported this on my return to the UK.Then came the emails that made no sense whatsoever and were even comical. They said I was asking for a refund when (thankfully) I had selected the "pay at hotel" option. Then they said I had asked for compensation (which I had not) and the hotel would not pay any.They just completely ignored that I had suggested that the Woodapple Residency in Delhi should be removed from their listings to save other travellers the trauma of having nowhere to stay after booking there.Avoid Hotels.com at all cost. One star says it all.

name: Rosemary
title: Horrible company
text: Horrible company. Horrible policies. Worst customer service I’ve seen in my life. Do not book thru them, they are useless, if you have any issue they simply don’t help. I can’t find a single reason why it will be helpful to do any booking they them. Stay away from this company

name: Freya Mehta
title: Awful experience - had to change hotels

We contacted hotels.com asking for a refund, as the hotel suggested they would be able to help accommodate this.Hotels.com have sent us the same generic message stating that they could not get through to the hotel. We managed to get through but they still couldn’t.It’s a joke that hotels.com partner with companies they cannot apparently get through to! We are now out of pocket by at least £1500 given we had to find another hotel last minute, as we would not stay where we were.I would never advise using hotels.com

name: Sophie Besgrove

name: Alexa

name: Dean Ayling
title: Sleeping on the streets in Cyprus
text: I booked a holiday to Cyprus on this site, we landed at Larnaka on the 13th of December. It was just a stop over for a week before we went to Saudi Arabia to watch the boxing between Tyson and usyk. We got in a taxi to the hotel and it was closed. It was to late to get another Hotel so me and my friend had to sleep by the bins alnight. I tried to complain via the app but it wouldn't let me put anything on there. ie photos were we had to sleep or a complaint.

name: Jeffrey Courrier
title: Hotels.com refuses to refund reservation when guesthouse had no room available
text: Do not use hotels.com! I made a reservation and drove more than an hour away from town because everything else was full. name: Katrina Lewis
title: False advertising of hotel, no refunds.
text: Paid for a hotel in Rome when we arrived, it was nothing like described. Hotels com wont do anything, and when I wrote an accurate review, that review was also declined, so there are no accurate reviews for the property. No wonder the reviews made it out to be better than it was.Have used hotels.com before, but this will be the last time, as they clearly do not look after customers, and don't get their money back, even when a hotel has been falsely advertised, and it is impossible to stay there.

name: Yawara Music

name: DPayne
title: I hate to even give this site a star
text: I hate to even give this site a star.  We reserved a room at a hotel in VA Beach. They would have taken the $ I'm sure.This company is the worst... I didn't read reviews prior to booking - lesson learned.

name: K Senior
title: SCAMMERS - unhelpful liars cost me 6k more
text: I booked a water bungalow in theMaldives riu palace for my family for 6 nights. My son was 13 at the time of travel. I was quoted 7528.19 dollars for a 6 night trip to include local taxes and domestic transfer for 2 adults and 1 child. I have the booking receipt and booking email.On arrival at the hotel I was informed that the booking had been made in an infant not a child by hotels.com whilst we could stay in the same room I would have to pay the difference for my sons all inclusive,I was absolutely shocked to have an invoice pushed under my door for 12099.18 just a few hours later. A huge increase whenThe original room rate booking was 866.01 per night.  The invoice has increased the room rate for 2 adults to 1105.18 (552.59 per adult per night) plus an additional 487.50 per night for my son= a total of 1592.68 per night. A huge and unjustified increase of 726.67 per night for my sons food and drink. Nearly double and the same cost of a water bungalow to himself!! In addition the full transfer amount has been added-  776 dollars per person ( x3)  when our booking included a 790 dollar payment towards transfers. The local taxes have also doubled from 6 to 12 dollars per person per night.hotels.com refuse any responsibility for the error and have accused me of forging the email booking confirmation or lying deliberately about my sons date of birth which is nonsense. denying all responsibility and making no contribution.There staff are rude and unhelpful I will never ever use them again.

name: Richard
title: New loyalty programme scam
text: New loyalty programme from 10% (1 free night in 10) to 2% rewards (OneKey Cash or some b**lsh*t). They lost me as a customer, I will intentionally now use their search function then book direct BYE BYE!

name: Bruno
title: I booked a hotel that DOES NOT exist!
text: On January 9th, 2025, I booked a hotel through Hotels.com for a stay at The Elm House Hotel in Hawick, Scotland. Upon arrival, I discovered that the hotel was permanently closed. This critical information was not disclosed on the Hotels.com platform at the time of booking. Consequently, I was left stranded, forced to find alternative accommodations at additional cost and under stressful circumstances.After contacting Hotels.com, they acknowledged the error and credited 85 One Key Cash points to my account. However, these points were insufficient to cover the expenses I incurred, and they have since been redeemed for another reservation. I requested a full refund to my original payment method, as well as compensation for the unexpected expenses, but my requests were denied.The credit of One Key Cash points does not compensate for the original payment made for a service that was never rendered.The additional expenses I incurred as a result of this mishap remain unresolved.The lack of oversight in allowing a permanently closed property to remain bookable reflects poor platform management and directly caused this incident.

name: Key Property
title: Crooks
text: I had a booking for 3 nights in December my father died suddenly a couple of days prior to arrival, I contacted the hotel and asked about a deferment/cancellation of my booking as it was not approriate for me to travel, no reply from the hotel whatsoever.Upon Hotels.com recommendation they suggested cancelling the booking so the hotel could resell the room which I duly did and sent them a copy of the death certficate (which was registered on the intended day of arrival).My booking was quickly resold and the hotel was full, however they refused to refund my booking! So essentially they resold the same room twice, and kept the money, what sort of shady disgusting business practice is this? Are you so short of a couple of quid that you need so screw over a greiving potential guest!Nothing short of a low down disgusting bunch of crooks & thieves!!My account is deleted and will never use this shower again

name: Josh Nelson

text: I booked two hotel rooms for the Olympics in Paris in a hurry. Without realising it, they had jacked up their prices fourfold. Horrible business. Genuinely horrible.

name: Andy P
title: Deeply disappointing customer service.
text: My wife and I were to stay at the Petersham hotel for our Wedding Anniversary on the 22/12/24 following a tough few months it was a real treat we were looking forward to.  Unfortunately our daughter became unwell the day before our stay and we were not comfortable leaving her following a number of hospital visits over the last few months.  I called the hotel to explain the situation and see if I could amend/cancel the booking and was told I need to contact the company I had booked it through, hotles.com.This proved to be extremely difficult and frustrating a process, hotels.com only have a customer support web chat which appeared not to work.  I attempted to use this to contact them on at least 3 occasions on the 21/12/24 but each time the chat timed out without any reply form an agent.  Finally on the morning of the 22/12/24 I tried several more times with the customer support web chat and got through to an agent, who then called the Petersham hotel.  Disappointingly we were told nothing could be done regarding the booking and that it would be cancelled.I feel deeply frustrated and let down by both the Petersham Hotel and Hotels.com.  For two businesses focussed on customer service this experience has showed a total lack of just that.So should you be looking to make alterations to your booking in the future be very wary!

I’m upping the stars to 3

name: vl
title: The Seymour Arms, Blagdon, Somerset
text: Booked two double bedrooms, each with single occupancy for two nights at the The Seymour Arms in Blagdon, Somerset.The rooms were spacious and the beds comfortable. When we arrived and before we were allowed to bring  our luggage in, we were asked to pay for the stay. On arrival, the rooms were freezing cold, the heating was off, the window frames in each bedroom were completely rotten with some of them sporting spider webs hanging off the frames. A few black tea bags, Nescafe [with clumps of coffee] and milk were provided on arrival. None of these were replaced during our stay; there was no room service and no breakfast. Each room cost in excess of £100.00 per night. Given the "service," the state of the rooms, and no breakfast, the price was outrageously high.

name: Priscilla K.
title: Roaches, Mold, Rust, Health Hazzard and Very Dirty
text: Extended Stay America Select Suites - Tampa, FL - Airport - Memorial Hwy.This hotel is contaminated,nasty, filthy, and dirty because management fails to do their job. The front desk manager thought that I was stupid and tried to convince me that the room was cleaned before my visit.  I asked her repeatedly to come to my room to see for herself and she refused.  I tried to show her pics of the dead and/or alive roaches, the mold, the refrigerator gasket that was crammed with roaches, roach eggs and mold and she became flustered, defensive, and rolled out plenty of weak excuses.  Her response to all of my inquiries was that she was "going to discuss it with the housekeeping staff". The corporate office or the owner of this hotel needs to do a unannounced inspection of this hotel today.No Ma'am,  it starts with you, the manager.  Discuss with yourself the ways in which you can improve as a manager.  Start with improving your communication skills with customers.  (I tried to show the manager photos of the mold that I had taken, she insisted that none of it "was mold, it was all just rust".)Visually inspect the work of the housekeeping staff and check the condition of the room BEFORE customers check in.The room was outdated, unkept and smells of cigarettes, musk, and moth balls. The carpet was stained throughout and had a foul odor. The room a/c sounded like a freight train, the toilet did not work properly and the tv remote did not work.My room had cockroaches, rust and tons of mold and grime. I saw roaches and roach eggs on the nightstand, in the refrigerator, the oven, in the microwave and in the bathtub.  I was afraid that the roaches were going to infiltrate my luggage and other belongings and that I would transport them home. I was also terrified that roaches were going to crawl on me while I slept in the hotel's bed. This hotel is potential health hazard if you have any respiratory or allergy issues,I specifically chose this hotel because I’m on a special diet and I prefer to cook my own meals.  The hotel's website falsely advertises that the hotel has cookware for purchase on site.  Prior to inspecting the kitchen, I went to the hotel’s front desk to purchase the cookware, I was advised by management that they no longer sold, loaned, or even kept cookware on site.No food prepared in that filthy, infested, moldy, repulsive kitchen would be safe for consumption.  The microwave was rusted and had stuck on food and grease inside. The refrigerator gasket was crammed with mold, dead roaches, live baby roaches, grime and it wreaked of rotted food. The interior of the oven has tons of dead roaches and what appears to be burnt trash on the oven floor. Unbelievably, management told me that the room had been cleaned and inspected.At the time of my check in there were no room keys available and the phone system was down. The front desk is not staffed at night and is only staffed sporadically throughout the day.I requested a handicapped accessible room on the first floor. This hotel is not handicapped friendly!  There is a big step that you must maneuver to get onto the ramp leading to the front door of the hotel. The front doors to the hotel must be manually opened, there are no grab bars in the bathroom, and you can't access the tub/shower unless you are able to walk/stand independently.I shared my experience with the front desk morning manager.  I asked her repeatedly to come to my room and to look at the roaches, the mold, and the filth. She refused, stating that she couldn't leave the front desk for even 5 mins although my room was on the 1st floor,  just a few feet from your office. So then a “valued" customer tells you the unsafe and horrific conditions of their room and you refuse to see for yourself?I tried to show her all of the photos that I had taken of the room, she became defensive and began to make one foolish excuse after another. Every picture of mold, she said it was not mold but rather "rust". I am well over 60 years old, and I know the difference between mold and rust!The hotel did refund my money (as they should have) however the lack of respect, care/concern that they demonstrate by booking people in those horrific rooms is absolutely frightening.  Sadly at this location, you are not respected or treated like a "valued" customer!

name: Never Again
title: NEVER USE! They list a trashed hotel
text: If I could give no-starts I would. Had a family member pass away in an adjacent town and could not find a room in town. I booked the Econo Lodge Eagle Nest. I drove over an hour to get to the hotel - no one was at the hotel to check in and there was no key like the instructions gave! Called the hotel at different numbers and no answer - the cell phone on the front desk kept ringing. Keys were on the desk, private guest information was strewn about for all who came to see. Waited for hours, walked around the hotel and can only describe the condition as a drug den. There was trash everywhere, the "game room" was a disaster, and there were hypodermic needles in the walkway. I have proof! I don't know how this hotel stays in business - fake positive reviews anyone? I called hotel.com to see what was going on and try to get other accommodations to no avail. Ended up sleeping in my car. Hotel.com was completely no help. Never again. (And never received a refund.)

name: Cristiano Mariani

title: I have been using Hotels.com for years
text: I have been using Hotels.com for 10 years, booking approximately 100 travel days per year, and I’ve always been happy with their service—until now.This Christmas, while traveling to Chile with my wife and two children, I encountered two terrible experiences that made me question whether Hotels.com is still a reliable platform.First Incident:I received a message from a hotel saying they hadn’t received payment from Hotels.com and, as a result, canceled my booking. When I contacted Hotels.com, I was told they didn’t have a phone number for the hotel and could only send an email. I was instructed to wait 72 hours for a response. After 72 hours with no update, I called again, only to be told the same thing: they would email the hotel and I needed to wait another 72 hours.Frustrated, I insisted they book a new hotel for me, and I was transferred to their English rebooking department. This interaction was a disaster. I was repeatedly put on hold, only for the call to disconnect after 20–30 minutes. No one ever called me back, so I had to start the process over from scratch multiple times. In total, I spent 5 hours and 35 minutes of my vacation on the phone, incurring high roaming charges.Their customer service agents, based in India, seemed to have no authority to take action without placing me on hold endlessly. Eventually, when an agent tried to book a replacement hotel, a "technical error" occurred, and I had to book it myself. I am still waiting to be reimbursed for my expenses.Second Incident:After the first experience, I began verifying bookings directly with the hotels. One of the hotels told me they had never worked with Hotels.com or Expedia. Once again, I was back to square one: hours on hold, disconnected calls, no follow-ups, and, predictably, another "technical error" when attempting to book a new hotel.Hotels.com has been my go-to platform for years, but these experiences have severely shaken my trust. Spending hours on hold, dealing with unresponsive and unpolite agents, and having to pay for rebookings myself is unacceptable. I have the feeling that the long waitingtimes and the sudden "technical errors" are on purpose.BTW. The hotel that never worked with hotels.com can still be bookedI am deeply disappointed and hope they address these issues before losing more loyal customers.

text: My review Severely Disappointed with Our ExperienceI recently attended a very special family birthday celebration at Mount Wolseley, and I cannot express how disappointed I am with the entire experience. Unacceptable Cleanliness: The accommodations were filthy. Dirt was evident throughout the property, and cigarette butts were scattered in plant pots outside. Plastic in Dessert: The final straw was discovering pieces of plastic on the plate and in the dessert – an apple and berry pie. I was completely appalled and could not believe this could happen in any establishment, let alone one purporting to be of high standard. This was both dangerous and utterly unacceptable.6.	Management’s Indifference: When I attempted to raise these issues with a senior manager, I was met with complete indifference. There was no apology, no accountability, and no attempt to address the appalling experience.To sum up, this was one of the worst experiences I have ever had at a venue. The event was mishandled from start to finish, and the lack of professionalism, cleanliness, and care shown by Mount Wolseley was appalling. I would strongly advise others to avoid this venue for any event or occasion.

So not only did they charge my card when I didn’t even authorize that ticket, but even after I immediately told them to refund the money back, they still haven’t! So for 2 days already, they still have $7,500 of my money that I can’t access on my credit card. title: Arjun
text: Arjun - The Rajinikanth of Ticket Booking!If booking international tickets was an action movie, Arjun from Indian Eagle would be the hero, villain (to sky-high prices), and background score , all in one.I gave him a messy brief: “SFO to Bangalore. Cheap but not painful. No 24-hour layovers in Mars. Vegetarian meals. Prefer aisle, unless there’s legroom to stretch like a yoga instructor.” Most agents would’ve ghosted me. Arjun? He treated it like a KBC rapid fire round.Within minutes, he shot back with options, prices, pros and cons , even airline meal gossip (IYKYK). Dude knows flight routes like an astrologer knows birth charts. More impressively, he remembered my priorities better than I do.Throughout the process, he was patient, sharp, funny, and always one WhatsApp away. I’d throw curveballs like, “Can I upgrade if I sell a kidney?” and he’d reply with something both informative and reassuring. No upselling. No pressure. Just pure desi jugaad magic.In the end, I got a great deal, a convenient itinerary, and a story to tell. Thank you, Arjun , Travel’s very own one-man army. If you’re reading this and still searching for flights on 12 tabs , close them and just call Indian Eagle and ask them to transfer your call to Arjun. Seriously. I did the same!
