title: Urgent Complaint – Lack of Guest Contact Information and Inaccessible Support
text: Dear Expedia Partner Team,I am writing to express my deep frustration and disappointment regarding the complete lack of accessible support on your platform. The bookings that arrive through your platform lack essential guest contact details — no email address, no phone number, no way to reach our guest directly.Today, for example, we have a guest arriving, and we have no way of contacting them to send the access code for the apartment. The phone number provided for Expedia support only leads to an automated system, which is entirely unhelpful in such cases.So let me ask this clearly:As a property owner, if we cannot get in touch with a guest and they arrive at an unknown time, are they supposed to sleep on the street?We do not understand why it is so difficult for your company to acknowledge that not all of your partners are 24/7 reception hotels. Many of us operate apartment accommodations without physical front desks — which makes direct communication with guests essential.Please treat this matter seriously. Your current system is failing your accommodation partners, and it is creating unnecessary operational issues and guest dissatisfaction.We urgently request that guest contact details be made available, or that you provide a functioning and responsive support channel for partners.Sincerely,

text: My wife and I booked through Expedia,our itinerary number is (73073369257628) we booked from Houston to Cancun. When we arrived at the hotel, the amenities that were advertised online did not match the hotel room or the hotel, we reached out to the hotel staff and asked them where was the telephone,the robe s, the coffee maker, the bath towels and the staff honestly told us they do not have non of these amenities they advertised online to sell this room. The mattress was soiled with an unknown substance, the toilet kept getting stopped up and the maintenance man openly told us do not place toilet paper inside the comode after (certain) usage. We reached out to Expedia with these concerns and worries and explained to them we had pictures of the soiled mattress and the hotel room unacceptable condition. Expedia reassured us they will get to the bottom of this problem and refund us the amount for hotel which was $582.00. Expedia lied to my wife and I, they said they could not contact the hotel manager to corroborate this situation. Expedia needs to be shut down as a whole when you lie to your customers there is no future in your service or commitment i would not recommend Expedia.com to anyone on this planet stay away from this company.

name: Ken
title: Don't Book Through Expedia
text: Like others - would give a zero if I could.  I booked a flight from Chicago to New Zealand for my family.  We weren't able to get seats for the leg from LAX to New Zealand.  Contacted NZ Air, they said ticket information hadn't been transmitted.  Contacted United Air, they said the issue was not on their end but by the ticketing agent - Expedia.  Contacted Expedia customer service 8 times over 48 hours, endless hours on hold.  Was promised multiple times that the problem was resolved.  Contacted the number they gave me for NZ Air to select our seats, nope.  They did not have our ticketing information.  Finally gave up and booked directly through NZ Air.  Went to Expedia for a refund, they tell me the tickets are nonrefundable.   They accepted no responsibility for the ticketing fiasco.  How are tickets that were never issued nonrefundable?

name: Consumer

title: Horrible Service. Incorrect Booking
text: please save yourself the hassle and do not use Expedia to book your travels.My first time flying with young kids and decided to try Expedia. booked a vacation package and chose to fly with Air Transat. name: Shanya Dejczak
title: Expedia failed my autistic child
text: After our home was destroyed by a flood, I booked a property through Expedia/VRBO to urgently house my family. One of my children is autistic and depends on routine, predictability, and sensory stability to stay regulated. The property was misleadingly advertised and would not be an appropriate space for my son. I explained this to Expedia in detail, provided documentation, and asked for appropriate action.Their response? They called my child’s autism a “minor issue” and offered only a partial refund before closing the case.This wasn’t just poor customer service. This was a total disregard for the needs of a disabled child during a family emergency. Expedia’s process is not built to accommodate real-life accessibility concerns—or sensory-based needs—and they’ve made it clear they don't care to fix that.Families like mine deserve better. If you care about transparency, disability rights, or supporting people in crisis—do not trust Expedia or VRBO.

name: Lucky Lady
title: I had an extremely disturbing and…
text: I had an extremely disturbing and traumatic experience during my stay to Iberostar Selection Rose Hall Suites in Montego Bay, Jamaica. Unprompted, I was assaulted by another guest who appeared to be either under the influence of drugs or possessed or mentally unwell. The individual exhibited erratic and threatening behavior, and as I was walking up the stairs to leave fiction nightclub (inside the resort) the situation escalated quickly and violently when she crawled up the stairs and grabbed on to my legs not allowing me to take another step and started biting the back of my legs, puncturing my skin and causing me to bleed.What’s even more troubling is how the hotel staff responded—or rather, failed to respond appropriately. No doctor on site. Nurse is a separate entity so they don’t take your travel insurance. And I did not feel supported or safe, and it was clear that there were no adequate security measures in place to protect guests in wild emergencies like this. This should never happen in a place that promises safety and hospitality.Following the incident, I wanted to leave the resort immediately and return home. Unfortunately, I had booked through Expedia, and they were entirely unhelpful. Despite the severity of the situation, I was offered no real assistance or resolution from their customer service team. I felt stranded and vulnerable during a very distressing time.This experience was traumatizing, and I would strongly caution others to consider their safety before booking here or with Expedia. Both the hotel and Expedia failed to meet even the most basic expectations of guest care and responsibility.

name: Ramadhan Praditya Putra
title: Booked a hotel, received confirmation, paid full. Check-in refused because hotel under renovation. No prior warning. Refund request refused.
text: Be careful when booking hotels with Expedia.I booked a hotel via Expedia and received a confirmation email. I paid the full price for 1 night.I flew to Beijing, took a taxi, saw that the hotel was full of cement sacks, and the hotel receptionist told me that the hotel is under renovation and I cannot stay there. No prior communication whatsoever from the hotel nor Expedia was conveyed to me to cancel my booking. The receptionist said that "I can easily cancel the reservation later".Through Expedia, I asked for a refund and according to Expedia, the hotel management refused. The hotel cost was $91.85 per night but Expedia offered me an inconvenience voucher of $25.Where was I wrong? Is this fair for me?I will surely post bad reviews for both this hotel and Expedia but in order for this to not happen next time, could anyone point out what I did wrong?Here is the email from Expedia:Thank you for contacting Expedia. We apologize for the inconvenience that you have experienced.We wanted to follow up after our last conversation, where you asked us to reach out to your property to see if a refund was possible.We've contacted Hanting Hotel(south of Railway Station You'anmen B to see if they could make an exception and grant a refund.Unfortunately, after multiple tries, we weren't able to obtain an approval from the property manager to waive the cancellation fee. This means the current rules and restrictions for your booking apply and a refund can't be granted.We apologize for your disappointing experience, and we'd like to offer OneKeyCash to the value of USD 25.00 in recognition of your inconvenience.We're really sorry about this; we always try to contact suppliers and advocate for our travelers in these situations. Properties often have strict policies around refunds, and there's nothing more we can do in this case.Again, we're sorry that a refund wasn't possible. If you have any other questions, please feel free to reach out to us.Regards,UPDATE: After 2 weeks of back and forth emails with Expedia, they finally refunded all my money. So problem solved. However, please do not stay at Hanting Hotel You'anmen Beijing.

name: Rebecca Kooser
title: I booked a hotel through expedia
text: I booked a hotel through expedia. It was a discounted rate which is why I booked through them. I looked at my receipt and I was charged full price. I called them and they asked me if I have proof of the discounted rate, such as a screenshot. I said no. I did not think I had to screenshot the price they were advertising. They said unless I could show them proof they will not honor it. I asked them how they expected me to show proof of what they advertised 2 days earlier. Those dates are no longer available to book. Upon checkout I got the receipt from hotel. The hotel shows that I was booked at the discounted rate. I called expedia and said I now have proof because the hotel shows my rate as the discounted one. They tried to tell me that prices can change. I said no the price didn’t change. You are only paying the hotel the discounted rate but then charging me full price. So you are stealing from me and gaslighting me in the process. I asked to speak with a supervisor and after back and forth they did discount me. Without asking for proof of the receipt, which leads me to believe they knew they were overcharging me but were relying on the hope I couldn’t prove it. They also said the hotel should not have shown me the receipt.Once I received confirmation of the refund, I told them I was going to file a complaint with the BBB and they said had they known that, they would have never refunded me. The entire business is shady and a scam.

title: Profit above everything
text: I recently booked a 4 night stay in a privately owned apartment in Sitges through Expedia. We were due to arrive at the property on the 12th of April 2025. I had not received any check-in information by the day before we were due to arrive, so I followed the instructions on my booking confirmation which was to contact the host directly. I tried but there was no reply. There had still been no reply by the time we had arrived in Sitges. The additional information emails referred to in a confirmation email, including the ‘’link to a Vrbo account’ that I was supposed to receive, had not arrived.I then tried to get help using the Vrbo live chat function. I was given some phone numbers, all of which were numbers with a +33 code (France). None of the numbers picked up. I left a voicemail. After a number of exchanges and disingenuous promises of help, the second Vrbo agent I communicated with eventually just referred me back to Expedia and then terminated the chat. Meanwhile I was In Sitges, having nowhere to stay despite having paid up front for it.I did eventually manage to get through to a person at Vrbo on the telephone who I explained my situation to (again). They told me that as it was past check-in time (which was 16:00) and neither me or Vrbo could get hold of the host, I could get a full refund and go ahead and book somewhere else. Although I had already provided it, the agent told me to provide them with my Vrbo booking reference again in order to do this. I did not have access to the booking reference as it was on an email on my phone and the battery had drained. I was therefore using my partners’s phone by this time.Because I had been told we could have a refund, we went ahead and booked somewhere else for the rest of our stay.We found a cafe with wifi and I charged my phone. When I called back, I was told I absolutely could NOT have a refund, in complete contradiction to what I had been told before. We asked to speak to a supervisor who said that whilst they had the authority to issue a refund they would not unless the owner agreed to it. They did not...I believe this is misrepresentation: I booked with Expedia, and was told to expect communication from Vrbo and the host, neither of which happened.  All of these third parties provided opportunities for one party to blame another. Clearly the host did not receive my messages, either because (by their own admission) their ‘phone didn’t work’ or because they had tried to contact me on the app ‘Abritel’ which I had never heard of and had not at any point been invited to use.I booked with Expedia in good faith. It was reasonable for me to have expected to have been given the information I needed to enable me check in at the published time (16:00). When I reached out for help, this was not forthcoming, instead, the host decided they deserved to keep my money which was (for obvious reasons) a decision fully supported by Vrbo and Expedia.

name: George Muigai
title: $7,800 in Flights & Insurance—And I Was…
text: $7,800 in Flights & Insurance—And I Was Left Stranded by Expedia & EtihadOver the past 20+ years, I’ve used a personal travel agent with great success, albeit with high commissions. Last year, I tried Expedia for a trip to China and it went smoothly, so I decided to give it another go for a trip to India. That was a huge mistake.I booked 3 business class tickets on Etihad through Expedia, spending approximately $5,650. During checkout, I was offered “Protection Plus” insurance for $740 for all three passengers—promising coverage for missed flights, changes, delays, etc. I bought it, thinking we were covered and could travel stress-free.Wrong. First, the Etihad aircraft felt like something from WWII—tiny business class with just 8 cramped seats that didn’t lie flat. No grooming kits, no comfort. Total disappointment for the price.Then things got worse. Due to a change in my mother’s medical procedure, I needed to adjust our return flights. That’s when I learned the “Protection Plus” insurance is only valid for U.S. citizens—something that was never disclosed when I purchased it from Kenya. That $740 went up in smoke. No help. No coverage. Just sorry.To make matters worse, Etihad wouldn’t let me change my flight on their site because it was booked through Expedia. So I turned to Expedia support, which turned out to be laughably powerless. Initially, the change cost was $560, but as we explored alternative flights, the price increased to $1,445—apparently, because searching created “artificial demand.” This is manipulation, plain and simple.Worse still, Expedia’s chat platform is deeply broken. Agents ended chats while I was still typing. I’d barely get a response before being kicked off, forcing me to start the painful process over and over again.In total, I paid $1,445 for the change and got zero benefit from the insurance I was mis-sold.Expedia, this experience was a total betrayal. Your platform let me down, your support team was unhelpful, and your policies border on unethical. I’m going back to human agents—even with their high commissions—because at least I get honesty and accountability

title: Avoid Expedia at All Costs – They Left Us Stranded in Jamaica and Refused a Refund

text: I booked my flights to Morocco through Expedia months in advance to secure a good price and a smooth itinerary. But just two weeks before my trip, I noticed a key connecting flight was missing. He hung up on me.I’ve never felt so disrespected by a company I trusted with such an important trip. text: I have been a loyal Expedia customer for years, always trusting that they offer the best prices and fair treatment. My trust in Expedia is completely shattered. If you’re considering booking through Expedia, I strongly advise against it.I have reached out to Expedia for an explanation and a partial refund, but their lack of transparency and fairness is unacceptable. Loyal customers deserve better.

title: Expedia is Engaging in Fraud! “Free Parking” Promised, Now Charging $20 Per Night!
text: I booked a hotel through Expedia for April 1–8, 2025, in Miami. On the reservation page, it clearly states “Included amenities: Free Parking” on Expedia’s official platform. Expedia is failing to deliver the service that was promised at the time of booking, and this is completely unacceptable.To make matters worse, I booked this trip as a package (hotel + flight), so cancelling is not a simple option for me.Expedia must honor what they advertised or transfer me to an equal or better property with free parking at no additional cost. If this is not resolved immediately, I will take legal action and escalate this complaint to every possible consumer protection agency.This isn’t just about me — it’s about protecting other customers from being deceived the same way.

name: David Reardon
title: The consequences of booking early
text: I have only recently signed up to Expedia, and taking the advice these sites give on saving money by booking early, I did. Never again. I had to have some dental work done in Antalya Turkey, so after browsing hotels, decided on the crowne plaza hotel. I thought it was going to be a painful week at the clinic so I treated myself and booked a 1 room suite for £1, 050.00 for 7 nights. I had to have the booked dental work done so I didn’t bother paying the extortionate cancellation fees, I had to go, like it or not. A few days later, I noticed that the same 1 room suite, same dates was now only £800 for the week! The price was now £250 cheaper than what I paid. I do understand that as the season progresses, the prices are bound to rise, but we are talking a matter of days, not weeks or months. I am flabbergasted! I queried this with Expedia, who just sent me a stock reply ‘prices can vary, can we help you with anything else’ now the suspicious side of me starts thinking; I was a brand new customer, with money to spend, how hard would it be for them to ‘tinker’ with the prices, let’s whack on a few hundred quid and see if he swallows it, if not, well can reduce the prices, a bit like the proverbial second hand car salesman, start off high, then reduce as necessary.This may seem outlandish to anyone reading this, but think about it. They are out to make as much money from you as possible, that’s just business and understandable, but to manipulate the prices in order to maximise their profits in this way is tantamount to fraud. I genuinely believed that by booking a bit earlier would save me money, how wrong I was, and want to warn others from falling into the same trap.I am also going to start investigating this in much more detail, I will start by informing all my Facebook friends and ask if they have experienced something similar, then ‘request’ information from Expedia themselves, with special interest in the algorithms they use with their pricing policy. I will leave no stone unturned and will update this review as and when. In the meantime, be very conscious of this when you book via Expedia.

title: Redeeming flight credit - fail
text: Caution when redeeming credit.I bought a flight and then cancelled it shortly after. I was credited the flight cost to use on the same airline.When i went to redeem the credit 6 months later, the amount was penalized and reduced by more than half of the credit i had owing. title: Misleading Prices & No Customer Support – Avoid Expedia for Car Rentals

The rental company refused to honor the Expedia price, and when I contacted Expedia for support, they sided with the rental company instead of helping me, their customer.Expedia clearly partners with shady rental companies that engage in bait-and-switch pricing tactics. Instead of standing by their customers, they wash their hands of the issue and leave you stuck with unexpected costs.This experience was frustrating, costly, and unacceptable. I strongly recommend booking directly with reputable car rental companies instead of trusting Expedia, as they do not take responsibility for the misleading pricing on their platform.🚨 Lesson learned: Expedia may show a cheap price, but don’t count on it being honored at pickup. 🚨Would not recommend using them for car rentals!

title: Unethical - Expedia Sold Us a Nightmare and Abandoned Us - Shameful!
text: Expedia has completely betrayed my trust as a long-time customer. My children were bitten by bedbugs, the room was filthy, and the bathroom had leaks and mold that made my child seriously ill. She even claimed to be the "final decision-maker" and ended the chat abruptly when I asked to escalate the issue. They stranded my family in a dangerous and unsanitary environment, showing no regard for customer rights or well-being. I am now exploring all options to escalate this matter, including reporting Expedia to consumer protection agencies, filing a dispute with my credit card provider, and sharing this experience publicly to warn others. name: pdb
title: Don't book through Expedia!
text: Don't book through Expedia!I booked through them for an SUV from Routes Car Rental at Calgary airport.When I arrived, they gave me an SUV that was about 10" shorter than the one I had booked so it was a bit tricky to fit our skis, snowboard and two large suitcases in it.  However, since our flight had been delayed and the Routes staff were friendly and actually stayed past closing time to set me up, I just took the SUV they gave me.I had pre-paid Expedia $177.40.  Routes claimed the SUV they gave me was "similar" but the receipt they printed came to a total of $140.79.  I don't know if it was cheaper because it was smaller, or less fancy or their rates fluctuate but I figured I would get a credit on my VISA because according to their paperwork, the SUV I got would have been $140.79 if I had not pre-paid for it.I contacted Expedia and they got back to me, saying that they had contacted Routes who said no refund would be coming.  I contacted Expedia back and explained that they had an obligation to tell Routes to provide the refund or that they should provide it to me directly.  They told me to contact Routes directly.  So apparently I work in the rental car business now because I am doing their job and wondering why I bothered dealing with Expedia at all.  I contacted Routes who said I need to contact Expedia since they were my primary point of contact. So for the third time, I contact Expedia who replied back that there is nothing they can do.It seems obvious that a customer should not have to pay more than the going rate simply because Expedia got the money in advance.  It is pretty standard that when you buy something and the price drops before you pick it up, you get the lower price.This tells me that Expedia is a joke because they don't have the stones to tell their providers to send a refund and/or think it's okay when their providers switch a reservation and provide a lower priced vehicle but keep the extra money I pre-paid for the vehicle I didn't get.The only other thing I can come up with to explain this is that maybe Expedia routinely charges 26% commission to book a car rental.  Next time I will just go directly to a car rental site and save the $36.I have no idea whether Expedia or Routes pocketed the extra $36.61 but I will not be using either company again in the future if I can help it.  I'm astounded that Expedia would not just resolve the issue directly.  Then to have both companies tell me to talk to the other one?  I feel that at least one of them is lying to me and/or at least one of them is incompetent.Expedia's site says "...We’re here to build great products, and facilitate connections between travelers and our partners that truly bring good into the world."I would just say that they are extremely unprofessional and recommend you avoid using their services.

name: David Zhou
title: Beware of booking with Expedia—they’ll…
text: Beware of booking with Expedia—they’ll treat you like dirt and leave you stranded! I booked a round-trip flight from Seattle to Phoenix for March 7-10, 2025, back in October 2024 through Expedia. Everything seemed fine until one traveler couldn’t go, and I contacted their online customer service on March 6, 2025, to cancel just her portion and get a credit from the airline. I explicitly told the agent not to touch the other travelers’ bookings. What did Expedia do? Within an hour, they canceled my entire itinerary without my permission!Furious, I started another chat with a different agent, who had the nerve to ask for my credit card to “rebook” it—like I’d trust them again after their colossal screw-up! I refused, since this was 100% Expedia’s mistake, and called their customer service instead. The phone agent promised he could restore my booking without needing my card. Sounded good, right? Wrong. Without my knowledge or consent, he charged $926 to the card Expedia had on file! I got a “card not present” alert from my bank and couldn’t believe Expedia had the audacity to do this behind my back.The nightmare didn’t end there. They managed to restore my Seattle-to-Phoenix flight on March 7, but I lost my carefully chosen seats and got stuck in the last row. Even worse? They didn’t bother rebooking my return flight from Phoenix to Seattle! I was left high and dry. I spent hours on the phone with multiple Expedia supervisors, who fed me a ridiculous story about needing to pay an extra $600 to rebook my return flight. They claimed they paid it, only for the airline to cancel it again, and then had the gall to say, “Well, we both lost $600, so we’re even.” Are you kidding me? I called the airline myself—they confirmed Expedia never even tried to rebook anything after their initial cancellation on March 6. Expedia flat-out lied to me.After wasting over 10 hours on the phone with their incompetent, untrustworthy customer service, I’m still fighting to get my money back. Expedia doesn’t care about its customers—they’ll butcher your plans, charge you without consent, and leave you to clean up their mess. Save yourself the headache and stay far away from Expedia. Book directly with airlines or use a company that actually values you!

name: Linda Ward
title: Expedia Incompetence
text: On January 28th, 2025, I made a hotel reservation through Expedia. This was for a three-night stay in Nashville, Tennessee.On March 5th I decided to reconfirm, although their confirmation says do not bother to reconfirm.Their virtual agent offered nothing and at one point had disabled my typing ability; it was a dead end.I finally found a number and got a human voice - Hank. After almost 45 minutes he found my reservation and said that it had been canceled by Marriott, because I did not let them know I was coming. What? Isn't that why we book with Expedia? I had no email from Marriott other than their confirmation for an October stay last year! Aren't they, Expedia, as a third site, responsible for relaying the reservation to the hotel? Otherwise, why would we use Expedia?After the 45 minutes on the phone, I then asked Hank if we would be through by 11:00, as I had an important phone call that had been set up for 2 months. He told me it would take longer than that, so I asked him if I needed to be on the phone with him when he was going to – according to him - reinstate my stay with the same itinerary number, but only after he said he had to cancel and rebook my original. Cancel and rebook? He had already told me that Marriott had canceled because they sent me an email that I did not answer! At this point I became very suspicious of what was going on.Hank then told me that I did not have to be on the phone for him to cancel and rebook. I questioned him as to the fact that he was absolutely sure it would be the same itinerary number - yes! I did not need to be on the phone with him while he did this - no, I did not. He would send me the rebooking within an hour- yes!lNeedless to say, we are now 21 hours from my finishing my conversation with Hank. When I go to Expedia to put in my 14 or 15 number itinerary, it says nothing is found. Nothing has changed since the first time of looking.When I first went to Expedia, it showed that no trips were booked - shall we start?I shall never use Expedia again and I hope you won't either.I went to their website and deleted any information that they had that included birthdays and telephone numbers.Had I not reconfirmed,  as previously mentioned, at the very top it says no reconfirming needed, three of us, from California, Georgia and Florida would most likely have been stuck in Nashville with no accommodations! These are spring break dates for many!

text: Best price on the market, at the time, but the booking process was made difficult due to website issues. name: Ale Rubanu
title: What is Expedia playing at? A vicious, cruel "price game" with their Customers!
text: Last week, I booked a Hotel via Expedia for 3 nights and a final price of £337. I did not think I was asking much, and yet these clowns keep replying to my with an automated reply, without any real explaining. Cowards normally hide behind an email or a machine, so I sent their machine and hope this miserable Company to do one! text: I have used Expedia for decades. I booked a trip to Europe and New York for my 70th birthday next month. I booked this last summer. name: Kenneth Pedersen
title: Terrible Customer Service – No Action Taken
text: I had a deeply frustrating experience with Expedia that has completely damaged my trust in their services.I booked a hotel through Expedia and fully paid for my stay in advance. However, the hotel accidentally charged me again for the stay, despite the booking already being paid through Expedia. I contacted Expedia support, and they assured me that they would contact the hotel on my behalf to resolve the issue and secure a refund.What followed was an extremely disappointing and drawn-out process:After waiting two weeks with no communication from Expedia, I contacted the hotel directly, and to my surprise, they were more than happy to help and processed my refund immediately—no questions asked.Meanwhile, it took Expedia four months to even get back to me. I only found out that they never contacted the hotel at all when I reached out to the hotel myself.This experience was not only time-consuming but also completely frustrating. I was misled and given false assurances, and ultimately, I had to resolve the issue myself. It’s shocking that a company like Expedia, which promises customer support, failed to provide any real assistance.Given this failure, I am now actively sharing my story across platforms to warn others.Avoid Expedia if you expect reliable customer support.

name: Adam
title: As bad as you think
text: Booked the hotel for a necessary work trip, it was Worldmark Anaheim.Got a notice a month later from Worldmark "confirming" the reservation was canceled.  They made it sound like we had canceled.Called the Worldmark.  They said it wasn't them.  I had to call Vacationshare.   I stayed on hold literally two hours before I gave up.First of all, what Expedia sold me wasn't a hotel.  It was a sublet of a time share.  Expedia did not made that clear at all.Meanwhile, I got Expedia chat.  The helpful (?) agent confirmed that we did in fact have a reservation, nothing was canceled.  The cancellation was a typo.I kept a transcript of the chat confirming we definitely had a reservation, no matter what anyone else said.3 days before the trip, we got a text saying our reservation was canceled.I called Expedia, went through a telephone tree, until someone finally told me I needed to call Expedia.  I said "I did call Expedia."  They said "no, this is Vrbo, hang up and call Expedia."  I did, and got Vrbo again.Vrbo could not help me, so had me hang up and dial another number at Expedia, which connected me to Vrbo.  Vrbo could not help me, so connected me to Expedia could not help me, so connected me to Vrbo.  Vrbo could not help me, so connected me to Expedia.  I am not exaggerating.  Every single time I had to give my information again.I finally got mad.  I was like "I booked this through Expedia, Expedia too my money, confirmed I had a reservation, double-confirmed I had a reservation, I don't have a relationship with Worldmark or Vacationshare -- why can Expedia not help me?"  They connected me to Vrbo, who can "definitely help you."90 minutes later, they told me there was a "book with security guarantee" or something like that.  They still can't tell me if I'll have a room when I show up or not (in 72 hours!), but they can at least give me a refund, and let me book again for myself at 5X the price I locked down two months in advance.

name: ReadOn
title: Expedia is a Scam – Avoid at All Costs!
text: Expedia is not a travel agency. It's a scam operation masquerading as one. If you book with them, you’re on your own the moment something goes wrong. They will ignore you, lie to you, and do everything possible to avoid helping you.My return flight was canceled last-minute, and Expedia/Ebookers refused to rebook me despite airline confirmation that they were responsible.Their customer service is useless. Chat agents ignore messages, provide false information, and refuse to take action. The nonsensical sentences they spit out are almost comical, if my situation would not be that dire.Their only “solution” was a flight 4 DAYS LATER, forcing me to cover all additional costs myself.When I demanded a real alternative, they stonewalled and blamed the airline, even though the airline confirmed it was Expedia’s responsibility.They only offered a partial refund – conveniently ignoring the fact that a round-trip ticket is a contract.Why You Should NEVER Book with Expedia:- No support when things go wrong – you’ll get ghosted or sent in endless circles.- They refuse to rebook flights they are responsible for.- They lie about their responsibilities and blame the airline.- You will lose money on hotels, transfers, and extra costs – and they won’t care.- Even if they cancel your flight, they won’t refund you fully.Expedia is not a travel company – it’s a scam machine designed to take your money and leave you stranded. Do yourself a favor: Book directly with airlines. If you book with Expedia, pray that nothing goes wrong – because if it does, you’re screwed.

title: DO NOT TRUST WHAT YOU THINK YOU BOOK ON…
text: DO NOT TRUST WHAT YOU THINK YOU BOOK ON EXPEDIA - THEY WILL COVER UP THEIR ERRORS AND NOT INFORM YOU OF THE CHANGESI booked the Novotel Hyderabad on line - Bing > Expedia - as it was a very good price. Immediately after entering my credit card details a screenshot appeared saying 'Your Booking Has Been Confirmed' - it contained details of the Booking - the Novotel, the Date and Price - I copied the screenshot.I waited for email confirmation and when it did not arrive I contacted Expedia - ensuring it was the correct number in case of Fraud. The gentleman I spoke to at first failed to grasp my issue - all I wanted to do was confirm my Booking for the Novotel in February. He mentioned the Fortune Hotel, which I clearly had not booked. I then slowly explained to him once again that I had screenshot confirmation of the Novotel. At this point he assured me that the hotel that I had booked, the Novotel, had been confirmed. I asked him to email me confirmation of the booking, which he agreed to do.When the email arrived it simply confirmed a Hotel booking and the date and price - it did not confirm the actual Name of the Hotel.I decided to log on to Expedia and open an account in order to check my booking. When I did this I discovered that they had booked me into the Fortune Hotel not The Novotel as stated when I initially booked..I then phoned Expedia and explained again. The girl said that she would cancel the Fortune - free of charge...very kind - and that I would have to rebook the Novotel myself. After being on hold for a long time she once again tried to persuade me to rebook myself - to which I replied I would have the same issues - which she said she would sort? I stood my ground and after another long hold she informed me that the price advertised when I booked - I told her who I had booked though - was a Members Only Price which had increased from £18 to £201.I explained to her that I had confirmation from Expedia of my booking for the Novotel for £18 - which she now wanted to charge me £201 for. I stated that they had advertised it at that price and I had booked it however they had decided to change the booking without my permission - as such they should honour the original booking.Another long wait and she then asked that I send her copies of the Screenshot Booking Confirmation  - which I did  - and that they would get back to me.That was yesterday at lunchtime and I have not even had an acknowledgement of the email. All that I have received is a Customer Service Survey -WHAT A JOKE OF A COMPANY THEY ARE.If I had simply accepted their Screenshot Booking Confirmation and incomplete email - and not logged into Expedia - I would have arrived in Hyderabad at 03:00 and went to the Novotel, where I assumed my booking to be - only to be informed there was no booking.WHAT A JOKE OF A COMPANY THEY AREI can only assume that the Novotel rate they advertised and sold to me was an error rate - an error that they decided to change without informing me.An error on their behalf that they have decided NOT TO HONOUR - I DOUBT THAT I WILL EVER GET A RESPONSE FROM THEIR CUSTOMER CARE - FAST ENOUGH AT SENDING SURVEYS BUT TOTALLY USELESS AT RESOLVING ISSUES OR HELPING CUSTOMERS - EVEN WHEN ITS THEIR FAULTNEVER AGAIN - FROM A FREQUENT TRAVELLER

name: Susan Williams
title: Misrepresentation at its best
text: After reading all the other bad reviews, I am even more compelled to write mines. This company should be ashamed of how disgusting their customer service reps are and how they misrepresent what they are offering. My flight was cancelled due to weather conditions yesterday. I missed the connecting flight which was an international flight that didn’t have another flight to get me to my destination for another 2 days. Spoke to a condescending character and asked to cancel the flight after several minutes says I’ll have to go thru the airline. Ok, what about my insurance, I’ll have to cancel that thru the third party. Ok, what’s that info? Hold on for another few minutes for him to tell me I sent it to your email would you like me to go ahead and cancel that for you? So I’m confused cause at this point I’ve been on the phone 45min between waiting for someone to answer and your several holds. So I asked what are you offering to cancel after you said you couldn’t? name: Nelly Defo
title: SHADDY BUSINESS PRACTICES
text: Made a booking on this site in USD and conversion in another currency was automatically done - without prior disclosure or my express consent, charging me in a different currency  than the actual receipt issued by the site! That is technically FRAUD!I concur with most of the reviews, do NOT use this site for any of your travel plans no matter how appealing the deals....Booking.com definitely more honest/transparent in their practices!

name: Alen
title: NEVER booking through expedia agian
text: NEVER booking through expedia agian. Booked a package deal with flights and stay through expedia to get 1 night free off of a hotel. We were told the hotel is fully refundable and the flights could be moved at no extra charge. What they don't tell you is that once you book, your package deal gets broken up into segments so if you ever need to make a change to your dates, you lose your package deal and free night. You also cannot cancel your flights and rebook. Customer service had me on the phone for an hour and fifteen minutes before being transferred to a supervisor that ended up disconnecting the line and not calling back. We are never using expedia again and we will make sure to let everyone we know to book elsewhere. I am not one to leave reviews but i am disgusted by this service.

name: Farhad Behzadi
title: Expedia is now just another scam third party site
text: Expedia used to be a legit travel site. Unfortunate;y, it has now turned into another third party scam bait and switch travel site. Do not try to book any multi city or complicated trip through them. They lure you in with a fake low fare on one leg of the trip and after you have booked the whole trip , they cancel the leg with the low fare saying that the airline didn't issue the ticket. You then end up spending hours with so called customer service agents in India that flatly lie to you to get you off the phone. The whole purpose is to drag you beyond the 24 hour no fee cancellation period on the rest of your trip. Buyer beware. Many of the airline rates that they quote are not real. They even confirm the trips and send confirmation codes but those codes never show up on the airlines' website and then they blame the airline. The worst part of it is that anytime you call to see what is going on, the agent comes up with a new excuse.

name: Helena B.
title: Expedia posted a 100% false review on my behalf
text: I booked a hotel reservation through Expedia. I received an email notification at 7:45 AM saying thank you for review. Expedia posted a review of the hotel on my behalf! It was a green smiley face with the word "Pleasing." The email from them yesterday requesting that I leave a review hasn't even been opened in my inbox yet btw. I immediately logged in to Expedia and tried to delete - I could not. I contacted customer support. They sent me a directworld form to complete. In summary: They posted a false review on my behalf, I wasn't allowed to remove it on my own, I had to contact support, fill out a form, and now I have to wait 3 business days for them to remove it, with the hope that I'll be able to leave a real review of the hotel later. I don't think I'll be using Expedia again. Ridiculous.

name: Erin McLaughlin

text: NEVER book a flight through Expedia. “Fully refundable” scam!I have a sensitive situation with my relative’s health.
